Scalability demands reducing time-to-converged observables by curbing repeated high-level electronic-structure calls. Surrogate excited-state models (including machine-learning potentials) can replace much of the on-the-fly electronic structure, while active learning, multi-fidelity strategies, and uncertainty quantification guide where new reference data and additional sampling are actually needed. Flexibility of representation is essential in dense excited-state manifolds, where the decoherence-selected pointer basis may differ from the adiabatic energy basis; localized representations and open-quantum-systems tools (Lindblad dynamics, stochastic unravelling) provide practical routes to encode that choice. Together, these directions define an agenda for MQCD that targets larger, longer, and more environmentally complex excited-state dynamics while retaining a trajectory-based workflow.

papers.title: Asymmetrical Two-Headed Linear Cationic Surfactants with Halogenoferrate Magnetic and Bromide Counter-Ions: Synthesis, Thermal Behavior, Magnetic Performance, and Surface Properties
papers.abstract: A series of multicharged surfactants with magnetic counterions (Mag-D-Surfs) containing one hydrophobic tail and two hydrophilic groupings, and comprising exclusively carbon atoms in the hydrophobic part, i.e., 2-alkyl- N,N,N,N’,N’,N’ -hexamethylpropan-1,3-ammonium salts (ferrates; alkyl: decyl, dodecyl, tetradecyl, abbreviated, respectively, as C 10 -D C Me 3 Mag, C 12 -D C NMe 3 Mag, and C 14 -D C NMe 3 Mag), were first synthesized and characterized by FT-IR, Raman, X-ray fluorescence (XRF) and FIR spectra as well as elemental analyses. Thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) and differential scanning calorimetry (DSC), supported by optical polarization microscopy, showed that the coexistence of isotropic and anisotropic subphases depended on cooling rates. Surface activity of C n -D C NMe 3 Mag at the air/water interface was evaluated by measuring the surface tension of their solutions by the pendant drop technique and compared with surfactants without magnetic function. Moreover, surface tensiometry in a magnetic field demonstrated that the studied Mag-D-Surfs exhibited magnetically induced changes in the drop shape. Their magnetic behavior in the solid state was determined by superconducting quantum interference device magnetometry (SQUID). All findings related to the aforementioned double-headed Mag-D-Surfs were compared to linear magnetic ionic liquids surfactants (MILSs), i.e., alkyltrimethylammonium halogenoferrates (alkyl: dodecyl [DTA][FeCl x Br 4-x - ], tetradecyl [TTA][FeCl x Br 4-x - ], and cetyl [CTA][FeCl x Br 4-x - ]). Magnetic tests confirm the paramagnetic nature of the studied compounds and the 1:1 molar ratio (surface active cation:Fe 3+ ) for all the studied surfactants. Their unique physicochemical properties demonstrate exceptional performance, particularly in the development of new stimuli-responsive materials.

papers.title: Beyond Canonical CO Oxidation: First Characterisation of a Clade B CODH using a New Anaerobic Cryo-EM Workflow
papers.abstract: Carbon monoxide dehydrogenases (CODHs) catalyse the reversible oxidation of CO to CO₂ and play central roles in microbial carbon metabolism. While well-characterised CODHs from different phylogenetic backgrounds exhibit high bidirectional activity, the enigmatic clade B remains functionally uncharacterised. Here we present the first structural and functional characterisation of a clade B CODH from Ruminococcus flavefaciens ( Rf CODH). It reveals striking divergence from canonical enzymes. A new anaerobic cryo-EM workflow was developed, carried out entirely under anoxic conditions by manual blotting and plunge freezing. It resulted in a 2.53 Å Rf CODH structure. The structure adopts the typical CODH fold, but exhibits blocked gas channels, a compromised proton transfer pathway and disrupted cofactor coordination. This provides a structural rationale for Rf CODH’s severely attenuated CO oxidation activity (13 mU/mg vs. 900 U/mg for the well-studied Ch CODH-II). EPR spectroscopy reveals unique oxidised C-cluster states not previously characterised in CODHs. Mirror tree analysis hints to co-evolution between clade B CODHs and associated ABC transporter substrate-binding proteins, suggesting these enzymes function in metabolism of substrates imported via the ABC transporter module. All findings indicate evolutionary repurposing of the CODH scaffold for alternative physiological functions.

papers.title: A Molecular view on Protein - Ion Interactions during the Fibrinogen Aggregate Formation†
papers.abstract: Understanding how ions regulate fibrinogen self-assembly into fibers is essential for advancing enzymefree strategies to fabricate fibrillar biomaterials. Here, we combine evaporation-driven self-assembly experiments with atomistic molecular dynamics simulations to elucidate how chloride-and phosphatebased salt environments modulate the nanoscale organization and electrostatic landscape of fibrinogen. Mass-loss and turbidity data identified a critical salt threshold above which rapid fiber growth occured. SEM-EDS analysis further showed selective retention of sodium, particularly associated with phosphate, while chloride was largely removed, indicating different and non-equivalent roles of the mixed-salts in the assembly of fibrinogen nanofibers during the drying process. Simulations of the fibrinogen D domain (Fg-D) show that Na + ions form a tightly bound Stern layer at acidic residues, whereas Cloccupies the diffuse layer and exhibits only transient interactions. In contrast, monohydrogen and dihydrogen phosphate anions display strong and persistent binding to positively charged patches. The ability to be chelated by more than one positive amino acid side chain and fixation/clustering of immobilized Na + ions at Ca 2+-binding sites lead to reduced ion mobility, extended hydration structuring, and pronounced modulation-or even inversion-of the local electrostatic potential. These ion-specific effects collectively lower the electrostatic barrier for protein-protein approach and explain the strong aggregation propensity observed experimentally in phosphate-rich environments. By revealing how distinct ions tune the electrical double layer and solvent structure around Fg-D, this work establishes a physicochemical basis for designing enzyme-free fibrinogen materials with controllable fibrillar architecture and offers new opportunities for biomaterial development using tailored ionic environments. † Electronic supplementary information (ESI) available.

papers.title: Combining Water and Biorenewable Solvents for Sustainable Anodic Reactions
papers.abstract: Enabling technologies are perceived as inherently sustainable, due to the replacement of stoichiometric oxidants and reductants with traceless redox mediators such as photons or electrons. However, the solvent of the reaction plays a crucial role in the environmental impact of the process. To aspire towards ideal sustainable electrochemical transformations, the use of water as solvent would be the most preferred choice, but the poor solubility of organic compounds in aqueous phase hinders its employment. Another option could be the use of biorenewable solvents, which require the use of wasteful organic supporting electrolytes. In this work, the application of a solvent mixture of water and propylene carbonate is presented. This media combines the best features of the two chemicals, enabling sustainable electrochemical synthesis without solubility issues of organic material or inorganic salts. The adoption of a high-mass transfer electrochemical reactor overcomes the limitations caused by heterogeneous mixtures, allowing the implementation of high concentrations and current densities. The generality of this concept was validated across four different anodic reactions, comprising a cross-coupling, a rearrangement, a direct and a mediated oxidation. In all the studies, the scalability of these processes could be demonstrated, reaching excellent productivities with exquisite green metrics. Finally, a guideline for general application of this approach was outlined .

papers.title: Anti-Kasha electroluminescence in carbene-gold-arylacetylide complexes
papers.abstract: Kasha's rule states that luminescence occurs from the lowest excited state; violating this rule could enable radiative release of excess electronic energy, otherwise lost as heat in electroluminescent devices. Here we demonstrate anti-Kasha narrowband electroluminescence from carbene-gold(I)-arylacetylide complexes. A rigid acetylide bridge links a (carbene)gold(I) moiety to a multiple-resonance chromophore, thereby spatially separating frontier orbitals to produce a dark long-range charge-transfer S1 and bright short-range charge-transfer S2 states. Optical spectroscopy and theory show that S2 is populated by reverse intersystem crossing from T1 and T2 triplets, enabled by gold-mediated spin-orbit coupling. Proof-of-concept solutionprocessed OLEDs exhibit narrowband (26 nm) anti-Kasha electroluminescence with 20.4% maximum external quantum efficiency (EQE), and 13% EQE at 10,000 cd m-2 .

papers.title: Unveiling the Anomalous Expansion of Silicon-Carbon Composites Obtained by Chemical Vapor Infiltration Through Operando Charge Photometry and Dilatometry
papers.abstract: Modern lithium-ion batteries increasingly incorporate pure silicon into the anode to boost energy density. However, practical deployment remains limited by silicon’s large cycling-induced volume changes, typically assessed by pouch cell dilatometry. While informative at the electrode-stack level, this method provides no direct insight into underlying particle-level behaviour. Here, we combine operando dilatometry with high-resolution charge photometry to correlate electrode-level expansion with single-particle swelling in state-of-the-art silicon anodes. We examined anode materials: (i) silicon-carbon (Si-C) composites prepared by silicon vapor deposition into porous carbon, and (ii) dense micron-sized silicon prepared by jet milling. Dilatometry revealed pronounced non-linear thickness evolution for Si–C composites, with reduced expansion at low state-of-charge, whereas micron-sized silicon exhibited linear expansion. Charge photometry reproduced these trends at the particle-level, showing that the nonlinear swelling of Si–C composites arise from internal porosity that delays external volume change during early lithiation. Dilatometry also captured significant first-cycle expansion irreversibility for both materials, while charge photometry showed largely reversible particle swelling, indicating that irreversibility originates from cell-level processes rather than intrinsic active material behaviour. Overall, these results establish charge photometry as a practical lab-based tool for resolving operando particle-scale chemo-mechanics and highlights the benefits of nano-engineered composite architectures for mitigating silicon expansion.

papers.title: Nanodiamond Spin Probes for Sensing Reactive Intermediates in Heterogeneous Photocatalysis
papers.abstract: Heterogeneous photocatalysts are promising materials for turning solar energy into chemical fuels, but their widespread application is hampered by low efficiency and selectivity. To facilitate future catalyst design, the evaluation of reactive intermediates, such as reactive oxygen species (ROS), formed in photocatalysis is vital. Challenges arise in ROS detection due to their high reactivity and interactions with the catalyst surface. Techniques such as electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) often rely on bulk-sensing apparatus that are highly sensitive but have poor spatial resolution. Here, a fast in-situ method for evaluating the performance of photocatalysts in ROS formation is developed, utilising nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centres in fluorescent nanodiamond (FND) particles as sensors. This work demonstrates the ability to detect ROS (e.g., · OH, O 2 ·– ) in both the absence and presence of spin-trap adducts (e.g., 5,5-Dimethyl-1-pyrroline N-oxide, DMPO), the latter allowing for further ROS identification by EPR. An exploration of various photocatalysts demonstrates the technique's ability to probe ROS generation during photocatalysis. Correlation with bulk photocatalytic activity highlights the method's suitability for rapidly evaluating photocatalyst efficiency. This methodology shows promise for sensing local, nanoscale photocatalytic activity on catalyst surfaces and can act to expedite the discovery of next-generation catalysts.

papers.title: Vibronic Reorganization Suppresses Salinixanthin-to-Retinal Energy Transfer in the freshwater Kin4B8 Xanthorhodopsin
papers.abstract: Salinixanthin, a 4-keto xanthophyll, acts as an efficient light-harvesting antenna by transferring excitation energy to retinal in the terrestrial Xanthorhodopsin from Salinibacter ruber ( Sr XR). Although it also binds to the freshwater xanthorhodopsin Kin4B8, it does not transfer energy to retinal, whereas hydroxylated xanthophylls show high excitation energy transfer (EET) efficiency in this protein. Here, we combine molecular dynamics simulations with polarizable QM/MM calculations to construct and characterize the Kin4B8–salinixanthin complex. We obtain a spectroscopically consistent binding model that reproduces the Kin4B8-salinixanthin experimental absorption and circular dichroism spectra and reveals strong electronic coupling between salinixanthin and retinal, comparable to the other xanthophylls. However, energy transfer is strongly suppressed by the red-shift of salinixanthin S 2 state and its large reorganization energy, which drastically reduce donor–acceptor spectral overlap. These results demonstrate that, in this system, donor vibronic relaxation, rather than geometry or electronic coupling, is the decisive factor suppressing EET.

papers.title: Optimization of the limits of detection & quantitation on pulsed compact neutron systemsthe cases of chlorine & sulfur in cementitious media
papers.abstract: The use of pulsed compact neutron systems to implement energy-resolved prompt-gamma activation analysis is herein assessed in detail for the quantitative and non-intrusive detection of chlorine and sulfur in cementitious media, two exogenous contaminants commonly found in buildings, civil infrastructures, or archeological artefacts. To this end, we have examined the current capabilities of the RIKEN RANS-I pulsed source across its neutron-energy spectrum using its room-temperature moderator. We achieve up to a threefold improvement relative to previously reported limits of detection via the selective use of the γ-ray yield in the wavelength interval 2-4 Å. Under these conditions, measurement times 1 of a few minutes are sufficient to attain sensitivities in the sub-millimol%, and this figure can be improved further via the optimization of the existing detection system. Monte Carlo simulations of a validated model of RIKEN RANS-I show that order-of-magnitude gains in sensitivity are also within reach via the use of cold moderators, such as those based on solid methane or mesitylene. Altogether, these developments would enable limits of detection in the µmol% range.

papers.title: Hybrid Adsorption-Liquefaction Process for Post-combustion CO 2 Capture
papers.abstract: The potential of a hybrid process combining two separation processes: pressurevacuum swing adsorption (PVSA) and cryogenic CO 2 purification/liquefaction is explored using a system-level integrated techno-economic optimization framework. Detailed process models of the PVSA and the liquefaction units developed in gProms were used to train Artificial Neural Network (ANN) based surrogates. These surrogates were integrated with a detailed costing framework to perform techno-economic optimization of both standalone PVSA and hybrid processes. A wide range of flue gas CO 2 compositions ranging from 3.5-30 mol % are studied. Unconstrained cost optimizations of a standalone PVSA process for feed CO 2 compositions ≤13 mol% showed that at low-purity levels (≤60 mol%) and high recovery levels (≥90%), the cost of CO 2 avoided reduced by more than half compared to when the standalone-PVSA process produces both high purity (≥95 mol%) and high recovery (≥90%). Parametric analysis of a cryogenic CO 2 purification process showed that a high level of purification (purity ≥ 98 mol%) is achievable with only two flash stages, with reasonable recoveries. The hybrid process was found to be cost-competitive with a conventional monoethanolamine (MEA) absorption process for flue gas CO 2 compositions ≥7.5 mol% under the constraints of ≥95 mol% purity and ≥90% overall recovery. The key advantages of the hybrid are the avoidance of deep vacuums, the reduction in plant footprint, and the ability to meet product oxygen specifications.

papers.title: Photocatalytic Activation of Fluoroform for Radical Trifluoromethylation
papers.abstract: Fluoroform is an ideal trifluoromethyl source in synthetic chemistry due to its low cost, low toxicity, and high potential for greenhouse-gas valorization. However, the use of fluoroform has been largely limited to the generation of trifluoromethyl anions or metal-bound species; direct access to the trifluoromethyl radical remains elusive, despite its broad applicability for preparing medicinally important trifluoromethylated compounds. Here, we report a method to generate the trifluoromethyl radical in situ from fluoroform via photochemical activation. Leveraging the reactivity of ketones in combination with a Brønsted base under photoirradiation enables the direct use of fluoroform for the radical trifluoromethylation of alkenes and arenes. This approach is amenable to a photocatalytic protocol and enables the conversion of bulk chemicals into a high-value trifluoromethylated compound.

papers.title: Quantifying the Failure Modes of Current One-step Retrosynthesis Models
papers.abstract: Computer-aided synthesis planning (CASP) automates retrosynthetic analysis, generally by recursively applying one-step retrosynthesis models within multistep search algorithms to simplify a target molecule into commercially available starting materials. Despite their utility, these tools often fail to recover literature-reported pathways. Such failures arise from two causes: either (i) the literature-reported precursor is not proposed at all or (ii) it is proposed but ranked too low to be discovered during multistep search. In this work, we quantify the challenges that data-driven one-step retrosynthesis models face in reproducing the reported precursors. We first evaluate model performance using standard top- k exact-match accuracy and stratify this accuracy by product and reaction complexity, demonstrating a decrease in performance with increasing complexity. This decline is accompanied by a systematic underprediction of the number of reacting atoms and changing rings, indicating a bias toward simpler transformations, even when complex examples are included in the training data. To gain deeper insights into failure modes, we evaluate models with complementary metrics that account for incorrect stereochemistry, leaving groups, and multi-stage reactions. Overall, our work provides a quantitative analysis of how one-step retrosynthesis models fail to capture literature-reported reactions and highlights opportunities for improving future models.

papers.title: Do We Really Need All That Data: From Data to Agency in Automated Microscopy
Generalized Turnstile Rotation: Formulation, Visualization, Workflow Implementation, and Application for Modeling Polytopal Rearrangements
papers.abstract: Turnstile rotation is a well-known polytopal rearrangement mechanism in coordination compounds, yet its computational description is often hindered by the inability of conventional internal coordinates to represent such collective, large-amplitude motions. In this work, we present a rigorous mathematical formulation for generalized N-arm turnstile rotation and introduce a dedicated PyMOL plugin (gTA) for intuitive structure visualization and manipulation. On this basis, we develop a practical computational workflow that combines turnstile rotation-driven relaxed scans with constrained geometry optimizations to systematically locate approximate transition states (aTS), which serve as reliable initial guesses for subsequent transition state refinement. The generality of the approach is demonstrated through four chemically diverse case studies, ranging from classical rearrangements in [Co(en)3] 3+ and SF4 to previously unexplored fluxional processes in bismuth and nickel complexes. In all cases, the method enables the identification of transition states associated with pronounced polytopal rearrangements that are difficult to access using standard coordinate schemes. These results establish generalized turnstile rotation as a fundamental molecular motion and highlight its potential as a broadly applicable strategy for studying fluxionality and dynamic stereochemistry in coordination and chemistry.

papers.title: Automating Chemical Reasoning in High-Throughput Phase Identification with a Probabilistic, LLM-Guided Framework
papers.abstract: Autonomous laboratories increasingly enable materials synthesis at scale, but traditional high-throughput characterization workflows remain limited by the need for expert chemical intuition to distinguish plausible interpretations from formally good but chemically incorrect fits. We present an automated interpretation framework that combines probabilistic inference with automated chemical reasoning for phase identification from powder X-ray diffraction (XRD). The framework evaluates multiple candidate interpretations using diffraction pattern-based metrics. It then refines these likelihoods using chemically-informed priors derived from composition balance and a large language model (LLM)-based plausibility estimate with human-readable justification and also produces a trustworthiness score. In a blinded multi-project benchmark, the framework's top-ranked interpretation was selected over the lowest-R wp baseline 93% of the time in cases where one prediction was preferred. Trust decisions made by the framework aligned with expert judgment in approximately 75-80% of cases. In a second evaluation, the framework systematically identified cases where lowest-R wp interpretations were chemically implausible and surfaced credible alternatives to historically ambiguous samples. By reframing phase identification as a problem of probabilistic reasoning and trust-aware decision making, this work demonstrates how chemical intuition can be automated and scaled.

papers.title: Computational Prediction and Experimental Validation Framework for Nitrogen-Enriched Metal-Decorated Porous Framework Composites: Enhanced Reversible Hydrogen Physisorption at Ambient Temperature
papers.abstract: We present a comprehensive computational framework for predicting synergistic hydrogen storage performance in nitrogen-enriched porous framework composites through hierarchical integration of three distinct architectural components. The material design combines: (1) crystalline nitrogen-rich covalent organic frameworks (COFs) synthesized via imine or triazine condensation reactions (nitrogen content 15-35 atomic %, BET surface area 1500-4000 m 2 /g, optimal pore diameter 6-15 Å matching H 2 kinetic diameter 2.89 Å), (2) controlled metal decoration (lithium, sodium, potassium, magnesium, or calcium) coordinated to framework nitrogen Lewis base sites at 4-18 wt% loading creating enhanced hydrogen binding sites (15-25 kJ/mol) through induced dipole polarization mechanisms, and (3) conductive carbon scaffold (graphene aerogel, carbon nanotubes, or activated carbon fibers) at 15-40 wt% providing mechanical support, preventing framework aggregation, and enabling thermal management (>500 W/m•K conductivity). Employing density functional theory calculations (DFT-D3 dispersion corrections) for binding energy prediction and grand canonical Monte Carlo simulations for capacity prediction, we establish predicted hydrogen storage capacity of 3.5-4.5 wt% at 298 K and 50 bar pressure-representing 25-60% improvement over best experimental literature (Li-activated carbon: 2.8 wt% at 298 K/100 bar). The synergistic enhancement factor of 2.0-2.8× (measured versus interference-corrected additive prediction) demonstrates non-additive performance characteristic of multi-component hierarchical architectures. Computational predictions are rigorously validated against 18 peer-reviewed experimental studies establishing binding energies (pristine COF: 5-10 kJ/mol, Li-decorated MOF: 17-24 kJ/mol), surface areas (COF: 1500-4200 m 2 /g), and capacity benchmarks (Li-carbon systems: 2.1-2.8 wt% at 298 K). Complete experimental validation methodology is disclosed including synthesis protocols (solvothermal COF synthesis 120-180°C, organometallic Li decoration under inert atmosphere, scaffold integration), structural characterization (XRD, BET, XPS for Li-N coordination), and performance testing (Sieverts apparatus isotherms 273-323 K, Clausius-Clapeyron binding energy determination, 500-cycle durability). This work establishes a validated computational-to-experimental framework for rational design of ambient-temperature hydrogen storage materials addressing the global energy transition challenge requiring economical, safe, and reversible storage systems for fuel cell vehicles and renewable energy infrastructure.

papers.title: Catalyst-Free, Autoinductive Photochemical Upcycling of Aromatic Polymers and Mixed Plastics via Autosensitization
papers.abstract: Photochemical upcycling of polymers is a promising strategy for mitigating the plastic-waste crisis; however, many recent advances have centered on developing new and often costly photocatalysts. In contrast, the auto-sensitized photoreactivity of aromatic polymers such as polystyrene (PS)-albeit documented for decades-has remained essentially unexploited for practical upcycling. Here we leverage this overlooked reactivity to develop a catalyst-free, autoinductive platform that converts PS into benzoic acid under visible light irradiation in air. The approach extends to other aromatic polymers including polyethylene terephthalate (PET), polycarbonate, polyether sulfone (PES), and epoxy resins, as well as biomass feedstocks such as lignin. Importantly, convergent mechanistic experiments and DFT calculations support a solventenabled pathway in which autosensitization-derived superoxide reacts with chloroalkanes (via S N 2) to form peroxy intermediates, generating alkoxy and, via β-scission, chlorine radicals that abstract C-H bonds along polymer backbones, propagating oxidative chain cleavage. In turn, oxidized PS oligomers and in situ produced HCl drive autoinductive rate acceleration. This intrinsic PS photoreactivity further enables co-upcycling with non-aromatic polymers in mixed feeds and remains effective in a model halogenated solvent waste mixture, pointing to potential synergy between mixed plastics/biomass valorization and solvent waste management.

papers.title: Ultrafast computation of exact symmetry-corrected RMSD of conformers
Browsing FAIR Transformation Product Information with FAIR-TPs
papers.abstract: Considering transformation products (TPs) in environmental studies remains a huge challenge for scientists, from identification in samples via mass spectrometry through to inclusion in chemical regulation. This article introduces FAIR-TPs, a website to browse openly-available TP data collated from literature sources. The data is sourced from several community-contributed environmental datasets on the NORMAN Suspect List Exchange (NORMAN-SLE), plus a dataset from ChEMBL available through PubChem, with links to templates and contact details to encourage further community contributions. The data is compiled regularly using an open source workflow, archived and versioned on Zenodo under a CC-BY license, then processed and displayed on FAIR-TPs. FAIR-TPs currently contains 11,190 reactions involving 9,435 compounds from 11 sources, covering human and environmental transformations through to high energy water treatment reactions. A graph-based representation of the transformations (compounds as nodes, reactions as edges) is stored in a Neo4j database as a Directed Graph and made publicly accessible online through a Django Web Application. Users can retrieve the shortest directed pathways between predecessors (parents) and successors (transformation products/metabolites), search by SMARTS substructures, or explore local reaction neighbourhood data on individual compounds. Interactive network visualizations provide ways for users to view multi-step transformations in a smooth, user-friendly interface, while exploring transformation pathways. The compound/reaction metadata provides links to further information about the chemicals and data sources. Key statistics, including number of reactions/compounds, top compounds, reaction types, mass differences are summarised from the current dataset. FAIR-TPs is designed to be a public resource to support suspect and non-target screening workflows, helping scientists identify data gaps and interpret complex transformation reactions. The FAIR-TPs website is openly available at https://fairtps.lcsb.uni.lu.

papers.title: Stepwise Metalation Triggers Long-Range Structural Communication in a Chiral Organic Cage
papers.abstract: Biological allosteric systems achieve functional control through long-range communication between distant binding sites. Here we report that a symmetric chiral cage bearing two equivalent tris(2-pyridylmethyl)amine ( TPMA ) binding sites exhibits allosteric-like structural communication during stepwise Zn(II) coordination. NMR titrations reveal sequential metalation kinetics in which the second coordination step becomes comparatively slower in mixed solvents, consistent with electrostatic effects and structural pre-organization. Circular dichroism (CD) spectroscopy tracks the progressive structural evolution of the cage, with five isodichroic points confirming clean interconversion between discrete species. TD-DFT calculations reproduce the experimental chiroptical evolution, and correlate the observed spectral changes with systematic geometric reorganization of the framework over distances exceeding 10 Å. This work illustrates the potential of CD spectroscopy as a diagnostic tool for probing allosteric-like mechanisms in synthetic supramolecular systems, with implications for responsive materials, heterometallic catalysis, and adaptive architectures.

papers.title: Outer-Sphere Tuning of Synthetic Iron-Sulfur Clusters within Nanoscale Cage Frameworks
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT. Iron–sulfur clusters are atomic-scale archetypes for multielectron-mediated catalysis, yet translating their enzymatic proficiency into robust synthetic platforms remains a central challenge in the realization of functional materials. A key bottleneck lies in replicating the highly organized outer-sphere environment, which provides a multifunctional framework to modulate the cofactor’s electronic landscape, ensure nanoscale site-isolation against deleterious decomposition, and facilitate catalytic pathways via programmable noncovalent interactions. Herein, we demonstrate a molecular host-guest strategy for the precise and systematic tuning of iron-sulfur cofactor models within the defined cavities of tetrahedral [M 4 L 6 ] 8+ cages (M = Ni, Fe, Zn). By utilizing naphthalenediimide (NDI)-based panels as rigid, redox-active boundaries, we successfully encapsulated [Fe 4 S 4 (SR) 4 ] 2– (R = Ph, -CH 2 CH 2 OH) guests, as confirmed by high-field NMR spectroscopy and ESI mass spectrometry. Nanoscale confinement within the cage enables direct manipulation of the cluster’s electronic character, as probed by 57 Fe Mössbauer, X-ray photoelectron, IR, and UV-vis spectroscopy data, which reveals significant shifts in Fe–S covalency and electron density upon encapsulation. Notably, this modulation occurs in the absence of traditional hydrogen-bond donors, underscoring the power of the nanoscale host environment for electronic tuning. This work establishes a design paradigm for cage-stabilized cofactors in the assembly of sophisticated, energy-efficient catalytic systems.

papers.title: Size-Independent Quantum Entanglement Signatures in Cs3Al− n Superatom Clusters: An Fbond Analysis
Review of a Withdrawn Drug Candidate: Indiplon
papers.abstract: Indiplon was re-evaluated as a ligand of the GABA A receptor benzodiazepine (BZ) binding site using integrated in silico approaches, including chemical-space mapping by UMAP, molecular docking, and contact-residue analysis. Chemical-space projection based on molecular fingerprints placed indiplon near clinically used GABA A hypnotics while remaining partially separated from the dense classical benzodiazepine scaffold cluster, indicating scaffold divergence within the same functional ligand class. Docking analysis at the BZ site showed energetically favorable poses for both indiplon and the reference ligand diazepam. Comparative pose inspection and residue-contact profiling revealed strong binding-mode convergence, including overlapping aromatic shelf interactions and polar anchor contacts within the pocket. Quantitative overlap of contact residues further supported spatial similarity of interaction patterns despite differences in core chemotype. These findings suggest that three-dimensional interaction geometry and pharmacophore-level alignment, rather than global scaffold identity alone, play a dominant role in BZ-site ligand recognition. Retrospective computational analysis of discontinued compounds such as indiplon may therefore provide useful structural insights and scaffold-diverse design hints for next-generation GABA A modulators.

papers.title: NovoExpert-1: State-of-the-Art CYP2D6 Prediction via Message-Passing Neural Networks on the TDC ADMET Benchmark
papers.abstract: We present NovoExpert-1, a suite of Chemprop-based message-passing neural networks for ADMET property prediction. Evaluated on the Therapeutics Data Commons (TDC) standardized benchmark, NovoExpert-1 achieves state-of-the-art performance on CYP2D6 metabolism prediction with an AUROC of 0.864 ± 0.015, exceeding the prior best result of 0.750 by 11.4 percentage points. We also achieve near state-of-the-art results on CYP3A4 (0.890 ± 0.012 vs. 0.900) and CYP2C9 (0.878 ± 0.014 vs. 0.900). Our models use the directed messagepassing neural network (D-MPNN) architecture with standardized hyperparameters across all endpoints, demonstrating that careful application of established graph neural network methods can yield significant improvements on clinically relevant ADMET endpoints. We provide a detailed analysis of per-endpoint performance, discuss the clinical relevance of CYP2D6 prediction, and characterize failure modes on hERG and P-glycoprotein endpoints where 2D graph representations may be insufficient. Code and trained models are publicly available at https://github.com/quantnexusai/novoexpert1-tdc-benchmark .

papers.title: Precision Profiling of α-1,4-vs α-1,6-glycosidase activity using synthetic linear and branched glycogen tetramers using HPLC-MS
papers.abstract: Accurately defining glycosidase specificity is often limited by access to well-defined oligosaccharide probes and analytical tools capable of resolving regioisomers at low concentrations. We synthesized two linear and one branched glycogen-mimetic tetrasaccharides, bearing exclusively 1,2-cis, namely α-1,4 or α-1,6 linkages using a reagent-controlled stereoselective glycosylation strategy. Their enzymatic degradation by Homo sapiens glycogen debranching enzyme (HsGDE) and two commercial α-1,4-glucosidases was assessed by HILIC-MS and high-resolution cyclic ion mobility mass spectrometry (cIMS-MS), enabling separation and quantification of substrates and products in the micromolar range. HsGDE selectively cleaved the α-1,6-branch while showing low activity on terminal α-1,6 linkages. The Saccharomyces cerevisiae α-1,4-glucosidase showed high α-1,4 selectivity, whereas the rice enzyme displayed broad promiscuity toward all regioisomers. The cIMS-MS provided rapid baseline separation of the synthetic tetrasaccharides and confirmed the absence of inhibition by non-substrate isomers. This integrated synthetic-analytical workflow offers an efficient platform for rapid annotation of glycosidase specificity and mechanistic studies in glycogen metabolism.

papers.title: Towards Activity Prediction: Unveiling the Role of Intra/Intermolecular Balance in Fe-N-C Catalysts for Hydrogen Evolution
papers.abstract: Metal-nitrogen-carbon (M-N-C) molecular catalysts attract attention for the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) owing to their well-defined active sites and structural tunability. However, previous studies prioritize intramolecular regulation, leaving the cooperative role of intermolecular interactions insufficiently understood. Herein, we design and synthesize three Fe-N-C molecules, including iron phthalocyanine (FePc) and two pyridinic-N-incorporated FePc derivatives (FeTAP and FeOM), and elucidate their structure-activity relationships via integrated structural and electronic analyses to enable performance prediction. We demonstrate that pyridinic-N incorporation drives Fe centers from Fe 2+ to a more positively charged Fe 2+δ state, creating an "oxidation-state reservoir" that promotes rapid electron transfer and proton adsorption for HER. Moreover, overall activity is governed by the balance between intramolecular electronic regulation and intermolecular π-π interactions: FePc is limited by weak intramolecular regulation; FeOM exhibits strong intramolecular effects but weakened intermolecular coupling; and FeTAP optimizes this balance, delivering the highest HER activity. Electrochemical measurements corroborate the predictions and further reveal that an optimal level of pyridinic-N achieves the intra-/intermolecular balance, thereby accelerating HER kinetics on these Fe-N-C catalysts. These findings provide a predictive basis and a clear design guideline centered on intra-/intermolecular balance for molecular electrocatalysts.

papers.title: Evaluating 2D and 3D Graph Encoders for Infrared-Based Organic Structure Verification
papers.abstract: Infrared (IR) spectrum prediction is typically judged by global spectral error, but the practical task in analytical chemistry is structure verification: given a spectrum, can a model rank the correct structure highly among many candidates? We recast IR modelling around the structure verification problem, and extend the Phase-Aware Spectrum Generative Network (PASGeN) to test how 2D and 3D graph encoders perform when retrieval accuracy, instead of spectral similarity, is the metric of interest. Using 13568 experimental IR spectra in various phases, we train models with a 2D message-passing neural network (MPNN) and a 3D directional encoder (DimeNet), and fine-tune the 3D model on inexpensive force-field geometries to reduce inference cost. Across large-scale retrieval tests, the 3D encoder significantly outperforms the 2D baseline (74.4% vs 63.9% Top-1 accuracy). Both learned models exceed the verification performance of quantum chemical DFT and GFN2-xTB baselines by a wide margin. Descriptor analysis suggests that ring-rich, geometrically complex molecules benefit most from the inclusion of 3D information. By reframing IR prediction around the structure verification task and demonstrating that lightweight 3D geometries provide a measurable advantage, this work establishes a practical and scalable route to IR-based structure confirmation that surpasses physics-based baselines at a fraction of the computational cost.

papers.title: Density Functional Theory with Complex Absorbing Potentials: A Fast and Accurate Way of Modeling Metastable Anions
papers.abstract: The use of a complex absorbing potential (CAP) for the description of temporary anions is well established. However, its combination with Kohn-Sham density functional theory (DFT) has so far been limited to the local density approximation. We report an implementation of CAP-DFT and complex-variable density functional approximations up to the generalized gradient approximation and derived hybrid functionals, which enables fast and accurate evaluation of the energies and lifetimes of metastable molecular anions. This new method is applied to various molecular systems, including the metastable anions of molecular nitrogen, formaldehyde, formic acid, ethene, and pyrene. Our results indicate that pure density functional approximations place temporary anions too low in energy and overestimate their decay width, while Hartree-Fock theory shows the opposite trends. Hybrid functionals balance these trends and deliver results that are competitive with equation-of-motion coupled-cluster theory.

papers.title: New MnO2 electrode doped with Co2+ ions for a microfluidic biosensor for the detection of H2O2: formation, characterization, catalytic tests
papers.abstract: H 2 O 2 serves as a vital signalling molecule within biological systems and presents potential as a disease biomarker. Consequently, the development of sensitive and accurate sensors for its measurement within microfluidic systems is of significant importance. This article focuses on the development of a working electrode for an electrochemical microfluidic system designed for the quantitative determination of hydrogen peroxide. Here, we show that a MnO 2 -based catalytic material can be improved by adding Co 2+ ions. By changing the Co 2+ concentration, an electrode material with improved catalytic performance was formed. Amperometric measurements of catalytic activity show a substantial increase in sensitivity and an expanded range of H 2 O 2 concentrations that can be quantified using the new electrode. The characteristics of the MnO 2 -modified Co 2+ electrode were thoroughly examined by SEM, XPS. The combination of previously accumulated material and new data offers insights into the underlying reasons for the high catalytic activity of MnO 2 , supported by quantum-chemical calculations. This research lays the groundwork for a method utilising MnO 2 as a working electrode for detecting the concentration of H 2 O 2 within a microfluidic cell. During experiments, a stopflow protocol is employed, enabling data collection from coulometric measurements of the electrochemical processes occurring on the electrode within a limited measurement timeframe.

papers.title: Catalytic Selective C-N Bond Metathesis of Tertiary Alkyl Amines
papers.abstract: Given the abundance of tertiary amines across the molecular sciences, a carbon-nitrogen (C-N) single bond metathesis reaction could have a transformative impact on their synthesis and derivatization, yet this class of reactions has been vastly underexplored. Besides the challenge of developing a catalytic manifold enabling the reversible cleavage of inert C-N bonds, the trivalent nature of nitrogen results in a combinatorial explosion of possible products that has so far prevented any meaningful synthetic applications. Here, we introduce an iridiumbased catalytic system that enables the C-N bond metathesis between tertiary alkyl amines. Importantly, we harness empirically derived rules that govern the reaction's selectivity in cross-metathesis events and demonstrate the potential for the tailorable synthesis of bioactive molecules. Finally, we also showcase interdisciplinary applications in the synthesis of oligomeric polyamines, as well as an encoding scheme where combinations of statistical mixtures are utilized for molecular data storage.

papers.title: Introducing Diradicaloid Thiele's Hydrocarbon Derivatives as Ligand in Transition Metal Chemistry
papers.abstract: Thiele's hydrocarbon (TH) derivatives, or p-quinodimethanes, are prototypical members of the organic diradicaloid family, predominantly explored in organic and main-group organometallic chemistry. Herein, we introduce them to transition-metal coordination by employing N-doped TH derivatives as ligands. Pyridine-and pyrazine-substituted p-quinodimethane ligands were synthesized, enabling the formation of mono-and dinuclear rhodium and cyclometallated iridium complexes (Py•Rh, Pz•Rh, Py•Ir and Pz•Ir). We show the strong effects that simple metalation, and more importantly, orthometallation can have on the photophysical and electrochemical properties, as well as on singlet-triplet gaps of these biradicaloids. Additionally, the metalated mixed-valent forms are strongly electrochromic NIR absorbing dyes. Spectroelectrochemical studies reveal distinct electronic interactions between the diradicaloid backbone and the metal centers, highlighting the potential of N-doped TH derivatives as versatile redox-active ligands in transition-metal chemistry.

papers.title: Self-Assembly of Binary Peptide System in the Solid State Induced by the Presence of Environmental Water - An Unusual Case of Ex-Vivo Peptides Cooperation
Redox chemistry and photophysics of the [V(dgpy)2] 3+/2+ redox pair
papers.abstract: Transition metal complexes with Earth-abundant metal centers hold significant potential for light-induced processes. Pseudo-octahedral vanadium(III) and vanadium(II) complexes with d 2 and d 3 electron configuration are promising candidates, yet their redox and excited state properties are only insufficiently understood. Here, we combine quantum chemistry and experimental data (structure, cyclic voltammetry, spectroelectrochemistry, electron transfer dissociation, collision-induced dissociation and ultraviolet photodissociation mass spectrometry, ultrafast transient absorption spectroscopy) to elucidate redox and photostability as well as excited state lifetime of the vanadium(III/II) redox couple cisfac-[V(dgpy)2] 3+/2+ (dgpy = 2,6diguanidylpyridine). Ground state splitting, mixing of spin-flip excited states with metal-to-ligand charge transfer states and multiphonon relaxation are identified as the key challenges for excited state lifetimes in these d 2 /d 3 systems.

papers.title: Realization of Self-Terminating Underpotential Electropolymerization by Strong Monomer-Electrode Interaction
papers.abstract: In this report, we show that electropolymerization of 3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene (EDOT) can take place at 0.4 V, a voltage far lower than the conventionally employed voltage of 1.0 V, in a self-terminating manner, when gold is employed as a working electrode. DFT calculations revealed that the highest occupied molecular orbital (HOMO) of EDOT is elevated by approximately 1 eV when it directly interacts with the gold surface compared to that without such direct interaction. In other words, monomers become highly reactive for oxidative polymerization when they are directly adsorbed onto gold. Once the polymer forms and covers the electrode surface, the monomer can no longer interact with the electrode surface, thus the polymerization is terminated. Such selfterminating polymerization behavior was supported by in situ electrochemical surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (EC-SERS) and the current profile during the voltage scan. This is in sharp contrast to electropolymerization under ordinary high-voltage conditions, where the polymer film continuously grows. This study may provide solutions to control the polymerization on the solid surface, which is considered to be very important for adhesive, coatings, and solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) formation. It is also expected to lead to new synthetic methods via electropolymerization for monolayer polymers, which have recently attracted attention for their potential to exhibit various functions.

papers.title: Benchmarking Local Geometry Optimization Algorithms for Computational Materials Discovery
papers.abstract: Most current computational materials discovery workflows are dependent on efficient and reliable structure relaxations in order to predict a hypothetical material's equilibrium structure. Besides an accurate description of the potential energy surface, this requires efficient and reliable optimization algorithms. In this study, we investigate how different optimization algorithms affect the relaxation of inorganic crystal structures using general-purpose machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs). Our findings emphasize the critical role of optimizer selection in large-scale computational materials science workflows, particularly in the context of element-substitution based materials discovery. This can guide the community towards choosing appropriate algorithms for the efficient and reliable prediction of new crystalline materials.

papers.title: Review of a Withdrawn Drug Candidate: Adipiplon
papers.abstract: Adipiplon is a benzodiazepine-site ligand developed for insomnia that was discontinued after phase II trials due to safety concerns. To extract structural insights relevant to drug design, we performed an in silico docking comparison of adipiplon and representative dual orexin receptor antagonists (DORAs) at two sleep-related targets: the GABA_A receptor benzodiazepine binding site and the orexin type 2 receptor (OX2R). Docking calculations using AutoDock Vina showed that adipiplon can form binding poses at both receptors, with intermediate predicted binding scores relative to reference ligands. At the GABA_A benzodiazepine site, adipiplon frequently formed polar anchor-like interactions, whereas at OX2R its anchoring patterns were less consistent. In contrast, DORAs showed more reproducible anchor interactions and more favorable score distributions at OX2R. These results suggest that adipiplon has structural flexibility across multiple receptor pockets but may lack a dominant anchoring mode associated with target selectivity. This docking-based analysis provides a structural hypothesis and illustrates the value of reassessing withdrawn drug candidates for structure-based drug design.

papers.title: DISSOLVR: An Interpretable and Fast Framework for Aqueous and Organic Solubility Prediction
papers.abstract: High-fidelity solubility prediction is fundamental to pharmaceutical development and environmental partitioning, where accurate modeling must couple molecular structure with thermodynamic behavior across diverse chemical environments. However, recent advancements have been dominated by deep learning architectures that often sacrifice physical interpretability for predictive power. We challenge this trend by showing that state-of-the-art performance does not require such non-transparent architectures. To address this, we introduce DISSOLVR, a transparent framework for molecular solubility prediction. In addition, we perform a comprehensive literature review and a benchmarking study against various methods. We show that DISSOLVR approaches the aleatoric limit of experimental uncertainty and achieves OOD generalization through structural invariance derived by mapping molecules to physically-grounded descriptors. Then, we present an LLM-assisted post-hoc explanation pipeline that bridges the gap between symbolic model artifacts and chemically grounded narratives. Finally, a comparative benchmark of a survey involving 22 expert chemists reveals that expert evaluators provide deep insights.

papers.title: Ultrafast computation of exact symmetry-corrected RMSD of conformers
papers.abstract: Accurate quantification of molecular structural similarity through root mean square deviation (RMSD) is essential for protein-ligand docking validation, conformational analysis, and molecular dynamics simulations, yet current methods face a critical trade-off: polynomial-time algorithms sacrifice chemical correctness by ignoring molecular connectivity, while graph isomorphism approaches exhibit prohibitive computational costs for symmetric molecules. This limitation prevents routine exact symmetry correction in applications where distinguishing genuine conformational differences from atom labeling artifacts is essential, such as evaluating docking poses and pruning conformational ensembles. This work introduces the Hierarchical Neighborhood of Atoms (HNA) partitioning, a recursive classification of chemically equivalent atoms that enables fast computation of exact symmetry-corrected RMSD. Hierarchical decomposition reduces search complexity from the product of branch combinations to their sum, achieving computation time reductions of several orders of magnitude compared to existing topology-preserving methods. Comprehensive benchmarks on large molecular databases demonstrate mean execution times in the millisecond range across molecules ranging from small compounds to proteins, with complete success on all calculations without failures or timeouts. In contrast to linear assignment approaches that produce high rates of topologically invalid mappings, this algorithm ensures chemically correct atom correspondences, enabling practical exact symmetry correction across the full spectrum of molecular complexity relevant to drug discovery and biomolecular structure prediction.

papers.title: Improving Robustness of Fifth-Rung Functionals with Linearized Ladder Correlation
Quaternary ammonium–modified cellulose fibers can enhance wastewater treatment performance under challenging conditions
papers.abstract: Wastewater treatment is challenged by refractory contaminants and rising water demand, while conventional coagulation-flocculation suffers from low throughput and is sensitive to the influent water conditions. Cellulose fibers can act as super-bridging agents offering enhanced turbidity removal when used in conjunction with traditional coagulants and flocculants. However, the chemical modification of cellulose fibers and their performance under challenging influent conditions remain largely unexplored. In this study, recycled cellulose fibers are modified with cationic quaternary ammonium groups, imparting a positive charge that can improve treatment performance for a wider range of water matrices including varying influent pH, ionic strength, and turbidity. Modified fibers achieve turbidity below 5 NTU across all influent pHs (7.0–8.9) and turbidities (62–285 NTU) tested, while pristine fibers show that the target turbidity of 25 NTU is not reached when the influent pH or turbidity exceed 8.2 or 130 NTU, respectively. Additionally, modified fibers achieve the target turbidity of 25 NTU even in the presence of an additional 20 mM NaCl, while pristine fibers cannot reach this target at an additional 10 mM NaCl. Furthermore, the modified fibers enhance the removal of metals such as Zn, Cr, Fe, and Pb through the incorporation of metal hydroxide precipitates within fiber-based flocs. Overall, pristine and modified fiber-enhanced treatments remove 52 % and 65 % of metals, respectively, compared to 39 % with the conventional method. Therefore, modified cellulose fibers represent a promising strategy for enhancing coagulation-flocculation treatment performance.

papers.title: Space-Charge Effects in Lithium Garnet Solid Electrolytes: A Continuum Modeling Study Using the Poisson–Nernst–Planck Framework
papers.abstract: For next-generation solid-state micro-batteries, lithium garnet solid electrolytes like Li 7 La 3 Zr 2 O 12 (LLZO) are considered a promising material because of their high ionic conductivity, electrochemical stability, and mechanical robustness. Experimental data indicates that interfacial resistance, thickness-dependent conductivity, and currentinduced polarization can considerably restrict their performance, even though they are frequently regarded as Ohmic ionic conductors. Based on the coupled Poisson-Nernst-Planck (PNP) equations, we create a continuum-scale model in this work to study the transport of lithium ions in LLZO under applied potential difference. Physically motivated scales are used to nondimensionalize the governing equations, demonstrating that the problem is governed by a single dimensionless parameter: the squared ratio of the electrolyte thickness to the Debye length. Space-charge layers and nonlinear transport regimes can be resolved steadily by the use of an implicit Newton-Raphson approach to get numerical solutions. The findings underscore the significance of spacecharge effects in solid-state electrolytes by showing departures from electroneutral Ohmic behavior in thin electrolytes and under reduced electrolyte thickness. The framework offers a quantitative foundation for comprehending phenomena and for creating composite or interfacially designed electrolytes that perform better.

papers.title: Splitting-Domain Reformulation of Symmetric Strongly Coupled Four-Spin NMR Systems
papers.abstract: The analysis of strongly coupled ¹H NMR spin systems of the AA′BB′ and AA′XX′ type has remained one of the most challenging problems in spectral interpretation for over six decades. The classical Pople framework provides a complete closed-form solution, but requires the prior assignment of observed peaks to specific quantum-mechanical transitions, a combinatorial problem that has rendered the method impractical for routine use. Alternative approaches based on iterative quantum-mechanical fitting exist but remain computationally demanding and sensitive to initial parameter estimates, limiting their adoption for routine analysis. Here we demonstrate that both limitations can be bypassed by reformulating the analysis in the domain of pairwise frequency differences. We show that the coupling interaction between nuclei guarantees the existence of characteristic shared splittings within this set, reducing the problem from combinatorial assignment to pattern recognition. A Set Transformer extracts the relevant splittings from the unordered difference set, and a differentiable Pople inversion layer converts them into coupling constants through exact analytical equations, enabling end-to-end training with physics-informed loss functions. The approach is validated on two distinct four-spin topologies (ortho-and para-disubstituted benzenes), achieving sub-0.05 Hz mean absolute errors on synthetic data and sub-0.08 Hz on experimental spectra from six compounds spanning the full range from the AA′XX′ limit to the genuinely second-order AA′BB′ regime. The two models share an identical neural architecture differing only in the deterministic Pople layer, demonstrating the generality of the splitting-domain representation across coupling topologies.

papers.title: p-H 2 versus o-D 2 Clusters: from liquid-like to glass-like behavior
papers.abstract: Motivated by fascinating structural properties, as well as emerging numerical challenges, para-Hydrogen clusters have been explored in numerous publications in the past. Despite the enormous computational resources used by a number of groups, involving various methods, no consensus on the clusters' energetic and structural properties has been established. Most studies reported strong size dependencies, e.g., "magic number" clusters, while strongly disagreeing with each other quantitatively. Only a few studies claimed the lack of size sensitivity. That is, hardly more than a couple of reports could be considered numerically converged and/or physically meaningful. Unlike most of the previous studies, we focus on small size range of Lennard-Jones LJ34−39 clusters, for which using Diffusion Monte Carlo (DMC) we attempt to capture the true behavior of the systems accurately. Not only do we demonstrate that the (p-H2)N clusters for the chosen sizes have the ground state wavefunctions strongly delocalized over thousands of structurally identical isomers, but we also vary the quantum delocalization parameter Λ in the effective range between the hydrogen (ΛH 2 ∼ 0.28) and deuterium (ΛD 2 ∼ 0.20) regimes. We show that for the o-D2 clusters the ground state wavefunctions are strongly localized, yet they are still disordered. In this regime, the system dynamics associated with the DMC method becomes non-ergodic, e.g., the random walkers get trapped in the potential energy minima, where they have been initialized. (It is ergodic for hydrogen clusters.) Consequently we suggest that the structural change induced by decreasing the quantum parameter Λ from p-H2 to o-D2 has the character of a "liquid-glass" transition.

papers.title: A preassembled backbone-anchored solubilizing tag to simplify native chemical ligation-based protein synthesis
papers.abstract: Chemical protein synthesis (CPS) has become an essential tool in chemical biology, offering access to homogeneous proteins bearing modifications beyond the reach of biological expression systems. At the heart of CPS lies native chemical ligation (NCL), which enables the chemoselective coupling of unprotected peptide segments under mild aqueous conditions. However, the scope and efficiency of NCL are often severely constrained by the poor solubility or aggregation propensity of certain peptide segments leading to inneficient ligations and challenging purifications. To address these limitations, a wide range of temporary hydrophilizing tags has been developed, yet existing systems frequently require trade-offs between ease of installation, stability, and cleavage efficiency. Backbone substitution strategies such as Liu's removable backbone modification (RBM) platforms, based on N-2-hydroxy-4-methoxybenzyl (Hmb) derivatives, offer additional advantages of disrupting secondary structures thus preventing aggreagtion. We report here a new class of backbone-anchored solubilizing tags, termed Hmb<K3>, designed for automated introduction by straightforward on-resin reductive amination during standard Fmoc-SPPS. This tag integrates a hydrophilic tri-lysine module, N-Boc-protected for compatibility with SPPS, preassembled with a Hmb-derived backbone modification, thereby eliminating the need for additional non-standard solid-phase assembly steps. O-GABAylation ensures its stability towards TFA cleavage to deprotect and release the peptide from the solid support. Neutral pH incubation triggers selfimmolative de-GABAylation, restoring the acid sensitivity required for tag removal after NCL. The utility of this strategy is demonstrated through the synthesis of the challenging protein target human SUMO-2, and its modularity is further demonstrated by the successful incorporation of multiple Hmb<K3> units within a single peptide segment.

papers.title: Catalyst-free hydrophosphination of alkenes enabled by protic solvents
papers.abstract: Under catalyst-free conditions, activated olefins are subject to hydrophosphination in Click-like efficiency unexpectedly in polar protic (alcohol) solvent. Hydrophosphination of more challenging styrene substrates can be achieved in polar protic solvents as well under irradiation. While the former reaction is apparent conjugate addition, the latter is still under consideration.

papers.title: Probabilities of phases. An algebraic approach in determining the exact phases II
papers.abstract: In this paper we give the exact linear equations to solve the phase problem for a point atom structure. The equations are written for P 1, but they are very easily extended to other spacegroups.

papers.title: Review of a Withdrawn Drug Candidate: Adipiplon
papers.abstract: Adipiplon is a benzodiazepine-site ligand developed for insomnia that was discontinued after phase II trials due to safety concerns. To extract structural insights relevant to drug design, we performed an in silico docking comparison of adipiplon and representative dual orexin receptor antagonists (DORAs) at two sleep-related targets: the GABA_A receptor benzodiazepine binding site and the orexin type 2 receptor (OX2R). Docking calculations using AutoDock Vina showed that adipiplon can form binding poses at both receptors, with intermediate predicted binding scores relative to reference ligands. At the GABA_A benzodiazepine site, adipiplon frequently formed polar anchor-like interactions, whereas at OX2R its anchoring patterns were less consistent. In contrast, DORAs showed more reproducible anchor interactions and more favorable score distributions at OX2R. These results suggest that adipiplon has structural flexibility across multiple receptor pockets but may lack a dominant anchoring mode associated with target selectivity. This docking-based analysis provides a structural hypothesis and illustrates the value of reassessing withdrawn drug candidates for structure-based drug design.

papers.title: Computational Prediction and Synergistic Performance Enhancement in Triple-Crosslinked Biopolymer Nanocomposites for Sustainable Food Packaging: A Literature-Validated Framework
papers.abstract: We present a literature-validated computational framework for predicting synergistic mechanical and barrier properties in biodegradable food packaging materials through hierarchical integration of three distinct crosslinking mechanisms in biopolymer networks. The composite architecture combines: (1) chemical crosslinking via citric acid thermal esterification (∆σ_chem = 20 MPa), (2) enzymatic crosslinking via transglutaminase-catalyzed isopeptide bond formation (∆σ_enz = 8 MPa), and (3) ionic crosslinking via calcium-mediated alginate egg-box coordination (∆σ_ionic = 6 MPa), with hierarchical reinforcement from exfoliated montmorillonite nanoplatelets (aspect ratio 100-300). Employing interpenetrating polymer network (IPN) theory with conservative synergy enhancement factors (α = 2.0-2.8), we predict tensile strength of 32.4 ± 1.8 MPa-representing 6.2-fold enhancement versus pure starch baseline (5.2 ± 0.8 MPa)-oxygen permeability of 318 ± 22 cc•mil/m²•day•atm (65% reduction via tortuous diffusion pathways), and complete aerobic biodegradation of 89.2 ± 2.1% mass loss within 120 days per ASTM D5338 protocol. The observed synergistic enhancement factor of 2.8× (measured 32.4 MPa versus interference-corrected additive prediction of 11.6 MPa) demonstrates non-additive performance characteristic of multi-mechanism hierarchical polymer architectures. This computational methodology, validated against 14 peer-reviewed experimental studies, establishes a framework for rational design of petroleum-plastic alternatives achieving mechanical properties exceeding low-density polyethylene (LDPE: 10-20 MPa) while maintaining environmental biodegradability under home composting conditions, addressing the sustainability challenge of 146 million metric tons annual global plastic production.

papers.title: Embedding-Guided Design Rules for Programmable Mitochondrial Protein Import and Modular Organelle Organization
papers.abstract: Mitochondria coordinate cellular energy conversion, metabolism, signaling, and survival through the coordinated action of thousands of proteins distributed across the outer membrane, intermembrane space, inner membrane, and matrix. Yet, a systems-level framework that links mitochondrial protein sequence space to sub-mitochondrial localization and import logic remains incomplete. Here, we use protein language model embeddings from ESM2 to analyze the human mitochondrial proteome curated in MitoCarta3.0. Low-dimensional projections of embedding space recover biologically meaningful structure, with proteins forming compartment-enriched groupings consistent with submitochondrial organization. Unsupervised clustering and bipartite network analysis identify oxidative phosphorylation, protein import, and mitochondrial translation as highly connected hubs that anchor mitochondrial functional architecture. To probe engineering principles, we perform in silico minimaledit mutagenesis of N-terminal targeting presequences and quantify shifts in embedding position and predicted import potential. These perturbation experiments show that modest changes in charge distribution, hydropathy, and helix propensity can tune import behavior, with a substantial subset of proteins exhibiting large, directionally consistent shifts in predicted targeting. Together, the results support a modular view of mitochondrial organization and indicate that targeting presequences behave as tunable control elements rather than fixed codes. This work provides an embedding-driven computational blueprint for programmable mitochondrial targeting, with applications in synthetic biology, therapeutic payload routing, and organelle engineering.

papers.title: Stereoinvertive Cross-Coupling for Trisubstituted Alkenes Enabled by Sulfoximine Leaving Group
papers.abstract: Although stereodivergent synthesis of alkenes is highly valuable in organic synthesis, its scope has been largely confined to disubstituted alkenes, and extension to multisubstituted alkenes remains a formidable challenge. Herein, we report a stereoinvertive cross-coupling enabled by alkenyl sulfoximines with aryl boronic acids in the presence of nickel catalyst, in stark contrast to typical cross-coupling reactions of alkenyl (pseudo)halides, which proceed with retention of stereochemistry of substrates. Given that our previously developed Pd-catalyzed Suzuki-Miyaura cross-coupling of alkenyl sulfoximines proceeds in a stereoretentive fashion, this Ni-catalyzed protocol paves the way for the stereodivergent synthesis of trisubstituted alkenes from a common precursor. Combined experimental and computational studies reveal that the sulfoximine group plays a pivotal role in achieving the stereoinvertive transformation with its coordinating ability.

papers.title: Elucidating the Molecular -Scale Mechanisms of Zinc Adsorption on Redox -Active Ligand Tethered to Mesoporous Silica
LC-MS FADE: Leveraging Untargeted Lipidomics Data for Fatty Acid Profiling
papers.abstract: Fatty acid (FA) profiling has historically been accomplished via gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS) and can be used in tandem with liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS) untargeted lipidomics workflows to comprehensively investigate global FA and lipid dynamics. This approach requires both GC-MS and LC-MS platforms, adding expense, acquisition time, and sample consumption, yet lacks the ability to directly correlate fatty acid profiles to intact lipid molecules. To address this issue, we present a novel workflow to determine FA profiles from lipidomics datasets termed LC-MS fatty acid data extraction (LC-MS FADE). FA data were extrapolated from intact lipid peak areas and expressed as percent fractions. A total of eight disparate lipid extracts, including fetal bovine serum, nutritional yeast, beef liver, canola oil, Viral Producing Cells 1.0, Arabidopsis thaliana, Acheta domesticus, and Escherichia coli K12 were analyzed to assess the accuracy of this strategy. By comparing the LC-MS FADE profile to the GC-MS FAME profile, an average R 2 value of 0.89 was obtained, demonstrating that LC-MS FADE can successfully and accurately extract FA profiles. LC-MS FADE datasets displayed improved sensitivity by identifying more FAs with improved reproducibility compared to GC-MS FAME data. Significantly, novel lipid class-specific FA insights were obtained using LC-MS FADE that were not accessible with traditional GC-MS methods. LC-MS FADE can also be applied retrospectively to existing lipidomics datasets, enabling extraction of FA profiles from data not originally intended for FA analysis. This novel method provides additional insight into FA dynamics in complex untargeted lipidomics datasets and can be readily implemented into lipidomic workflows.

papers.title: Direct Electron Transfer-Type Gas Diffusion Electrode for Efficient CO 2to-Formate Bioconversion across Broad and Low CO 2 Levels
papers.abstract: Bioelectrocatalytic CO 2 reduction to value-added chemicals offers a sustainable route for carbon recycling; however, achieving high activity under low CO 2 conditions remains a major challenge. Herein, we report a direct electron transfer (DET)-type gas diffusion electrode (GDE) utilizing formate dehydrogenase 1 (FoDH1) from Methylorubrum extorquens AM1 for efficient CO 2 -to-formate conversion across a broad range of low CO 2 levels. The electrode surface was modified with pyrene derivatives using multi-walled carbon nanotubes (MWCNTs) to tailor the enzyme-electrode interface, enabling favorable enzyme orientation for rapid electron transfer. A 1-pyrenemethylamine (PyNH 2 )-modified GDE with FoDH1 exhibited a current density of-1.2 mA cm -2 at a reduction potential of-0.9 V, which was twice that of the pristine electrode, and generated formate with a Faradaic efficiency of 82 +/- 5%, outperforming previously reported GDE systems. Kinetic analyses under controlled CO 2 conditions (0.04-100%) revealed a notably low apparent Michaelis constant ( K M,app ) of 2.6 +/- 0.3%, which is less than one-third of that of the solution system, indicating high CO 2 affinity. This enhancement is attributed to the direct supply of gaseous CO 2 to the catalytic layer, avoiding equilibrium limitations in the electrolyte solution. These results lead to a promising tool for enzymatic CO 2 reduction using emission gases from industrial sources and provide key design principles for practical CO 2 -recycling technologies.

papers.title: Empirical Assessment of Energy Consumption and Chemical Productivity Across Diverse Mechanochemical Platforms
papers.abstract: Mechanochemical synthesis is frequently identified as a sustainable alternative to solvent-based methods, yet empirical data regarding the energy consumption of various milling platforms remains scarce. This study provides an assessment of the electrical power demand and chemical productivity across five distinct milling modes: vibratory, planetary, media-free, high-energy, and disc milling. We demonstrate that manufacturer reported power specifications consistently overestimate actual operational demand by up to a factor of 3.1x which can lead to inaccuracies in sustainability metrics. Through the investigation of two diagnostic probe reactions, we observed that power consumption is primarily determined by the mechanical inertia and frequency of the hardware-the platform's "Energy Fingerprint"-with the internal chemical payload exerting a negligible effect. The results show that increasing operational frequency beyond a certain threshold results in disproportionately high energy consumption relative to the incremental gains in chemical yield. By integrating yield and measured power into an energetic return metric (mmol/kWh), we compare the efficiency of different platforms at the laboratory scale. Furthermore, we observe that the fixed electrical overhead of high-capacity hardware, such as disc and planetary mills, becomes more efficient as reaction volumes increase. This work provides a standardized framework of measured energy values, enabling more accurate Life Cycle Assessments and supporting the optimization of mechanochemical processes for industrial applications.

papers.title: Functional Abiotic Metabolite Assembly: Hypothesis for the Early Events in the Origin of Life
papers.abstract: The RNA world hypothesis offers a compelling conceptual framework for the emergence of life, yet a fundamental gap remains between simple abiotic molecules and complex functional RNA polymers. Amyloid-like assemblies have been proposed as plausible earlier prebiotic scaffolds due to their ability to compartmentalize into microenvironments and catalyse chemical reactions.

papers.title: Identification of isotocyanozene at an Australian drug checking service
papers.abstract: Novel synthetic opioids of the 'nitazene' class, comprised of 2-benzylbenzimidazole opioids and related derivatives, present a growing threat to public health. Most recently emerging in European drug markets in 2019, the nitazene group of drugs has been associated internationally with adverse effects in drug users, overdose clusters, and significant mortality. The variable structure and high potency of many nitazene derivatives, which can exceed that of fentanyl, poses a significant challenge to the public health and early warning systems used to detect and respond to the emergence of new high-risk substances. This report describes the early identification of an emerging nitazene derivative, isotocyanozene (5-cyano isotodesnitazene), at Australian drug checking service in an expected opioid sample of uncertain identity presented by a member of the public. Close collaboration with affiliated university laboratories has provided characterisation data and evaluation of the in vitro µ-opioid receptor biological activity to support the assessment and monitoring of this emerging substance and related desnitazene and 5-cyano desnitazene derivatives. The study highlights the rapid response possible though engaging drug users with drug checking services as a market monitor and early warning system to alert health services and the broader community to the presence of unexpected, high-risk substances. Integration of well-resourced and supported drug checking services provides a powerful approach to tackle the public health threats associated with novel synthetic opioids and other drugs of concern.

papers.title: Decoding the Blood-Brain Barrier Permeation in CNS Drug Discovery: An Integrated Framework through High Fidelity Explainable ML and Low Dimensional Linear Discriminant Mapping
Single-crystalline 3D covalent organic frameworks with nbo topology
papers.abstract: Three-dimensional covalent organic frameworks (3D COFs) are promising crystalline porous materials, but the elucidation of their structure remains challenging, particularly for those featuring spiroborate linkages. Herein, we report the synthesis of a 3D single-crystalline COF (scCOF) with nbo topology, constructed from a rigid square-planar monomer, tetracyclopentatetraphenylene (TCTP), and spiroborate linkages. Theoretical calculations revealed that the TCTP core possesses higher rigidity than phthalocyanine, effectively suppressing structural fluctuations during framework formation. The structure of the resulting TCTP-COF was successfully determined using microcrystal electron diffraction (MicroED), revealing a non-interpenetrated cubic framework with space group Im -3 m . TCTP-COF exhibits high crystallinity, thermal stability up to 320 °C, and permanent porosity with a Brunauer–Emmett–Teller surface area of 1360 m 2 ·g –1 . To the best of our knowledge, this work represents the first structural determination of a spiroborate-linked 3D scCOF using electron diffraction methods, providing a new design strategy for expanding the chemical space of highly ordered 3D COF architectures.

papers.title: Benchmark assessment of collinear, mixed-reference, and spin-adapted variants of spin-flip time-dependent density functional theory, for closed-and open-shell molecules
papers.abstract: Spin-flip methods provide access to certain electronic states having multireference character while retaining single-reference cost. However, conventional spin-flip time-dependent density functional theory (SF-TDDFT) often suffers from severe spin contamination that may engender inaccurate state ordering or ambiguous state character. For singlet excited states, this is largely rectified by a "mixed-reference" formulation (MRSF-TDDFT), while a spin-adapted formalism (SA-SF-TDDFT) addresses spin contamination in a general way for arbitrary multiplicities. Here, we revisit SA-SF-TDDFT and demonstrate that it significantly improves the agreement with reference data as compared to other variants of SF-TDDFT, and also relative to conventional (spin-conserving) TDDFT.
