papers.abstract: Autonomous scientists enabled by large language models and agentic reasoning have become a compelling narrative for accelerating research. Here, we pose that laboratory autonomy is not primarily a text problem, since experiments have to be run in the world of instrument-addressable actions and constraints, and planned based on costs, latencies, and rewards. We argue for a bottomup foundation for self-driving laboratories (SDLs) that complements language-first planning by introducing frameworks that translate hypotheses into decisions executable on real tools. We propose three operational principles, including (a) adopt an information-efficiency objective that maximizes decision-relevant information per unit experimental cost through comprehensive acquisition and minimal decisive experimental design, (b) require hypotheses to compile into experimental footprints defined by experimentally-accessible actions, constraints, observables, and decision rules, and (c) treat reward design as the central bottleneck in closed-loop experimentation, especially when mapping high-dimensional measurements to utility and extending to sequential decision-making. We frame SDLs as long-horizon, out-of-distribution discovery systems where accelerating the full experiment–model–decision loop and emphasizing physical and chemical knowledge discovery over short-term correlations is necessary to translate lab-scale optimization into durable technological and manufacturing impact.

papers.title: Systematic evaluation of a cluster-continuum-model workflow to compute the free energies of solvation of ions in different solvents
papers.abstract: A partially automatized computational protocol for the construction of embedded microsolvated clusters based on a combination of the quantum cluster growth algorithm, DFT reoptimization, higher-level energy computations, conformer selection based on free energy, embedding into advanced implicit solvation models like COSMO-RS, and averaging over a range of cluster sizes, has been validated and applied to systematic cluster-continuum calculations of various single-ion Gibbs free energies of solvation in different solvents. For aqueous solution, excellent agreement with a widely accepted single-ion scale based on the cluster pair approximation is found, to within the error margins of that scale, but without anchoring to one particular ion like the latter. The same cluster-continuum method has been applied to test the underlying assumption of equal free energies of solvation of large spherical cations and anions of the other scale in wider use, the TATB scale. The calculations suggest that in water the BPh 4 - anion has a ca. 20 kcal/mol more negative solvation free energy than the AsPh 4 + cation. Application of such corrections to the widely used TATB-based values shifts them even further from the CPA scale and from the present calculation. Applications of the cluster-continuum method to single-ion values in acetonitrile show that here the CPA-based proton value may be less settled than with water, methanol, or DMSO, and it deserves closer examination. Finally, the solvation of the fluoride ion is compared in a variety of different solvents (water, acetonitrile, methanol, DMSO, diethylether, and benzene). While water and methanol provide the most negative solvation free energies, acetonitrile, methanol, and DMSO are not far behind, and even the relatively nonpolar diethylether and benzene exhibit appreciable stabilization. This is due to significant charge-assisted C-H...F hydrogen bonds to the highly compact fluoride ion in all of the formally aprotic solvents, involving in some cases more than one proton from a given solvent molecule in a chelate binding mode.

papers.title: Sustained Redox Photodynamic Therapy via Supramolecular Charge Separation of a Redox-active Dye
Food Informatics: Transforming Food Systems Through Data-Driven Discovery
papers.abstract: The term Food Informatics has been increasingly used in scientific publications. However, its definition and scope remain inconsistent across disciplines and applications. This lack of conceptual clarity limits cumulative knowledge development and constrains the formation of Food Informatics as a coherent interdisciplinary field. In this commentary, we review representative definitions and usages of Food Informatics and propose an updated definition with a clearer scope. The aim is to provide a more consistent conceptual foundation that supports integration across data, methods, and food systems research.

papers.title: On the Prospect of Chemically Transferable Coarse-Grained Electronic Models for Soft Materials
Operando Characterisation of SEI Formation in Ni-Rich Lithium-Ion Cells to Explore Ethylene Carbonate-Free Electrolyte Systems
papers.abstract: The pursuit of high-energy lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) has driven the adoption of Ni-rich layered oxides such as NMC811, but their reactivity with conventional ethylene carbonate (EC)-based electrolytes leads to interfacial instability and performance loss. Here, we systematically investigate how electrolyte composition and additives influence the formation and stability of the solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) in graphite||single-crystal NMC811 cells. Using commercial-grade pouch cells under a consistent formation protocol, we combine operando acoustic emission (AE) and electrochemical atomic force microscopy (EC-AFM) with complementary electrochemical and structural characterisation to probe SEI formation in real time. We first assess common additives in EC-containing electrolytes, then progressively reduce EC content, and finally introduce SEI-forming additives into EC-free electrolytes. While EC promotes SEI growth on graphite, it also accelerates parasitic reactions at the Ni-rich cathode, resulting in limited gains in cycling stability. By contrast, EC-free electrolytes with targeted additives, particularly 10% fluoroethylene carbonate (FEC), form more uniform SEI layers, suppress gas evolution, and significantly enhance cycling stability, achieving 95.5% capacity retention after 300 cycles. This work demonstrates the dual role of EC in Ni-rich systems and highlights how correlative operando methods can guide rational electrolyte design for long-lived, high-energy LIBs.

papers.title: A Computational Fluid Dynamics Analysis of Haemodynamics in Renal Arteries Following Endovascular Aneurysm Repair: The Impact of Stent-Induced Partial Coverage and Arterial Orientation
FAST COMPUTATION OF EXACT SYMMETRY-CORRECTED RMSD OF CONFORMERS
papers.abstract: The root mean square deviation (RMSD) quantifies molecular structural similarity in computational chemistry, yet accurate computation requires accounting for topological symmetry. Existing methods face severe limitations: graph isomorphism approaches exhibit prohibitive costs for symmetric molecules, while polynomial-time algorithms sacrifice chemical correctness by ignoring connectivity. This work introduces a novel algorithm leveraging Hierarchical Neighborhood of Atoms (HNA) partitioning, a recursive classification of chemically equivalent atoms, to enable fast exact symmetrycorrected RMSD while maintaining topological validity. Hierarchical decomposition reduces search complexity from the product to the sum of branch combinations, achieving computation time reductions of several orders of magnitude. Comprehensive benchmarks on the Chemical Component Dictionary (1,437,176 pairs) demonstrate mean execution times of 3.8 ms per pair, outperforming topology-preserving methods by 11-42× while completing all calculations without failures. For the Biologically Interesting molecule Reference Dictionary (26,203 pairs), the algorithm achieves sub-millisecond mean performance (488 µs per pair). For proteins, the method produces chemically correct assignments compared to 83%+ topologically invalid mappings from Hungarian algorithm implementations. For myoglobin, hierarchical decomposition reduces 4.1 × 10 176 total hydrogeninclusive assignments to merely 1,536 tractable combinations. This algorithm enables practical exact symmetry correction across the full spectrum of molecular complexity.

papers.title: Circularity in Sequence-Controlled Copolyamides Enabled by Regioselective Enzymatic Hydrolysis
papers.abstract: Sequence-defined polymers enable precise control over macromolecular structure and function, but both their synthesis and end-of-life management remain fundamental challenges. Achieving high sequence fidelity is synthetically demanding, and conventional depolymerization methods lack regioselectivity, leading to irreversible loss of encoded molecular information and limiting polymer circularity. Enzymatic catalysis offers a potential solution by combining substrate specificity with selective bond cleavage. Here, we report the synthesis, characterization, and regioselective enzymatic depolymerization of poly(MAXA), an alternating sequence-defined copolyamide composed of hexamethylenediamine-adipic acid (MA) and p-xylylenediamine-adipic acid (XA) repeat units. Poly(MAXA) was synthesized via solid-state polycondensation of sequence-defined oligomers, enabling precise control over repeat-unit order. Polymer microstructure and sequence fidelity were confirmed by 13 C NMR spectroscopy and MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry. Comparison with a statistical copolymer analogue and Nylon-66 demonstrated pronounced differences in crystallinity, morphology, and thermal behavior arising from sequence control. Screening of 96 nylon hydrolase homologs against poly(MAXA) revealed strongly enzyme-dependent depolymerization profiles. While tetrad formation was generally favored, enzymes displayed pronounced sequence selectivity, preferentially releasing distinct sequence-encoded tetrads XAMA or MAXA. Computational modeling of enzyme–substrate complexes identified structural features consistent with the observed regioselectivity. Together, these results establish selective enzymatic depolymerization as a viable strategy for the circular recycling of sequence-defined polymer and provide a foundation for the rational engineering of enzymes for programmable polymer deconstruction.

papers.title: Antimony Recovery and Debromination of Flame-Retardant Electronic Waste Plastics
papers.abstract: Antimony oxide is a common synergist for brominated aromatic flame retardants. These are combined in plastic housings for electronics from televisions to computers, as well as plastics used in transportation vehicles such as automobiles, ships and aircraft. Antimony is deemed a critical metal that is insufficiently mined to meet demands; hence, routes for its recovery are essential. Conventional pyrolysis results in substantial antimony loss and toxic emissions, whereas solvent-based recycling relies on time-consuming and hazardous sequential steps of debromination followed by antimony recovery. Here, we introduce isothermal-clamped flash Joule heating (IC-FJH), which generates a spatially isothermal reaction zone and enables simultaneous debromination and Sb recovery within seconds. Ultrafast isothermal heating stabilizes Sb predominantly as the metal, achieving a recovery yield of ~90% and a purity of >97%, reducing losses from vapor-phase transport and from residual solids. At the same time, IC-FJH achieves deep debromination, reducing toxic brominated organic species by 34 to 51%, compared to slow heating conditions. The toxic brominated organics were converted into inorganic streams, predominantly forming HBr with 83% recovery. By life-cycle assessment, IC-FJH reduces resource consumption by 72%, climate change burdens by 65%, water use by 80%, and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon formation by 100% compared to conventional pathways. Overall, IC-FJH offers a viable route for the sustainable recovery of antimony and the end-of-life management of e-waste, while advancing cleaner production and a circular economy.

papers.title: MXene Synthesis in Seconds by Flash Joule Heating
papers.abstract: MXenes exhibit exceptional structural and physicochemical properties, enabling them to be applied in a wide range of fields, including energy storage and electromagnetic shielding. However, conventional etching synthesis routes, such as hydrofluoric acid (HF) etching, Lewis acid etching, and molten-salt etching, are limited by long reaction times, high energy consumption, and severe chemical hazards. Here, we developed a rapid, scalable, and environmentally benign approach for MXene synthesis via sequential flash Joule heating-chlorination and fluorination (FJH-ClF). By precisely tuning the thermodynamic and kinetic parameters, diverse high-quality layered MXenes with excellent electrochemical performance were synthesized through the selective removal of interstitial atoms from nine different MAX phases, each within 30 s. This universal FJH-ClF strategy drastically reduces energy and reagent usage, establishing a safe, cost-effective, and sustainable method for next-generation MXene manufacturing.

papers.title: Quantifying the Spin-Optical Properties of Bent π-Carbene Molecular Qubits
papers.abstract: Through spin-selective intersystem crossings (ISCs) among photoexcited electronic states, organic π-diradicals can be spin-polarised by optical excitation, positioning them as long-lived, tunable, and scalable qubits. Recent advancements have utilised triplet π-carbenes of bent structures, which unlock an additional spin-selective ISC channel between the ground states, improving the qubit's spin-optical properties. However, bent π-carbenes also lose spin selectivity in the excited-state ISC step and a compromise has yet to be found. In this work, we balance the two effects by developing a minimal Hamiltonian for bent π-carbenes, the first of its kind, and solving its spin-optical interactions analytically. Our approach is a valuable alternative to large-scale ab initio screenings, which are highly intensive given the costs of existing open-shell ab initio methods. We find the ideal π-carbene to have a high spin density on its central atom and excitations dominated by HOMO-to-SOMO transitions. These strategies minimise deleterious ISC steps through destructive interferences, which can be accentuated by populating the carbene non-bonding orbital. These chemically intuitive results not only inform qubit designs but also offer a minimal Hamiltonian framework for accelerating high-throughout discovery of optically addressable π-carbenes. As an illustration, we exemplified our design rules on a realistic molecular prototype, completed by a rigorous ab initio characterisation over different carbene bond angles.

papers.title: From 'KGeP' to the Protonated P 4 -like Anion (HGe 3 P) 2− and the Endohedral Zintl Cluster [Mn@Ge 10 P 2 ] 3−
papers.abstract: Supporting information for this article is given via a link at the end of the document.

papers.title: Exploring Molecular Orbital Pseudospins as All-Optical Quantum Sensors
papers.abstract: Recent developments in molecular qubits have focused on transitions among electron spin states, interfaced with optical electronic transitions for better sensing resolutions. However, molecular electronic states can also form pseudospins, and using them as qubits would bypass the additional step of spin-optical interfacing. In this work, we discuss whether precessions of molecular orbital pseudospins under environmental influence can allow for all-optical quantum sensing via optical pump-probe spectroscopy. We find that these oscillations can survive rotational averaging and be detected in isotropic environments. Unfortunately, fast electronic decoherence is likely to constrain measurements to environmental quantities that strongly influence orbital pseudospins, which are uncommon. This pitfall may be mitigated by further molecular engineering, which can be faster than spin-based qubits given the high ab initio predictability of molecular electronic states.

papers.title: Synthesis of Tetrakis-Amino-Ethylene Derived Organic Reductants via Thermal Decomposition of Tris-Aminomethanes
papers.abstract: Tetrakis-amino-ethylene (TAE) based reductants are valuable in organic transformations, such as cross-electrophile coupling, but are not widely utilized due to their high cost and complicated syntheses. Here, we report the one-pot synthesis of TAEderived organic reductants via thermal decomposition of tris-aminomethanes. Specifically, the neat reaction of N,N-dimethylformamide dimethylacetal (DMF-DMA) with pyrrolidine or piperidine generates tetrakis-pyrrolidino-ethylene (TPyE) or tetrakis-piperidino-ethylene (TPiE) in one-pot through the in-situ generation of a tris-aminomethane intermediate. The thermal decomposition of other tris-aminomethanes was also investigated.

papers.title: Benchmarking Machine-Learned Potentials for Water-Splitting Catalysts: Validation on Pt and IrO2 Surfaces Using OC20 and OMat24
papers.abstract: Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials (MLIPs) enable first-principles accuracy in modeling complex catalytic interfaces at reduced cost. The Open Catalyst 2020 (OC20) and Open Materials 2024 (OMat24) datasets consist of density functional theory (DFT) data for adsorbates on metals and inorganic bulk materials, respectively. In this work, we benchmarked the Universal Model for Atoms (UMA) trained on the OC20 and OMat24 datasets with DFT calculations for adsorption energies on Pt and IrO 2 , respectively. We evaluated adsorption energies of common adsorbates such as *H, *O, *CO, and *NO on Pt, and reaction intermediates in the water splitting reaction, such as *O, *OH, and *H, on IrO 2 . UMA-OC20, trained using non-spin polarized DFT-RPBE energies with no van der Waals (vdW) corrections on metallic surfaces, reproduced the adsorption energies from the same flavor of DFT within 0.1 eV. However, the energy difference between UMA-OC20 and spin-polarized DFT was ∼1.2 eV, with the difference mainly arising from the reference gases. UMA-OMat24, trained using spin-polarized DFT-PBE with vdW corrections, predicted adsorption energies within 0.3 eV of the energies from the same flavor of DFT on IrO 2 . When both the DFT flavor and geometry were kept fixed between the MLIPs and DFT, UMA-OC20 and UMA-OMat24 predicted adsorption energies within 0.1 and 0.2 eV of their corresponding DFT adsorption energies, respectively. The norm of coordinate differences between UMA-OC20 and DFT was ∼0.1 Å for a system size of ∼20 atoms, while it was < 0.6 Å for a system size of ∼60 atoms, between UMA-OMat24 and DFT. MLIP requires considerably fewer (∼6000 times less) CPU-hours compared to DFT. Thus, we recommend opting for an MLIP-followed-by-DFT procedure, as it not only reduces the total compute time but also ensures accurate geometry and energies.

papers.title: CO2 reduction by lanthanide borohydride complexes and hydroboration reactivity
papers.abstract: Although lanthanide borohydride precursors are useful building blocks to access a variety of molecular lanthanide complexes, the nucleophilic reactivity of the attached [BH 4 ] – unit has not been thoroughly investigated. We herein report the reaction of [La(Cp ttt ) 2 (BH 4 )] ( 1 , Cp ttt = 1,2,4-tris( tert -butyl)cyclopentadienyl) towards CO 2 , leading to the formation of a formate complex, which exists as an equilibrium mixture between the dimeric and monomeric forms in aromatic solvents. DOSY 1 H NMR experiments allowed a convenient analysis of the reaction mixture and provided an estimation of the hydrodynamic radii for both species. Hydroborane reagents (BH 3 , HBPin, H(9-BBN)) further react with the formate complex, leading to the formation of borylated methanol and the corresponding lanthanide boroxide complexes. Preliminary investigations were performed to investigate the viability of complex 1 as a pre-catalyst in the hydroboration of CO 2 .

papers.title: Data-centric training enables meaningful interaction learning in protein–ligand binding affinity prediction
papers.abstract: Predicting protein–ligand binding affinity remains a fundamental challenge in drug discovery, where deep learning models have become central. However, these models often struggle with protein and ligand biases and limited generalization. Here, we present a convolutional neural network (CNN)-based scoring function, DockTDeep , that accurately predicts protein–ligand binding affinities by carefully designing the training strategy instead of increasing architectural complexity. A systematic evaluation of data augmentation strategies shows that random rotation, unlike commonly used 90-degree rotations, effectively mitigates rotational variance. We also introduce a straightforward but efficient regularization technique that reduces reliance on isolated protein or ligand features and, coupled with random rotation, promotes learning of meaningful intermolecular interaction patterns. DockTDeep outperforms or matches state-of-the-art scoring methods on standard benchmarks across diverse external datasets, supporting its applicability in drug design. Moreover, a comparative evaluation of existing out-of-distribution splitting schemes identified Pfam-CV as the most stringent, enforcing a degree of separation by similarity that surpasses other strategies. Additionally, our results indicate that the performance degradation observed under more stringent splitting schemes is unlikely to reflect an intrinsic inability of the model to capture physically meaningful interactions. Instead, it points to limitations in the available training data, which inadequately sample the diversity and complexity of binding landscapes required for robust generalization to previously unseen interaction patterns.

papers.title: Vibronic contributions to hyperfine-mediated spin kinetics
papers.abstract: The hyperfine interaction is a cornerstone of spin-dependent processes, yet the kinetic modelling of this mechanism remains limited by the Born-Oppenheimer approximation, obscuring the observation of coherent pathways that underpin many photophysical systems. Here, we introduce a unified theoretical framework that rigorously incorporates vibronic contributions through a phase-consistent Herzberg-Teller expansion of the hyperfine Hamiltonian. Application to the FMNH•-Cys• radical pair shows that second-order vibronic coupling enhances h y perfine-mediated electronic transitions between spin states by up to 10 8 to 10 9 -fold. The S◦→T◦ rate increases from ~ 5 − 40 s −1 (Franck-Condon) to ~ 2 × 10 8 s −1 − 1 × 10 9 s −1 (Herzberg-Teller), while the T◦ →S◦ rate increases from ~ 4 × 10 2 − 1 × 10 3 s −1 to ~ 1 × 10 10 − 5 × 10 10 s −1 . This observed nanosecond timescale correlates well with the microsecond lifetime photoadduct formation central to its function. This work underscores the importance of incorporating a vibronic description in hyperfine-driven dynamics and provides a generalised and transferable methodology that captures essential non-Condon effects even at the single-structure level; thus serving as a complementary tool for systems where full ensemble sampling is impractical or not yet integrated into standard workflows.

papers.title: NeuroRepurpose: An In Silico Approach to Repurposing Drugs for Multiple Sclerosis Treatment
papers.abstract: Multiple Sclerosis affects nearly 2.9 million people worldwide. Recent studies have identified STAT3 as a key factor in the disease, making it a prime target for drug development. However, most STAT3 inhibitors are extremely expensive, and creating cheaper alternatives could take another decade to refine and bring to market and the public. To address this, I developed a neural network designed to differentiate between STAT3 inhibitors and non-inhibitors. I trained the model using experimentally verified inhibitors sourced from PubMed. After clustering the data and applying feature selection, I optimized the model for accuracy. Once the model was trained, I screened FDA-approved drugs to identify potentially repurposable treatments. The top 9 candidates were subjected to molecular docking simulations to test their binding affinity for STAT3. Finally, I conducted ADMET (Absorption, Distribution, Metabolism, Excretion, and Toxicity) predictions to assess their suitability as viable treatments, and tested the compound in an artificial neural tissue environment to ensure accuracy. This approach revealed Celecoxib as the most viable treatment, and could revolutionize Multiple Sclerosis treatment plans for the better.

papers.title: Beyond Atom Economy: Reconciling Catalytic Activity with Lifecycle Sustainability Through Dynamic Metal-Ligand Cooperativity
papers.abstract: Traditional catalyst design optimizes turnover frequency and selectivity while neglecting lifecycle sustainability. This mini-review addresses a critical research question: Can dynamic metal-ligand cooperativity enable catalysts that simultaneously achieve high activity and inherent regenerability through reversible ligand exchange? We examine how hemilabile ligands, redox-non-innocent frameworks, and self-healing coordination environments create catalysts with built-in lifecycle optimization. Analysis reveals that 10-40 kJ/mol weaker metalligand bonds enable poison release and active site restoration without external intervention. Mechanistic studies show Mars-van Krevelen cycles and pendant base assistance maintain activity over 10,000+ hours while facilitating low-energy regeneration. Lifecycle assessment demonstrates 60-80% reduction in cradle-to-grave carbon footprint through synthesis energy reduction (15-35 vs 75-100 MJ/kg), regeneration efficiency (85-95% recovery), and metal recyclability (90% vs 20%). Research gaps include limited understanding of ligand dynamics under industrial conditions and absence of standardized sustainability metrics. This framework positions dynamic coordination chemistry as the missing link between catalytic performance and true sustainability.

papers.title: Catalysts for a Sustainable Future: Designing the Molecular Architects of Green Chemistry
papers.abstract: Catalysis drives nearly 90% of chemical manufacturing, yet the environmental costs of catalyst production, operation, and disposal remain underexplored. This review outlines the principles of sustainable catalyst design through a lifecycle perspective, emphasizing earth-abundant materials, low-energy synthesis routes, extended operational lifetimes, regeneration strategies, and end-of-life recyclability. Advances in single-atom catalysts (SACs) are highlighted as transformative, enabling nearly complete metal atom utilization, alternative reaction pathways at reduced temperatures and pressures, and enhanced stability through strong coordination environments. Ammonia synthesis is presented as a proving ground, where sustainable SAC systems demonstrate significant reductions in energy demand and CO 2 emissions compared to the conventional Haber-Bosch process. Green synthesis methods-including hydrothermal, sol-gel, and mechanochemical approachesare shown to lower production footprints by 60-80% relative to traditional hightemperature techniques. A comprehensive set of sustainability metrics is proposed, integrating synthesis energy, turnover number, deactivation rate, regeneration efficiency, atom utilization, embodied carbon, and recyclability. Collectively, these strategies illustrate how environmental responsibility and economic viability can converge in catalyst innovation, with the potential to avoid hundreds of millions of tonnes of CO 2 annually while reshaping the chemical industry toward a circular and renewable future.

papers.title: Markovnikov-Selective α-C(sp³)-H Alkylation of Glycine with Alkenes via Photoredox/Co Dual Catalysis
papers.abstract: This study reports a synergistic photoredox/cobalt catalytic strategy for the Markovnikov-selective addition of glycine derivatives to alkenes. The transformation proceeds under mild conditions, without external oxidants or stoichiometric hydrogen sources, and exhibits broad functional-group tolerance and high site-selectivity across diverse substrates, including heteroaryl motifs, pharmaceutical scaffolds, natural products, and oligopeptides. Gram-scale reactions confirm the scalability and synthetic practicality of the protocol. Mechanistic investigations reveal a dual catalytic cycle involving radical cross-coupling and identify the nitrogen-bound proton of the glycine derivative as the key hydrogen source, with α-C–H bond cleavage as the rate-determining step. This method complements our previously developed anti-Markovnikov platform, providing a concise, efficient, and controllable approach for the modular assembly and late-stage modification of α-amino acids and peptides.

papers.title: Thionation of structurally isomeric polymers for tuning thermoresponsive behavior
papers.abstract: Lower critical solution temperature (LCST) behavior in water-soluble polymers arises from a delicate balance between polymer-water and polymer-polymer interactions, which in turn depend on backbone and side-chain structure. Recently, thionation (the replacement of the amide carbonyl oxygen by sulfur) was introduced as a new tool to adjust LCST behavior in poly(2-oxazoline)s by weakening hydrogen bonding and reducing polarity. However, it remains unclear how this approach translates across different amide-based polymers and LCST mechanisms. The effect of thionation on a set of structurally isomeric homopolymers having secondary, tertiary, and cyclic amide motifs and distinct phase-transition behaviors is systematically studied. By combining thionation with solution characterization techniques and molecular dynamic simulations, we examine how modifying the amide functionality influences polymer hydration, aggregation, and phase separation. This comparative approach reveals how thionation acts not only as a cloud point modifier, but as a structure-dependent alteration that reshapes polymer-water, polymer-polymer interactions and agglomeration pathways.

papers.title: Sustainable Catalyst Design for Ammonia Synthesis: Single-Atom Catalysts, Green Synthesis Routes, and Lifecycle Optimization Strategies
papers.abstract: The environmental footprint of industrial catalysis extends beyond operational emissions to encompass catalyst synthesis, deactivation, and disposal-phases that collectively contribute 30-45% of total lifecycle carbon emissions for long-lived heterogeneous catalysts. This review examines emerging strategies for sustainable catalyst design through the lens of ammonia synthesis, a process consuming 1.5% of global energy (5.5 EJ annually) and generating 450 million tonnes CO2 per year. We critically evaluate five interconnected design principles: utilization of earth-abundant materials (Fe, Co, Ni) rather than precious metals (Ru, Pt); implementation of lowenergy synthesis methodologies (hydrothermal, sol-gel, mechanochemical routes reducing production energy by 60-80%); engineering of extended operational lifetimes through deactivation-resistant architectures; development of regeneration protocols restoring 80-95% activity; and design for end-of-life metal recovery exceeding 90%. Particular emphasis is placed on single-atom catalysts (SACs), which achieve nearcomplete metal utilization (90% vs. 10-30% for nanoparticles) while enabling alternative reaction mechanisms at reduced temperatures (200-300°C vs. 400-500°C conventional). Characterization by X-ray absorption spectroscopy, scanning transmission electron microscopy, and operando infrared spectroscopy reveals that atomically dispersed Fe-N4 coordination sites facilitate associative N 2 activation pathways with activation barriers 40-60 kJ/mol lower than dissociative mechanisms on Fe nanopar30 ticles. Comprehensive lifecycle assessment frameworks demonstrate that integration of these sustainable catalyst design principles could reduce global chemical industry emissions by 300-400 million tonnes CO2 annually while simultaneously improving economic competitiveness through extended catalyst lifetimes and reduced material costs. The review concludes by identifying critical research directions required to 35 accelerate translation from laboratory innovation to industrial implementation.

papers.title: Removing Dyestuff From Wastewater Using Zeolite Adsorbents -I -Preparation Of The Adsorbent
papers.abstract: The presence of dyes in wastewater from the textile industry represents a significant environmental problem, primarily due to the toxicity of reactive dyes to microorganisms and their adverse impact on aquatic ecosystems. Adsorption is one of the most commonly applied treatment approaches for dye removal, largely because of its operational simplicity, relatively low cost, and the possibility of regenerating the adsorbent material. Clinoptilolite, a naturally occurring and widely available zeolite, is characterized by a porous framework and a relatively uniform pore size distribution, which has led to its use in diverse applications, including the removal of cationic dyes from water and the purification of natural gas. Nevertheless, the negatively charged surface of natural clinoptilolite restricts its ability to adsorb anionic reactive azo dyes in aqueous systems. This drawback can be addressed through surface modification with appropriate surfactants, which impart a positive charge to the zeolite surface. In the present study, clinoptilolite was modified using dodecyl dimethyl ethyl benzyl ammonium chloride, and the influence of key operational parameters, including solid-to-liquid ratio, contact time, and initial dye concentration, was systematically examined. The findings indicate that surfactant modification substantially improves the adsorption performance of clinoptilolite, supporting its potential use as an effective adsorbent for the removal of reactive azo dyes from wastewater.

papers.title: Accelerated development of ethanol-to-butadiene conversion catalysts by high-throughput experimentation
papers.abstract: Ethanol-to-1,3-butadiene (ETB) conversion proceeds through a cascade of elementary steps, including ethanol dehydrogenation, dehydration, C-C coupling, and hydrogen transfer. Because these steps require a coordinated balance of redox and acid-base functions, and because their density, strength, and spatial proximity depend strongly on synthesis and post-treatment, ETB catalyst optimization is sensitive to both composition and preparation history. Here, a parallelized preparation platform is developed that integrates wet impregnation under agitation with gas-flow drying and calcination as a program-controlled sequence in a single furnace-based workflow. Coupled with high-throughput fixed-bed evaluation, this workflow was used to screen Zn-Hf catalysts supported on mesoporous silica and to map how pore structure and preparation history govern butadiene (BD) formation between 400 and 450 °C. Support type dominated product distributions, with Q-10 preferentially yielding BD, Q-30 favoring acetaldehyde (AcH), and Q-3 exhibiting ethylene-rich behavior. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy revealed pronounced surface enrichment of Zn and Hf on Q-3, consistent with a stronger contribution from dehydration-promoting surface-expressed species. Follow-up tests at fixed nominal composition showed that preparation history can further tune product distributions, and sequential impregnation combined with a dilute HCl washing step after Hf impregnation increased BD yield to 58% on Q-10 while maintaining low ethylene yield. These results provide practical guidance for designing Zn-Hf ETB catalysts and demonstrate how workflow integration enables scalable, quantitatively comparable screening across preparation-dependent parameter spaces.

papers.title: NMR and Ultrafast Spectroscopic and Mass Spectrometry Characterisation of a Carotenoid Isolated from Methylobacterium extorquens strains PA1 and AM1
papers.abstract: Methylobacterium species are prominent members of the plant phyllosphere, where they are exposed to fluctuating environmental conditions, including intense ultraviolet (UV) radiation. To mitigate such stressors, these bacteria commonly synthesise carotenoids as an oxidative protection. In this study, we investigated the carotenoid production of two closely related methylotrophic strains, Methylobacterium extorquens PA1 and AM1 (short PA1 & AM1), with a particular focus on the influence of iron availability. We identified and comprehensively structurally characterised the main carotenoid produced by both strains by using ultraviolet-visible (UV-Vis) spectroscopy, high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC), high-resolution mass spectrometry (HRMS) with collision-induced dissociation (CID), ion mobility-mass spectrometry (IM-MS), nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy, and ultrafast transient absorption (TA) spectroscopy. We show that both strains produce, unaffected by the iron availability, the same carotenoid, identified as 4-[2-O-11Zoctadecenoyl-β-D-glucopyranosyl]-4,4′-diapo-Ψ,Ψ-carotene-4,4′-dioate. However, the iron availability strongly influenced the carotenoid production making it an potentially interesting factor for boosting bacterial carotenogenis in biotechnological settings.

papers.title: Aqueous synthesis of nucleoside analogs via direct coupling of natural sugars and purines
papers.abstract: Nucleosides are the most widespread and fundamental N-glycosides in biological processes. Despite their prevalence in nature and significance of their analogs in medicinal chemistry, conventional synthetic approaches rely on complicated upstream preparation including well-designed glycosyl donor and pre-silylated nitrogen-containing acceptor. Here we report a direct coupling strategy delivering purine glycoside by the N-glycosylation between natural sugar and purine in aqueous solution. The transformations are realized by one simple and concise step using a new imidazolinium chloride salt, with high chemo-, regio-, and stereo-selectivity. These findings greatly simplify access to various nucleoside analogs. Mechanistic studies suggest that sugar and purine are respectively activated by the imidazolinium cation and chlorine anion of the reagent.

papers.title: Synthesis of Tetrakis-Amino-Ethylene Derived Organic Reductants via Thermal Decomposition of Tris-Aminomethanes
papers.abstract: Tetrakis-amino-ethylene (TAE) based reductants are valuable in organic transformations, such as cross-electrophile coupling, but are not widely utilized due to their high cost and complicated syntheses. Here, we report the one-pot synthesis of TAEderived organic reductants via thermal decomposition of tris-aminomethanes. Specifically, the neat reaction of N,N-dimethylformamide dimethylacetal (DMF-DMA) with pyrrolidine or piperidine generates tetrakis-pyrrolidino-ethylene (TPyE) or tetrakis-piperidino-ethylene (TPiE) in one-pot through the in-situ generation of a tris-aminomethane intermediate. The thermal decomposition of other tris-aminomethanes was also investigated.

papers.title: Construction of Shape-Persistent All-sp2 Square Nanohoops via the Formation of Multiple Imine Bonds
papers.abstract: Shape-persistent all-sp 2 square nanohoops represent a synthetic challenge due to the difficulties associated with maintaining bond angles of ca. 90° between adjacent π-conjugated panels. Here, we report the rational design and synthesis of square-shaped nanohoops by employing dibenzo[b,f][1,5]diazocine as rigid perpendicular units. Density-functional-theory (DFT) calculations suggested that the formation of cyclic tetramers is thermodynamically favored. Accordingly, the acid-mediated formation of multiple imine bonds via condensation of monomers bearing 2-aminobenzoyl groups afforded cyclic tetramers in yields of up to 60%. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction analyses confirmed square geometries with preserved panel planarity and tunable internal cavities. The strategy is applicable to a variety of panels (benzene, biphenyl, terphenyl, and pyrene), whereby panel rigidity controls tetramer selectivity. The thus obtained square nanohoops exhibit reversible acid responsiveness and enable high-yield monomer recovery via acid hydrolysis—a unique recycling strategy currently unattainable to conventional cross-coupling methods. This study hence establishes a versatile platform for the construction of shape-controlled π-conjugated macrocycles with tunable properties.

papers.title: Exploring the influence of substitution in the gelation characteristics of oxotriphenylhexanoates (OTHOs)
papers.abstract: Gels are broadly applicable as they are very adaptable smart materials. Currently their utility is limited as there is a scarcity of information about the effects of the addition of a functional group to a gelator. This work investigates the effect of placing substituents in different positions on the modular oxotriphenylhexanoate (OTHO) scaffold. Nine different Br-substituted OTHO compounds (OTHO-Br) were synthesized, and tested in 18 different solvents, observing a clear influence from substitution on the behavior of the system, supplemented with single-crystal XRD studies. The influence of the solvent on gelation was studied using Hansen solubility parameters, and the morphology of the xerogel fibers was studied using SEM. Finally, the mechanical properties of the gels were determined by oscillatory rheology. The observed structure-property relationships were subsequently validated using additional, differently substituted OTHO derivatives, providing a general framework for rational gel design for this rather unexplored gelator type.

papers.title: Single-Atom Engineered Poly(Heptazine Imide) Photocathodes for Efficient Alkaline Hydrogen Evolution
papers.abstract: The development of sustainable photoelectrocatalysts for the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) is key for advancing solar-to-X energy conversion technologies. Ionic crystalline poly(heptazine imides) (PHI) emerges as a versatile platform owing to their facile synthesis, high chemical stability, and tunable electronic structure under visible-light irradiation. Herein, Fe, Cu, and Co transition metals are incorporated into PHI via cation-exchange strategy, acting as co-catalytic centers that enhance charge separation photoelectrochemically. Photoelectrochemical tests reveal that metal-modified PHIs outperform pristine NaPHI for alkaline HER upon blue-light activation, with CoPHI showing the highest 2 activity. CoPHI displays a current densities at voltages vs RHE of ≈ −60 mA cm-2 at −0.76 V (or −5 A mg-1 at ≈ −0.72 V), with a favorable onset potential (≈ 0.55 V), a low Tafel slope (53 mV dec-1), reduced charge-transfer resistance (≈ 120 Ω), and an enhanced photocurrent response (≈ 9 μA cm-2). Advanced spectroscopic and microscopic analyses reveal that atomically dispersed Co sites operate as Co 2+ centers, facilitating interfacial charge transfer, due to their lower electronegativity and favorable electronic coupling with the PHI framework. These findings suggest CoPHI as an efficient carbon-based proof-of concept platform for single-atom-engineered photoelectrodes in alkaline HER.

papers.title: Low-temperature retro Diels-Alder reactions
papers.abstract: The Diels-Alder (DA) reaction is a widespread synthetic tool that can be employed both in the forward and reverse directions. The retro Diels-Alder (rDA) reaction is used to prepare reactive organic molecules and, more recently, as a type of Dynamic Covalent Chemistry (DCC) for applications in polymer healing and reprocessibility. Synthetic and DCC applications of the rDA are limited by the high temperatures it typically requires. By tuning the sterics of a modular, electron-rich tetramethoxyanthracene donor platform, we are able to observe rapid rDA reactivity below-50 °C for cycloadducts with tetracyanoethylene (TCNE). We access these frontiers of reversibility by simultaneously stabilizing the free anthracene and destabilizing the DA adduct: the electron-rich nature of the tetramethoxyanthracenes lowers the energy of the starting materials, while alkyl substituents at the 9,10-positions of the anthracene donor destabilize the DA adduct. These features manifest in dynamic DA adducts with kinetically accessible DA/rDA reactions between-70 and 55 °C, as well as in the longestknown CC bond in a DA adduct formed by intermolecular cycloaddition (1.637(4) Å).

papers.title: Reaction kinetics of liquid organic hydrogen carriers from first-principles: The methylcyclohexane/toluene pair on Pt(111)
papers.abstract: The use of hydrogen as an energy carrier relies on efficient storage technologies. One appealing alternative is Liquid Organic Hydrogen Carriers (LOHC) where hydrogen is stored in liquid organic molecules at standard conditions. Catalysts are used to facilitate the loading and unloading of hydrogen in the organic molecule and one example is the storage of three hydrogen molecules in toluene (C 7 H 8 ) forming methylcyclohexane (C 7 H 14 ). We have used Density Functional Theory (DFT) calculations in combination with mean-field microkinetic modeling to understand the factors controlling the activity and selectivity of Pt(111) as catalyst for the toluene/methylcyclohexane LOHC pair. The simulated temperature dependence of turnover frequencies, reaction orders, and apparent activation energies are in agreement with experimental trends and the rate controlling steps are identified. The simulations reveal that stabilization of methylcyclohexane adsorption is one potential way to improve the rate of dehydrogenation. The unwanted side reaction of hydrodemethylation of toluene to benzene is not relevant on Pt(111), however, the simulations indicate that the presence undercoordinated Pt-sites will make this pathway an issue.

papers.title: Computer Vision Enables Monitoring and Kinetic Analysis of Structurally Diverse Carbon Monoxide Surrogates
papers.abstract: Carbon monoxide (CO) surrogates are valuable synthetic reagents that circumvent the hazards of handling CO gas directly. However, owing to the structural diversity of available surrogates, their varied triggering conditions, and the requirement for sealed reactor systems, quantitative understanding of their CO release kinetics has remained elusive. Here, we report a non-contact computer vision method for monitoring and comparing vessel-specific CO release from ten structurally diverse surrogates in two chamber COware reactors. By tracking the colorimetric response of a ruthenium-based chemosensor, we establish a scoring system based on cumulative CO flux-from surrogate activation through gas-phase mass transfer to sensor capture-benchmarked against a CO balloon reference. This approach reveals a four-fold range in surrogate reactivity scores and enables systematic investigation of how reaction parameters such as base strength, solvent polarity, and stirring rate modulate CO release kinetics. We demonstrate that these kinetic differences translate directly to carbonylation reaction outcomes: in Pd-catalyzed Suzuki-Miyaura carbonylation, surrogate score correlates linearly with product conversion, consistent with an inverse dependence on CO concentration. The methods presented enable rational surrogate selection and open new possibilities for the quantitative design of synthetic methodologies dependent on controlled gas release.

papers.title: Scalable Modeling of Multi-Spin Ensembles in SABRE Hyperpolarization: A Symmetry-Based Framework for Zero and Ultralow Fields
papers.abstract: This work presents a theoretical framework for quantitative, scalable modeling of SABRE (Signal Amplification by Reversible Exchange) experiments under zero- and ultralow-field (ZULF) conditions. SABRE exploits the singlet spin order of parahydrogen to hyperpolarize nuclear spins of substrates without chemical modification, enhancing NMR signals. In ZULF SABRE method polarization transfer occurs in ultralow magnetic fields where Zeeman interactions are comparable to or weaker than scalar couplings, enabling coherent mixing of spin states and revealing interactions often suppressed at high fields. Our approach captures the full quantum dynamics of the SABRE complex, including coherent evolution, chemical exchange, and relaxation, within a Liouville-space formalism. We demonstrate that the Hamiltonian, relaxation, and exchange superoperators possess symmetry with respect to the total spin, allowing the dynamics to be rigorously restricted to the zero-quantum coherence subspace. This symmetry-based reduction yields a scalable framework for efficient simulation of multi-spin SABRE systems. The approach is validated against full Liouville-space calculations for small systems and is further applied to a 14-spin SABRE complex, demonstrating its ability to treat spin systems of a complexity well beyond the reach of conventional full Liouville-space simulations. The framework thus provides a predictive tool for optimal polarization fields, ZULF NMR spectra and the design of novel hyperpolarization experiments.

papers.title: Operando Interfacial Dynamics Govern Cation Effects in Electrochemical CO2RR
papers.abstract: Electrolyte cations profoundly influence electrocatalytic reactions, such as the electrochemical CO 2 reduction. How cation identity controls operando interfacial dynamics and selectivity remains unresolved, not least due to a lack of methods capable of resolving such dynamics. Here we show that understanding cation effects requires a time-domain perspective, by combining Dynamic Response Spectroscopy with operando ATR-SEIRAS and sequence-learning neural networks trained on over 10 5 time-resolved spectra. We resolve cation-specific (Li + , Na + , K + , and Cs + ) differences in charge-discharge reversibility and temporal coupling between solvent, ions, and adsorbates. Supported by AIMD simulations, we reveal that the double layer evolves through smooth relaxation and intermittent collective reorganizations, dependent on cation identity. Catalysis depends on whether interfacial reorganizations are dynamically coupled to adsorbate stabilization and electricfield buildup. These results identify time-domain descriptors of interfacial adaptability as key activity and selectivity determinants, opening pathways toward dynamic catalytic operation that leverages interfacial reorganization for enhanced performance.

papers.title: Uncertainty in MD-Derived Diffusion Coefficients Depends on Analysis Protocol, Not Just Simulation Data
papers.abstract: Bonkowski and De Souza [Sol. Stat. Ionics 429, 116967 (2025)] provide a guide for performing molecular dynamics simulations of ion transport, including methods for estimating diffusion coefficients and their uncertainties from mean-squared displacement (MSD) data. The discussion of uncertainty in estimated diffusion coefficients presents the statistical properties of specific analysis protocols—ordinary least squares regression with particular data processing choices and other, statistically equivalent, approaches—without explicitly stating the scope of applicability for these results. Without explicit scope statements, the guide presents these results as universal characteristics of diffusion coefficient estimation; i.e., uncertainty in D* is determined only by the input simulation data. Here, we clarify that for diffusion coefficients estimated by linear regression of MSD data, the uncertainty depends not only on the input simulation data, but also on the choice of statistical estimator (OLS, WLS, GLS) and data processing decisions (fitting window extent, time-averaging). By clarifying this dependence on analysis protocol, we hope to help researchers avoid incorrect uncertainty estimates and encourage the adoption of statistically efficient methods for analyzing molecular dynamics simulations.

papers.title: Synthesis of α-Ethylidene β-lactones via lactonization/1,3-H-transposition of α-vinyl-β-hydroxy acids.
papers.abstract: Since their discovery, β-lactones have garnered significant interest due to their unique chemistry and bioactivity. Our ongoing synthesis and evaluation of β-lactones for biological activity have revealed that DIC lactonization of α-vinyl and α-ethynyl β-EWG- β-hydroxy acids results in 1,3-H transposition, leading to the formation of α-alkylidene and α-allene lactones, respectively. The straightforward synthesis of these compounds will enable us to explore their utility for further chemical transformations.

papers.title: SynFrag: Synthetic Accessibility Predictor based on Fragment Assembly Generation in Drug Discovery
papers.abstract: AI-driven molecular generation encounters a "generation-synthesis gap": most computationally designed molecules cannot be synthesized in laboratories, limiting AI-assisted drug design (AIDD) applications. Current approaches to assess synthetic accessibility (SA) include computer-aided synthesis planning (CASP) tools that perform retrosynthetic searches, and machine learning-based SA prediction models that provide rapid scoring. CASP tools are computationally expensive for high-throughput screening, while existing SA prediction models may lack chemical synthesis logic or exhibit variable performance across different chemical spaces. We developed SynFrag, an SA prediction model using fragment assembly autoregressive generation to learn stepwise molecular construction patterns. Self-supervised pretraining on millions of unlabeled molecules enables learning of dynamic fragment assembly patterns beyond fragment occurrence statistics or reaction step annotations. This approach captures connectivity relationships relevant to synthesis difficulty cliffs, where minor structural changes substantially alter SA. Evaluation across public benchmarks, clinical drugs with intermediates, and AI-generated molecules shows consistent performance across diverse chemical spaces. The model produces sub-second predictions with attention mechanisms corresponding to key reactive sites. SynFrag provides computational efficiency suitable for large-scale screening while maintaining interpretability for detailed SA assessment in drug discovery workflows. Online platform: https://synfrag.simm.ac.cn . Code and data available: https://github.com/simmzx/SynFrag .

papers.title: When Chemistry is Too Colourful: Gamut Clipping in 8-bit sRGB Risks Misinterpretation of Camera-Based Chemical Analysis
papers.abstract: Digital cameras are increasingly utilised to capture visual changes in chemical processes. Monitoring colour with computer vision tools serves as a valuable proxy for monitoring bulk chemical changes. Most consumer-grade cameras digitise the colours captured using the 8-bit sRGB colour space. Despite its ubiquity, it restricts the range of colour information that can be stored. With regards to chemical analysis and process monitoring, the limitations of using the 8-bit sRGB gamut have not been addressed. When real-world vivid colours one attempts to record lie outside the bounds of 8-bit sRGB, the digitisation of those colours can result in distortion, clipping, or loss of chemically relevant colour data. Ultimately, these sRGB gamut limitations risk the chemist misinterpreting the data they collect from a camera. In this paper, we examined the visible spectrum of a series of common dyes, and determined their colours spectroscopically, without the limitation of 8-bit sRGB encoding. We investigated how 8-bit sRGB encoding affects the interpretation of time-series data from theoretical colour changes in five dyes. Highly saturated chemical samples exceeded the 8-bit sRGB colour gamut, causing colour distortions and structural breaks in reaction-monitoring time series data, risking misinterpretation as kinetic phenomena of genuine chemical origin. Our findings underscore the importance of paying close attention to colour representation in digital chemistry. We offer practical guidance for researchers using and interpreting colour data for use in computer vision method development.

papers.title: Web Platform for Automated RMSD Calculation Across Heterogeneous Molecular Files
authors: Caius Vinicius Coelho Moreira de Souza
papers.abstract: The Root Mean Square Deviation (RMSD) is essential for molecular conformational comparison in computational chemistry and structural bioinformatics, with a wide range of uses from protein-ligand docking pose comparison to analysis of molecular dynamics trajectories. One challenge in computing RMSD is ensuring a precise matching of atoms between structures, especially with different file formats like PDB, PDBQT, SDF, MOL2, and XYZ, each with their own conventions for atom ordering, naming, and content. To ensure consistency in atom mapping, scientists often dedicate a significant amount of time to manually preprocess files, a process that is both cumbersome and error-prone, ultimately discouraging reproducibility. In response to this bottleneck, we have developed a web platform that automates the computation of RMSD for molecules across different file formats. The platform utilizes a strong backend pipeline to standardize variable inputs into a common molecular representation, resulting in a consistent atom map. This removes the necessity for manual intervention and enables accurate and direct RMSD computation. The program utilizes the Streamlit framework for a user-friendly interface and is hosted on an institutional server for widespread use. Preliminary findings show that the platform can accurately compute RMSD values between files of varying formats, simplifying a crucial step in molecular modeling. This advancement marks a significant achievement in enhancing the efficiency, accessibility, and reproducibility of structural comparisons in computational life sciences.

papers.title: Leveraging Hidden-Space Representations Effectively in Bayesian Optimization for Experiment Design through Dimension-Aware Hyperpriors
papers.abstract: Hidden-space molecular representations derived from pretrained graph neural networks, Transformer models, and large language models offer an appealing alternative to conventional encodings for Bayesian optimization (BO) in chemical experiment design. However, their performance benefits in BO remain poorly understood and difficult to assess in practice, and, when deployed within current chemical BO frameworks, they often do not yield clear advantages over traditional representations. Here, we show that this behavior arises from a previously underappreciated interaction between representation dimensionality and Gaussian process kernel hyperpriors, rather than from limitations of the representations themselves. We demonstrate that different chemical representations induce substantial variations in search-space dimensionality, which, when paired with fixed or mismatched lengthscale hyperpriors, lead to flat marginal likelihood landscapes and severely degrade surrogate learning and acquisition optimization. To address this issue, we introduce a dimension-aware adaptive hyperprior, tailored to reaction optimization, whose characteristic lengthscale scales with the square root of the search space dimensionality. Benchmarking across multiple reaction optimization datasets and molecular representations shows that this adaptive hyperprior consistently restores and amplifies the performance advantages of hidden-space featurizations over traditional representations, such as Mordred or one-hot encoding. Our results identify hyperprior calibration as a critical requirement for fair evaluation and effective deployment of modern molecular representations in chemical BO.

papers.title: Physicochemical Properties of α-Fluoroalkyl-Substituted Cycloalkylamines and Amino Acids
papers.abstract: A systematic matched molecular pair analysis of α-fluoroalkyl-substituted alicyclic amines (C 3 –C 6 cycloalkanes and tetrahydropyran) and their benzamide models by benchmarking them against β- and γ-substituted analogues is reported. Experimentally obtained acidity and lipophilicity values (p K a and Log P ) revealed an exceptionally strong and predictable impact of α -fluoroalkyllation on the acid-base properties of the amine moiety with an approximately additive contribution of 1.6 ± 0.1 p K a units per fluorine atom. Lipophilicity trends were more nuanced, yet α -substitution produces distinctive ΔLog P patterns consistent with competing inductive and local polarization effects near the amide fragment. Mapping the obtained dataset in Log P– p K a space highlights the cluster-type localization of the various fluoroalkylated patterns, enabling property tuning via isosteric substitutions. Finally, multigram-scale access to diastereopure α -CF 3 cycloalkyl amino acids was proposed along with quantification of their ionization profiles, supporting application of these scaffolds as versatile fluorinated building blocks for drug discovery.

papers.title: Synthesis and Physicochemical Properties of trans-2-Fluoroalkyl-Substituted Cyclopentane Building Blocks
papers.abstract: A scalable synthesis of trans -1,2-fluoroalkyl-substituted cyclopentane building blocks was developed. The approach relies on orthogonal late-stage functionalization of a common precursor – monoester of trans -1,2-cyclopentanecarboxylic acid. Fluoromethyl-substituted derivatives were accessed via exhaustive reduction of the COOH group, activation of the resulting primary alcohol as a triflate, and nucleophilic substitution with fluoride. Meanwhile, difluoro- and trifluoromethyl groups were introduced through deoxofluorination of the corresponding aldehyde or carboxylic acid. The resulting fluorinated esters were efficiently diversified into a broad range of building blocks relevant to medicinal chemistry, including carboxylic acids, primary amines, azides, alcohols, and sulfonyl chlorides. In addition to the synthetic developments, the effect of the fluoroalkyl substituent (CH 2 F, CHF 2 , CF 3 ) on physicochemical properties of the cyclopentane derivatives was established by measuring p K ₐ and Log P values of model derivatives.

papers.title: Multi-Step Oxygen Redox Mechanism in the Polyanionic Lithium-Rich Cathode Li2FeSiO4
papers.abstract: Lithium-rich cathode materials offer significantly increased energy densities compared to conventional cathode materials, due to their ability to store charge beyond the formal transition-metal redox limit through what is conventionally termed "oxygen redox". The nature of this excess charge storage, whether it involves formal oxygen oxidation or other mechanisms, remains actively debated. Here, we report a computational study of the redox behaviour of the prototypical lithiumrich polyanionic cathode, Li 2 FeSiO 4 , where the covalently-bonded [SiO 4 ] 4− framework has been proposed to stabilise the structure against oxygen oxidation. Using density functional theory and ab initio molecular dynamics, we predict that removal of the second lithium (LiFeSiO 4 → FeSiO 4 ) results in the oxidation of oxide ions to form molecular O 2 within the bulk material, mirroring the degradation pathway observed in lithium-rich oxides despite the distinct polyanionic structure. This oxygen redox process proceeds via a multi-step mechanism involving initial formation of Fe IV with high Fe–O covalency, followed by Fe IV disproportionation to Fe III and Fe V , with subsequent oxygen dimerisation via peroxide intermediates as the high-valent Fe species are reduced. The complete mechanism incorporates multiple processes previously proposed as competing explanations for oxygen redox, including high-valent metal formation, ligand-to-metal charge transfer, and oxygen dimerisation. Our findings demonstrate that polyanionic frameworks do not inherently prevent O 2 formation, and reveal that different proposed oxygen redox mechanisms can function as components of a compound process rather than mutually exclusive pathways.

papers.title: Dicationic Tetrylene Ligands Modulate Pt0 π-Acid Catalysis
papers.abstract: Dicationic heavy tetrylenes [E] 2+ (Ge, Sn, Pb) represent a rare class of potentially ambiphilic yet electron-withdrawing ligands for transition-metal catalysis and bond activation. However their broader exploration has been hampered by intrinsic instability, donor quenching, and weak polycation–metal affinity. Here we overcome these limitations by utilizing neutral double-decker bis(phosphinophenylimino)pyridine ligand 1 to anchor Pt 0 and [E] 2+ in a one-pot synthesis, forming a series of heterobimetallic [ 2E ] 2+ . [E] 2+ as Z-type ligands results in polarized Pt 0 →E II interaction, which leads the rare square-planar geometries for Pt 0 centers and consequently π-acid catalysis on a Pt 0 center. [ 2E ] 2+ is ambiphilic, binding isocyanides at Pt and [M(CO) 5 ] fragments at the tetrel center (E = Sn, M = Cr, Mo, W), respectively. Using ν CN of isocyanide adducts as an IR probe, we benchmark the σ-acceptor strength of [E] 2+ across the platform for the first time (Ge 2+ > Sn 2+ > Pb 2+ ). This trend translates directly into Pt 0 -catalyzed 1,6-enyne cycloisomerization, enabling up to ~1,000-fold rate tuning via (i) element identity (Ge, Sn, Pb) and (ii) Lewis-acid binding at E (e.g., [M(CO) 5 ]; M = Cr, Mo, W). Collectively, these results establish a coarse-to-fine tuning strategy for Pt 0 π-acidity using a modular and electronically adjustable [E] 2+ ligand platform, representing a new main-group strategy for catalyst design. Supporting information for this article is given via a link at the end of the document.

papers.title: Perdefluorinative borylation of perfluoroalkyl and gem-difluoroalkenes
papers.abstract: Polyfluorinated organic molecules including perfluoroalkyl substances (so-called PFAS) are broadly used as water-repellents and flame retardants, in paper coatings, fire extinguishing chemicals, agrochemicals, and drugs. However, these compounds are resistant towards degradation and known to bioaccumulate in the environment and organ tissue with numerous associated negative health effects. This persistence further renders the chemical treatment of PFAS highly challenging. We herein report a “zipper” reaction that strips off all fluorine atoms from a perfluoroalkyls bound to an alkene and converts these PFAS compounds into synthetically useful boronate building blocks without destruction of the carbon framework. This is achieved by a combination of pinacolborane and lithium methoxide that iteratively removes the fluoride substituents from the attached perfluoroalkyl chain through repeated hydroboration/β-F-elimination steps. The reaction then installs a boronate function at the chain terminus, which overall turns the problematic PFAS into useful synthesis reagents. Yields of up to >99% are achieved per fluorine atom and the isolation of LiF by simple filtration is demonstrated. The reaction also works on gem -difluoroalkenes, which we conclude to be intermediates of the PFAS perdefluoro-monoborylation reaction.

papers.title: Machine learning-based screening of high-entropy alloy AlCoCrFeNi particles produced via high-energy mechanical alloying method
papers.abstract: There is a growing interest in exploring high entropy alloys (HEAs) due to their superior mechanical and thermal properties. Although numerous routes exist for producing HEA particles, mechanical alloying (MA) remains the most conductive method at the laboratory level due to its simplicity and cost-effectiveness. In powder metallurgy, the degree of alloying plays a crucial role in achieving the desired quality of final manufactured parts. However, in mechanically milled HEA powders, segregation often arises from localized energy concentrations, leading to significant compositional inhomogeneity. Currently, researchers rely on conventional energy-dispersive spectroscopy (EDS) to assess alloying state. SEM alone is less time-consuming than with EDS integration. Yet, EDS maps can be inaccurate, have low reproducibility, and be misleading for HEA powder, indicating alloyed composition, even when the opposite is true. This study proposes a deep learning regression approach to predict compositional homogeneity, which can be thresholded to classify alloyed and segregated particles directly from scanning electron microscopy (SEM) images. The approach utilizes compositional/alloying uniformity derived from per-particle EDS composition vectors of the AlCoCrFeNi HEA system, serving as a ground truth. Different regression models were trained to directly predict Shannon entropy (H), a nondimensional measure of compositional uniformity, with DenseNet121 achieving an R² of 0.918 and an MAE of 0.03, corresponding to an average deviation of approximately 3% of the full alloying uniformity scale. This approach enables rapid, objective, reproducible, and automated screening of HEA powder, offering a scalable alternative to conventional microanalysis techniques. The proposed model can be integrated into existing laboratory workflows for mechanically alloyed AlCoCrFeNi systems, enabling quality assessment during the intermediate and final stages of milling using only bench-top SEMs without requiring an EDS detector.

papers.title: TUNING CRYSTAL GROWTH OF HYDROXYAPATITE NANOPARTICLES FOR ENHANCED FOLIAR PHOSPHORUS DELIVERY
papers.abstract: Phosphorus fertilization remains inefficient in many cropping systems, motivating the search for alternative delivery methods that minimize losses and boost plant uptake. Nano-sized hydroxyapatite particles have become a promising phosphorus source, though their effectiveness heavily relies on particle design. In this study, we synthesized nano-sized hydroxyapatite by hydrothermal method with controlled crystal growth and physicochemical properties to better suit foliar applications. We systematically examined how synthesis parameters affect particle size, morphology, and crystal growth to identify an optimal suspension formulation for foliar fertilization. Foliar application trials of engineered nano-sized hydroxyapatite on potato plants showed successful uptake. These findings indicate that controlling the crystal growth of nano-sized hydroxyapatite could provide a basis for developing advanced nanofertilizers with improved nutrient efficiency.

papers.title: Investigating CO electrolysis on cobalt at elevated temperatures to produce C4+ hydrocarbons
papers.abstract: CO2 electrolysis has emerged as a promising route to carbon-neutral fuels, but Cu-based catalysts are largely limited to producing short-chain (< C3) products. In contrast, strong *CO-binding metals that underpin thermochemical Fischer-Tropsch (FT) catalysis remain largely unexplored under electrochemical conditions. Here, we investigate Co catalyst for producing C4+ hydrocarbons in membrane electrode assembly (MEA) reactors operated at elevated temperatures (30-80 °C) and industrially relevant current densities. At 80 °C and 250 mA/cm 2 , Co produces a complex spectrum of 28 distinct C₁-C₆+ products, with hydrocarbon partial current densities increasing linearly with temperature. Density functional theory calculations reveal that direct *CO dissociation on Co remains kinetically inaccessible under these reaction conditions, pointing instead to protonation-mediated pathways in CC bond formation. Strong adsorption of unsaturated hydrocarbons leads to surface coking and progressive deactivation, which is mitigated through pulsed electrolysis. Unlike Cu, the activity and selectivity trends on Co are only weakly dependent on alkali-metal cation identity, highlighting a mechanistic regime more closely analogous to FT catalysis than to classical *CO-*CO dimerization. Together, these findings establish Co as a prototype strong *CO-binding catalyst for electrochemical long-chain hydrocarbon synthesis and provide mechanistic design principles for developing high-temperature electrochemical routes to sustainable, naphtha-range fuels.

papers.title: Chemically Fueled Systems Chemistry Across Length Scales
papers.abstract: Inspired by nature, chemically fueled reaction cycles provide a general strategy to couple the dissipation of chemical potential to controlled changes in molecular structure, assembly, and material function. Here, we review how kinetically stable yet thermodynamically activated fuels, catalytic activation–deactivation cycles, and supramolecular transformations integrate into a common design spanning molecular, assembly, and material length scales. We unify terminology across communities using diverse systems into state-network descriptions that capture reciprocal coupling between chemical and supramolecular states. Central to function is kinetic asymmetry (feedback from the supramolecular state on reaction rates), which biases reaction flux and enables work-like behavior, including directional motion, adaptive lifetimes, self-healing, oscillations, bistability, and spatiotemporal control of optical, mechanical, and catalytic properties. By contrasting single-point versus multipoint activation and intramolecular versus intermolecular processes, we extract practical design principles and highlight open challenges, including quantitative kinetic descriptions at the assembly scale, management of waste accumulation under sustained fueling, and scaling chemo-mechanical coupling toward higher-order autonomous systems. Overall, this review provides a shared mechanistic language and a set of transferable guidelines for engineering functional, adaptive, chemically powered systems across all length scales.

papers.title: Evolution of Acetylacetone from Solution to Film in Indium Nitrate Combustion Sol-Gel
papers.abstract: This study investigates the evolution of acetylacetone (AcAc) fuel in indium nitrate (Innitrate) combustion sol-gel solution and spin-coated films. The combustion mechanism is studied by varying the AcAc-to-nitrate ratios, referencing pure In-nitrate, pure AcAc, and In(AcAc)3, in which AcAc molecules are fully chelated to indium. Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectra reveal that the functional groups present in the In-nitrate solution are nitrate and hydroxyl. With the addition of AcAc, coordinated keto and enol peaks are also observed along with coordinated nitrate peaks, indicating AcAc and nitrate are both coordinated with indium. However, when spin coating the In-nitrate sol-gel solution to form a film, FTIR spectra show peaks corresponding to water, ammonia, and nitrate only, but no keto/enol peaks associated with indium-coordinated AcAc in the sol-gel films. Thus, AcAc is absent from the film, even though it was coordinated in the precursor solution. On the other hand, AcAc is retained in the film when it is made from an In(AcAc)3 solution without nitrate. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy results corroborate the FTIR findings. Through drying and evaporation studies, we determine that AcAc leaves the In-nitrate sol-gel solutions with the 2-methoxyethanol solvent during spin coating. This study sheds light on the role of AcAc as a fuel and the combustion sol-gel process in thin films.

papers.title: Additive Manufacturing of Metabolically Active Living Materials with Physicochemical Biocontainment
papers.abstract: Additive manufacturing (3D printing) of engineered living materials (ELMs) enables the spatial patterning of cells within three-dimensional (3D) polymer matrices. However, a critical barrier to deploying ELMs is the lack of universal and reliable strategies to contain cells within 3D printed matrices. While synthetic biology renders cell-specific containment, a materials-centric approach can provide a cell-agnostic biocontainment platform. Therefore, this study presents a hydrogel-based additive manufacturing strategy to fabricate ELMs with physicochemical biocontainment. The 3D printed ELMs are fabricated by copolymerizing Pluronic F127-bisurethane methacrylate (F127-BUM) with methacrylic acid (MAA) and 2-(dimethylamino)ethyl methacrylate (DMAEMA). Varying concentrations of these comonomers allow modulation of the ELM functionalities, namely, biocompatibility or antimicrobial properties. In particular, MAA-containing ELMs enable tunable biocontainment of the yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae after immersion in 70 vol.% ethanol, leading to the formation of a time-dependent cell-free zone. The resulting yeast-laden ELMs enhance cell retention up to 300% (98 ± 12 h) and provide an average 38% fermentation increase compared to ELMs composed of only F127-BUM. In conclusion, this hydrogel-based spatiotemporal control strategy improves cell retention and metabolic activity performance in 3D-printed ELMs. These capabilities are promising for several applications, including 3D printed bioreactors and living therapeutic materials.

papers.title: Supertrityl Radical and Cation: The Effect of Large π-Surface for Intermolecular Interactions and Spin/Charge Delocalization
papers.abstract: We report the synthesis and properties of a π-extended trityl radical and cation bearing three hexa- peri -hexabenzocoronenes (HBCs), that is, supertrityl radical and cations. X-ray analysis of cation revealed a propeller-shaped structure with two-dimensional honeycomb assembly through the π-π stacking on HBC units. The radical showed an equilibrium between monomer and dimer, and the computationally optimized dimer has not a σ-bond but a multicenter pancake bond. Despite the large π-surfaces, spin/charge remain mainly localized on the central carbon, resulting in high reactivity under ambient conditions. This behavior is rationalized by Clar’s aromatic sextet rule, offering design principles for π-surface–controlled radicals and cations.

papers.title: Dual Laser LILBID-MS: A new approach for adjustable softness and higher sensitivity
papers.abstract: Biomechanical investigation of native protein complexes is essential to understand structural features, assembly pathways and dynamic interactions, providing key insights into cellular mechanisms. As research questions become more detailed and sample complexity increases, current analytical platforms are often pushed to their performance limits, underscoring the need for continued advances in instrumentation to enable deeper and more comprehensive investigations. Laser-Induced Liquid Bead Ion Desorption (LILBID)-mass-spectrometry (MS) has proven to be a highly suitable native mass spectrometry method for identifying affinities, complexes, stoichiometries and assembly pathways, even for challenging membrane proteins. In LILBID-MS, microdroplets containing the sample are irradiated by a mid-IR laser pulse, leading to desorption of the sample into the gas phase without additional active charging, preserving native-like interactions. Both ion yield and in-source dissociation are regulated by laser energy. This correlation creates a trade-off between ion yield and soft conditions. Increasing laser energy results in higher ion counts but also boosts in-source dissociation, consequently weak protein interactions are difficult to detect. Here, we present a duallaser LILBID approach, which employs two laser pulses with separately controllable intensities and time delay. This new setup allows optimizing the degree of in-source dissociation independently of ion count. This increased control provides the option to adapt to sample specific requirements, e.g. allowing for soft condition measurements, which were previously inaccessible.

papers.title: Characterizing Post-Fire Fine and Ultrafine Particles in the 2025 Eaton Fire Burn Zone and Nearby Areas Authors
papers.abstract: Particle emissions may persist in wildland-urban interface (WUI) fire burn zones during the post-fire period, yet their characteristics remain poorly understood.
