Following full containment of the 2025 Eaton Fire, we conducted mobile and stationary aerosol measurements to characterize the spatial variability and temporal dynamics of fine and ultrafine particles within and around the burn zone. Our results show that the median PM 2.5 concentrations were slightly lower within the burn zone (inside the fire perimeter) than at locations >1000 m outside the perimeter (11.1 vs 12.0 μg/m 3 ), but the burn zone exhibited a higher frequency of PM2.5 spikes (2.8 vs 2.2 peaks/km) with greater peak prominence (9.0 vs 6.0 μg/m 3 ) and shorter durations (2.9 vs 7.5 s). These results indicate transient and intense PM2.5 emissions within the burn zone, which may not be captured by time-integrated measurements. In addition, particle number concentrations within the burn zone were higher than the urban background measured ~23 km downwind (1.2×10 4 vs 9.5×10 3 particles/cm 3 ). Distinct aerosol dynamics were observed within the burn zone that may contribute to elevated particle number concentrations, including (1) formation and growth of ultrafine particles and (2) shrinkage and disintegration of submicron particles. Together, these observations demonstrate that post-fire period represents an active and evolving phase of WUI particle emissions with important implications for human exposure and health.

papers.title: Atmospheric mixing controls air pollution chemistry and mitigation efficacy in high-latitude cities
papers.abstract: Urban air pollution in cold environments poses a significant public health risk. However, the physicochemical processes determining the concentrations of primary and secondary pollutants remain poorly understood. This is due to fundamentally different conditions compared to warmer environments, such as extremely shallow polluted surface layers (PSLs) and low ultraviolet radiation. We apply an observation-driven chemical transport model to a multi-day persistent PSL event during the 2022 Alaskan Layered Pollution and Chemical Analysis (ALPACA) experiment in Fairbanks, AK, USA. The simulations account for pollutant emissions, multi-phase chemical kinetics, and turbulent and advective exchange of PSL air with the clean background atmosphere. This exchange is continuous, occurs on a time scale of 30 min to 3.5 h, and is essential for an accurate representation of the PSL composition. We find that measured diurnal cycles of particulate nitrate reflect the interplay between photochemical nitric acid formation and the loss of nitrate aerosol from of the PSL through mixing with clean background air. The continuous removal and replenishment of PSL aerosol counteracts self-acidification and prevents coagulation with acidic primary sulfate aerosol, thus sustaining sulfate and hydromethanesulfonate (HMS) formation throughout the pollution event. Sensitivity calculations show that within the coupled chemistry and transport system of a shallow PSL, reductions of nitrogen oxide emissions can change the multi-phase oxidation regime and thereby even increase the levels of secondary nitrate and sulfate in the PSL.

papers.title: Refined on-tissue chemical derivatization expands MALDI-MSI capabilities for spatial metabolomics of mammalian organs using EDC and 4-APEBA
papers.abstract: Matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization mass spectrometry imaging (MALDI-MSI) is widely used in metabolomics because it enables high-resolution spatial characterization of molecular distributions directly from tissue. Nevertheless, comprehensive analysis of small, polar metabolites remains difficult due to limited ionization efficiencies and diverse chemical structures. On-tissue chemical derivatization (OTCD) has emerged as an effective strategy to improve ionization efficiency, sensitivity, and selectivity for these analytes. In this study, we established and systematically optimized an OTCD approach for spatial analysis of carbonyl-and carboxyl-containing metabolites in murine tissues using 4-APEBA in combination with carbodiimide crosslinker EDC. Optimization of reagent concentrations, solvent composition, and spray parameters resulted in robust and reproducible derivatization across multiple tissue types. Application to metastatic liver and lung tissue demonstrated the method’s performance in biologically complex environments. Pronounced metabolic heterogeneity correlated with histopathological features in tumor-rich liver sections, and clear tumor-specific localizations were obtained in lung tissue with only small metastatic foci. Metabolic differences between tumor and adjacent healthy regions were consistent with established cancer metabolism pathways, including glycolytic reprogramming. These findings establish a reliable OTCD workflow for MALDI-MSI-based spatial metabolomics capable of interrogating metabolic heterogeneity in clinically relevant tumor models and demonstrate its value for future investigations of tumor metabolism.

papers.title: From Preinstalled AIEgens to In Situ-Generated AIE Motifs: Photo−Triggered Dynamic C=S Bond Formation in Polymers for 4D Luminescence Encryption
papers.abstract: Achieving aggregation-induced emission (AIE) in polymers via in situ, real-time generation of chemically explicit emissive motifs, while simultaneously enabling programmable 4D (time-/sequence-dependent) luminescence, remains challenging. Herein, we report a facile platform that converts nonemissive polymer precursors into AIE-active materials through photo-triggered radical reactions that dynamically construct thiocarbonyl (C=S) motifs in polymer backbones. Two kinetically programmable modules are established by molecular design: Switch 1 affords a metastable C=S motif with reversible write–read–erase behavior, and can further evolve into a stabilized thiobenzophenone-like state under prolonged irradiation; Switch 2 yields a more stable C=S motif featuring delayed-write and write–fix characteristics. Spectroscopic evidence confirms the radical pathway and reversible/stable C=S formation. By substituent engineering of diphenylmethane-derived cores and sulfurcontaining groups, the emission is rationally tuned across the full visible range, supported by quantum-chemical simulations correlating color with frontier-orbital gaps. Leveraging orthogonal control of activation and erasure kinetics via photoinitiators and oxygen-free atmospheres, we demonstrate two modes of 4D fluorescence encryption with time-gated decryption and time-window decoding. This work shifts AIE polymer design from “preinstalled AIEgens” to writable covalent emissive motifs, providing a scalable strategy for smart luminescent coatings and advanced information-security materials.

papers.title: Immunometabolism in Cancer: Targeting Metabolic Pathways to Enhance Immune Responses
papers.abstract: Cancer cell metabolism and immune cell functions have complex interconnections. This review discusses emerging metabolic targets which have the potential to improve immune cell functions. The tumor microenvironment (TME) presents unique metabolic attributes such as nutrient competition, hypoxia, and buildup of immunosuppressive metabolites. These components collectively impair anti-tumor immune responses. Novel therapeutic approaches targeting key metabolic pathways, including glutamine metabolism, adenosine signaling, fatty acid oxidation, and amino acid metabolism have shown potential in improving immunity. For example, glutamine antagonists have demonstrated reprograming of tumor-associated macrophages and enhanced T cell responses. Also, adenosine pathway inhibitors have exhibited synergism with existing immunotherapies. Further, strategies like mitochondrial transfer resulted in rejuvenation of exhausted T cells. Integration of metabolic inhibitors with conventional immunotherapies, such as glutaminase inhibitors with immune checkpoint blockade, have displayed synergistic effects. Notwithstanding the advantages many challenges, like metabolic plasticity, tumor heterogeneity, and poor drug delivery, remain to be overcome. Approaches including development of specific metabolic inhibitors, identification of reliable biomarkers, and implementation of adaptive treatment strategies with the help artificial intelligence are also discussed. This review highlights the potential of immunometabolic interventions in cancer treatment while acknowledging the complexity of targeting cellular metabolism.

papers.title: Leveraging Mechanistic Insights into Stereoretentive ROMP for Precision Synthesis of Poly(p-phenylene vinylene)s
papers.abstract: Poly(p-phenylene vinylene) (PPV) is an important class of conjugated polymers whose properties are largely dictated by structural parameters such as backbone regioregularity, defect content, alkene geometry, sidechain structure, and the sequence of repeat units. Despite decades of development and applications spanning optoelectronic devices to biomedical imaging, a controlled, defect-free polymerization method that affords predictable command over all structural attributes of PPVs has remained elusive. We report herein the synthesis of a variety of regioregular and stereodefined PPVs through stereoretentive ringopening metathesis polymerization (ROMP) of electronically and sterically diverse [2.2]paracyclophane-1,9-dienes (PCDs). Computational studies were combined with experimental findings to uncover structural design principles underlying controlled propagation as well as regio-and stereoselectivity. These findings were harnessed to access well-defined one-shot gradient and block PPV copolymers, as well as unprecedented stereoblocks with cis and trans block geometries through in-situ photoisomerization. The influence of monomer composition and alkene geometry on the optical properties of the synthesized PPVs was also investigated. The exceptional structural control achieved through stereoretentive ROMP of PCDs establishes a unique platform for the precise synthesis of PPVs with tailored properties.

papers.title: Automated Copper-Mediated Radiofluorination of [18F]SynVesT-1: a New Perspective in the Profiling and Control of Chemical Purity
papers.abstract: Copper-mediated radiofluorination (CMRF) of arylstannanes has emerged as a powerful strategy for accessing fluorine-18 labelled radiotracers. Yet concerns regarding chemical impurity profiles remain insufficiently addressed. Here, we report the fully automated production of the clinically relevant synaptic vesicle glycoprotein 2A tracer [¹⁸F]SynVesT-1 on a GE FASTLab module, together with a systematic investigation of the associated impurity profile. Trimethyl- and tri(n-butyl)stannane precursors, as well as non-radioactive analytical standards for all major putative impurities were synthesized. Automated radiosynthesis afforded [¹⁸F]SynVesT-1 in 20-25% non-decay-corrected radiochemical yield, >99% radiochemical purity, and with preserved enantiomeric excess. Comprehensive UPLC-MS analysis revealed the formation of protodesstannylated, hydroxylated, methoxylated, and dimeric side products. Notably, the methoxy-substituted analogue was identified as the major chemical impurity. Systematic variation of fluoride preprocessing conditions and precursor structure demonstrated that both residual methanol and trimethylstannyl leaving groups contribute to methoxylation. Replacement of methanol by n -butanol during fluoride processing, combined with a tri( n -butyl)stannane precursor, dramatically improved chemical purity. Beyond [¹⁸F]SynVesT-1, these findings underscore the critical importance of thoroughly investigating the influence of all reaction parameters on the impurity profile in CMRF-based radiopharmaceutical production.

papers.title: A Three-Dimensional A-D-A Structured, [2.2]Paracyclophane Linked Organoboron Complex Displays Masked Dual Fluorescence and Solvatofluorochromism
papers.abstract: We synthesized and studied an organoboron complex which has a three-dimensional A–D–A structure, 2BF 2 , and is composed of two dihydrodioxaborinine ring moieties linked by [2.2]paracyclophane. In solution, 2BF 2 exhibits dual fluorescence, with one band displaying solvatofluorochromism and the other not. Theoretical calculations revealed that the dual fluorescence of 2BF 2 derives from coexsistence of centrosymmetric and non-centrosymmetric conformers in the excited singlet state, which exhibit contrastingly emission behaviors owing to their different symmetry characteristics and dipole moments.

papers.title: Steric and Electronic Effects Govern Electron Transfer Rates in Pyridinium Electrolytes
Nonlinear shear and extensional rheology of telechelic metallosupramolecular networks
papers.abstract: The nonlinear viscoelastic response of telechelic metallosupramolecular polymer networks in the melt state is investigated under start-up shear and uniaxial elongation. Networks are formed from well-defined poly( n -butyl acrylate) (P n BA) star precursors with varying molecular spans (unentangled, barely entangled, and well-entangled) and metal-ligand bond strength (Zn²⁺, Cu²⁺, and mixtures). Linear viscoelastic properties are quantitatively described using the Rouse model for short stars and a tube-based time-marching algorithm for entangled stars. In start-up shear, densely crosslinked networks exhibit pronounced shear hardening, with the transient viscosity η⁺(t) increasing well above the linear viscoelastic envelope before reaching a maximum when stickers start dissociating. For these systems, a strong failure of the Cox-Merz rule is observed, in contrast to networks based on entangled precursors. In shear, the strain at the stress overshoot, 𝛾 max , is found to be independent of shear rate when sticker exchange is slow relative to deformation, indicating strain-controlled bond dissociation and an effective nonlinear sticker lifetime scaling as 𝜏 sticker,NLVE ≈ 𝛾 max /(d𝛾/dt). The maximum stretching ratio is a key parameter to rationalize transient behavior in both shear (𝜆 max ≈ 𝑁 strand 1/2 ) and elongation (𝜖 H,max ≈ ln 𝑁 strand 1/2 ). Entanglements introduce additional dissipation through chain sliding, reducing strain hardening and enhancing network toughness.

papers.title: Optimized xanthenium photocages with fused ring systems for photoactivated chemotherapy and GPCR photopharmacology
papers.abstract: Photocages are light-responsive chemical protecting groups that enable the controlled release of bioactive molecules. As the need for precise spatiotemporal manipulation in increasingly complex systems continues to grow, the development of novel photocage scaffolds remains essential. Herein, we show how the structural and electronic properties of xanthenium photocages determine their ground state stability. Based on rational design, we introduce their next generation built on the julolidine auxochrome, resulting in ultra efficient, green to red light activatable photocages, X590 and X600H. X590 was applied in the light-controlled delivery of a potent tubulin inhibitor, monomethyl auristatin E (MMAE) and a topoisomerase inhibitor (SN38) with low light doses above 600 nm. The light activatable prodrugs possess excellent photoindices both in 2D cell cultures and 3D tumor spheroids and show anti-tumor effects in the chorioallantoic membrane (CAM) assay in live chicken embryos. The versatility of this new scaffold was demonstrated using a caged agonist for the light activation of serotonin 2C G protein-coupled receptor. Overall, these photocages should find wide applications in photopharmacology and the detailed studies presented herein could contribute to the clinical translation of photoactivated chemotherapy.

papers.title: The Future of Epigenetics: Emerging Technologies and Clinical Applications
papers.abstract: Epigenetics, the study of heritable changes in gene expression that do not involve alterations to the DNA sequence, has emerged as a transformative field in biology and medicine, revealing how gene expression is modulated in response to internal and external cues. Its applications span from understanding fundamental biological processes and disease mechanisms to developing novel diagnostics and therapies, making it a cornerstone of modern biomedical research. This report explores data from the CAS Content Collection to examine recent transformative advances in epigenetic research, highlighting technological innovations that are revolutionizing our understanding of gene regulation and therapeutic applications. Environmental epigenetics research shows strong research interest, demonstrating how external factors induce heritable epigenetic changes with implications for transgenerational inheritance. These findings bridge environmental exposures with health outcomes across generations, informing public health strategies and personalized medicine approaches. Disease applications span multiple pathologies, with cancer research leading epigenetic studies. Emerging applications in aging research, metabolic diseases, and autoimmune conditions demonstrate the field's expanding clinical relevance. Clinical translation has achieved significant success, with 13 FDA-approved epigenetic drugs primarily targeting hematological malignancies through HDAC inhibitors (6 drugs) and DNMT inhibitors (2 drugs). The robust clinical pipeline includes 37 ongoing trials across novel targets, with encouraging diversification beyond oncology into metabolic, neurological, and inflammatory disorders.

papers.title: Computer Vision Enables Monitoring and Kinetic Analysis of Structurally Diverse Carbon Monoxide Surrogates
papers.abstract: Carbon monoxide (CO) surrogates are valuable synthetic reagents that circumvent the hazards of handling CO gas directly. However, owing to the structural diversity of available surrogates, their varied triggering conditions, and the requirement for sealed reactor systems, quantitative understanding of their CO release kinetics has remained elusive. Here, we report a non-contact computer vision method for monitoring and comparing vessel-specific CO release from ten structurally diverse surrogates in twochamber COware reactors. By tracking the colorimetric response of a ruthenium-based chemosensor, we establish a scoring system based on cumulative CO flux-from surrogate activation through gas-phase mass transfer to sensor capture-benchmarked against a CO balloon reference. This approach reveals a four-fold range in surrogate reactivity scores and enables systematic investigation of how reaction parameters such as base strength, solvent polarity, and stirring rate modulate CO release kinetics. We demonstrate that these kinetic differences translate directly to carbonylation reaction 1 outcomes: in Pd-catalyzed Suzuki-Miyaura carbonylation, surrogate score correlates linearly with product conversion, consistent with an inverse dependence on CO concentration. The methods presented enable rational surrogate selection and open new possibilities for the quantitative design of synthetic methodologies dependent on controlled gas release.

papers.title: Natural Language Control of Computational Chemistry Software « DataWarrior » Through Macro Orchestration
papers.abstract: We present a tool that enables users to control the DataWarrior cheminformatics platform using natural language commands. DataWarrior is a powerful open-source tool for computational chemistry, but mastering its graphical interface to execute operations requires time and expertise, making it sometimes difficult for non-experts to leverage its full potential. Our solution employs specialized AI agents powered by Large Language Models (LLMs) that interact with DataWarrior's built-in macro system (automation scripts) through Model Context Protocol (MCP). These AI agents understand user requests, select appropriate macros, modify their parameters and execute them accurately to bridge the gap between what users want to do and how the software executes it. Beyond workflow automation, the system enables users to query their datasets directly through natural language, asking analytical questions and receiving grounded responses based on actual data values. The system works with both open-source models that can be installed locally on the user's machine (such as LLaMA 3.1 via Ollama) and cloud-based services (GPT, Claude), making it accessible and flexible. The system currently implements conversational dataset querying and core cheminformatics operations including descriptor calculation, filtering, column deletion, and visualization, with ongoing work to integrate DataWarrior's complete catalog of capabilities.

papers.title: Boron-mediated synthesis of phthalides
Red-Light Photoredox C-H Alkylation Enabled by Catalytic NADH
papers.abstract: NADH is an essential redox mediator in biology and biocatalysis, yet its catalytic use in non-enzymatic synthetic chemistry remains essentially unknown. Here we show that NADH can act as substoichiometric reductive-quencher in red-light photoredox catalysis, enabling a redox-neutral C(sp 2 )-H alkylation of heterocycles. This strategy avoids stoichiometric waste and leads to excellent yields and selectivity by suppressing overreduction. The reaction proceeds in air under mild, aqueous-compatible conditions and operates in complex biological media, establishing NADH as cofactor for artificial red-light photoredox catalysis under potentially biocompatible conditions.

papers.title: Energetics of Non-covalent Interactions of Protein-Ligand Complexes for Drug Discovery
papers.abstract: Accurate modeling of non-covalent protein-ligand interactions is critical for applications such as enzyme engineering and drug discovery. Here, we present a dataset of 14,905 protein-ligand interaction energies using experimental structures derived from HiQBind, a high-quality protein-ligand structural database, and subsequently fragmented into dimer configurations that are classified into non-covalent interaction (NCI) types-including hydrogen bonds, hydrophobic contacts, halogen bonds, salt bridges, cation-π, and π − π interactions. Each NCI category was further evaluated with energy decomposition analysis (EDA) as a powerful framework to partition total protein-ligand energies into physically meaningful NCI components for electrostatics, Pauli repulsion, dispersion, polarization, and charge transfer. We further use this data to benchmark the performance of current classical force fields, and current state of the art machine learned interaction potential (MLIP). Together, this dataset provides a quantitative quantum mechanical survey of protein-ligand energetics, offering new insights into the molecular origins of protein-ligand NCIs to inform drug design, and establishing benchmarks for next-generation force field and MLIP development.

papers.title: Circularly Polarised Luminescence (CPL) as a Contingency Assay for 'Mirror Life' Bio-Hazards
papers.abstract: Life on Earth is predominately based upon a single chirality set, but so-called “mirror life” - speculated life of the opposite chirality, either of artificial or natural origin - presents a low-likelihood, but high severity global biosecurity threat. Such an existential risk necessitates that technologies for surveillance and containment of mirror life are developed as a contingency. In this perspective, we propose a method for screening against mirror life hazards via an optical chirality assay, based upon circularly polarized luminescence (CPL) generated either via achiral fluorophores (via supramolecular chirality effects) or intrinsically chiral molecular probes. When bound to biological molecules, CPL-generating probes enable Enantioselective Differential Chiral Contrast (EDCC) imaging to verify chirality of a biological specimen. We set out why a multi-reporter panel approach – incorporating many CPL generating fluorescent/luminescent complexes – in conjunction with testing on conventional life’s chirality set, would be necessary to avoid false positives, and thereby screen against mirror life with a high degree of confidence. The all-optical approach could be deployed via recently innovated optical technologies, i.e. rapid CPL spectroscopy, CPL EDCC microscopes, and CPL EDCC cameras. We envisage that this CPL-based approach to screening against mirror life could be a useful tool for safeguarding against mirror life biohazards in a complimentary manner to any future legislative controls.

papers.title: Circularly Polarised Luminescence (CPL) as a Contingency Assay for 'Mirror Life' Bio-Hazards
papers.abstract: Life on Earth is predominately based upon a single chirality set, but so called "mirror life"-speculated life of the opposite chirality, either of artificial or natural origin-presents a low-likelihood, but high severity global biosecurity threat. Such an existential risk necessitates that technologies for surveillance and containment of mirror life are developed as a contingency. In this perspective, we propose screening against mirror life hazards via an optical-readout chirality assay, based upon circularly polarized luminescence (CPL) generated either via achiral fluorophores (via supramolecular chirality effects) or intrinsically chiral molecular probes. Such systems enable Enantioselective Differential Chiral Contrast (EDCC) imaging. We set out why a multi-reporter panel approach incorporating many CPL generating fluorescent/luminescent complexes-in conjunction with testing on conventional chirality life, would be necessary to avoid false positives, and thereby screen against mirror life with a high degree of confidence. The all-optical approach could be deployed via recently innovated CPL/EDCC optical technologies, i.e. CPL/EDCC rapid spectroscopy, microscopy, and cameras. CPL/EDCC microscopy could enable identification of even a single mirror life cell, whereas CPL/EDCC cameras could be used for in situ inspection. We envisage that this CPL-based approach to identifying mirror life would be complimentary to speculated future international legislation against mirror life research.

papers.title: WITHDRAWN
papers.abstract: Withdrawn at the author’s request because it contained confidential information.

papers.title: Prediction of aluminium distributions in zeolites using basin-hopping and machine learning potentials
papers.abstract: In this work, we present a systematic approach to predicting the structures of three sodiated aluminosilicate zeolites (Chabazite, Mordenite and RHO) by combining a state-of-the-art neural network potential with a custom basin-hopping algorithm. We show that the lowest energy, thermally accessible configurations are rare in comparison to the number of possible structures, accounting for a few percent of viable structures. For Chabazite and Mordenite, it is found that there is a tendency for aluminium to preferentially aggregate with 2 or 3 silicon atoms separating aluminium atoms with a strong disincentive to form Al-O-Si-O-Al linkages. However, clear and contrary topological preferences are observed in RHO where Al-O-Si-O-Al linkages are strongly favoured at moderate Al concentrations. Crucially, randomly generated or non-basin hopping approaches to structure generation results in configurations that are highly metastable and activated with respect to minimum energy structures. Using such activated structures for modelling catalysis processes could potentially yield qualitatively incorrect predictions of reactivity and transport properties.

papers.title: AEP-Net: Angle-aware Electrostatic Potential Point Network for Molecular Property Prediction
papers.abstract: Molecular representation learning is a fundamental task in computational chemistry and drug discovery. While graph neural networks (GNNs) have significantly advanced molecular representation learning, they rely solely on conventional molecular graph, inherently failing to capture critical three-dimensional electronic structure, which are crucial determinants of molecular interactions. To address this, we propose the Angle-aware Electrostatic Potential point Network (AEP-Net), a novel paradigm that explicitly integrates high-resolution 3D Electrostatic Potential (ESP) represented as point clouds. AEP-Net represents molecules as collections of Atomic-centered Electrostatic-potential Subgraphs (AES). We design an angle-aware convolution mechanism that explicitly captures 3D spatial geometric features through learnable directional bases. Each AES processes its internal ESP points via a field-aware interaction layer, employing a triple weighting mechanism based on angular similarity, spatial proximity, and electrostatic values to capture fine-grained local electrostatic patterns. Features from different AESs are aggregated at the atomic level through global pooling, preserving the integrity of the local ESP environment while enabling a scalable architecture. Subsequently, a hierarchical hybrid network deeply integrates multi-scale features at the point cloud, atomic, and molecular levels,

papers.title: Reductive Disproportionation of CO2 Beyond Redox Limits Enabled by Lewis Acid-Coupled Electron Transfer
papers.abstract: A frustrated redox triad comprising Al(C 6 F 5 ) 3 ( Al CF ), CO 2 , and decamethylferrocene (FeCp* 2 ) promotes reductive disproportionation of CO 2 to CO and carbonate under ambient conditions. Spectroscopic and computational data show that a Lewis acid-bound CO 2 adduct undergoes outer-sphere Lewis Acid-Coupled Electron Transfer (LACET) with FeCp* 2 , resulting in the formation of electron donor-acceptor complex [FeCp* 2 ] + [ Al CF (μ-CO 2 •- ) Al CF ] featuring a coordinated CO 2 radical anion motif. The latter evolves into [(Fe IV )(Cp*)(C 5 Me 5 CO 2 -( Al CF ) 2 ] ( 1 ) through a CC bond forming event that sets a Cp*-bound carboxylate fragment. Isotopic labeling studies establish that intermediate 1 can be further reduced with another equivalent of CO 2 and FeCp* 2 to trigger CO 2 disproportionation. Remarkably, the redox potential of FeCp* 2 (-0.59 V vs. Fc +/0 , Fc = ferrocene) lies far above those usually required for this process. This suggests that LACET could be a strategy for energy-efficient chemical processes.

papers.title: Quantum Chemical Insight into Electrochemical Upgrading of Bio-oil
papers.abstract: Bio-oil derived from lignocellulosic biomass represents a sustainable alternative to fossil fuels as an energy source and chemical feedstock. Fast pyrolysis of lignocellulosic biomass yields a rich mixture of oxygenated organic species with low energy density and low stability, which can be electrochemically upgraded to increase energy density and stability and produce value- added chemicals. Here, we focus on electrocatalytic hydrotreatment of furfural (FF) and 4-propylphenol (4-PP), two constituents of raw bio-oil. In a binary mixture, the presence of FF has been shown to inhibit the reduction of 4-PP. The underlying mechanisms of these competing reactions are probed using density functional theory (DFT) and experimental electrochemical deposition techniques. The binding energies of FF and 4-PP, as well as their respective reduction products and associated reaction thermodynamics, are examined comparatively on multiple facets of single-crystal platinum and ruthenium catalysts. FF is shown to bind competitively compared to 4-PP, particularly on Pt(111) and Ru(0001), and hydrogenation products such as tetrahydrofurfuryl alcohol (THFA) and 4-propylcyclohexanol (4-PCOL) were found to bind less strongly to the surfaces than the reactants. FF reduction side products, including dimers furoin (FUI) and hydrofuroin (HF), were also found to bind competitively with 4-PP. No thermodynamic barriers were observed for FF hydrogenation to THFA, whereas 4-PCOL formation is favored on Pt facets, and propylcyclohexane (PC) formation is favored on Ru. The presence of barriers to 4-PP hydrogenation indicates that FF hydrogenation is thermodynamically favored on Pt and Ru. Further, limiting potential calculations suggests that the FF reduction pathways are generally favorable around 0 V vs. RHE. In contrast, the 4-PP reduction pathways require a more cathodic bias, achieved at potentials less than -0.1 V vs. RHE. Adsorption behavior of FF-derived reduction products on polycrystalline Pt is experimentally validated using a Quartz Crystal Microbalance (QCM). Such experiments yield estimates of aqueous-phase free energies of adsorption, which are correlated with the gas phase for comparison with computational results. Overall, the DFT model results suggest that the observed inhibition of 4-PP by FF is due to competitive adsorption and favorable FF reaction thermodynamics.

papers.title: Towards a new era for open and FAIR data in catalysis research – A catalysis plugin for NOMAD
papers.abstract: The field of catalysis currently lacks a structured repository for experimental data, and the publication of machine-readable datasets remains uncommon. To address this gap and support FAIR (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, and Reusable) data principles, we introduce a new plugin within the NOMAD platform for managing and publishing heterogeneous catalysis data, the nomad_catalysis plugin. This plugin enables the upload of structured experimental data and metadata with built-in visualization and alignment to the community-developed vocabulary Voc4Cat, ensuring long-term interpretability. In addition to facilitating efficient data sharing, the catalysis app offers intuitive search functionality, enabling researchers to quickly identify relevant catalytic reactions, catalyst materials, reaction conditions and kinetic properties. This infrastructure lays the foundation for advanced data analytics and machine learning applications, supporting more efficient and reproducible catalyst development.

papers.title: Optical Properties of New Donor–Acceptor Dyes for RNA Imaging: Insights from Ab Initio and Hückel’s Model Calculations
papers.abstract: Optical properties of 11 donor–acceptor dyes based on pyridinium–indole, pyridinium–indolizine, isoquinolinium–indole, and isoquinolinium–indolizine motifs developed for RNA imaging are investigated using high-level quantum chemistry methods and semi-empirical Hückel’s model. The goal of this study is three-fold: (i) to develop and benchmark computational protocols that can be used for computational design and screening of novel dyes; (ii) to explain the trends in optical properties of the model dyes in terms of underlying charge distributions and connectivity; (iii) to propose a strategy for tuning their optical properties by structural modiﬁcations. We also present the results for a new dye designed to have red-shifted absorption and emission.

papers.title: Cost-Effective Solid-state NMR of Fungal Glucans: A case study on Schizosaccharomyces pombe
papers.abstract: Solid-state NMR provides molecular-level insights into fungal cell walls, but full 13C-enrichment is costly and limits biological replication. Here, we show that 10% 13C-glucose labelling in Schizosaccharomyces pombe is sufficient to resolve the major carbohydrate resonances and quantify glucan composition with high reproducibility. We then examined cell wall composition at two temperatures, both in whole cells and in extracted wall fractions. Interestingly, whole cell spectra indicated minor, non-significant changes with temperature, while extracted walls revealed differences between the rigid glucan matrices with beta-1,3-glucan especially enriched at 36°C. Together, these results establish low-level 13C labelling as a cost-effective strategy for fungal solid-state NMR and highlight the complementary strengths of whole cell and extracted wall-level analysis in uncovering how the effect of elevated temperature is encoded in cell wall architecture.

papers.title: Orthogonal Solvent Mediation for Solid Composite Electrolyte Synthesis: Phase Integration via Particle Dispersion
papers.abstract: Ceramic-rich solid-composite electrolytes exhibit ceramic-like ionic conductivity and enhanced mechanical property, making them promising candidates for market-relevant solid-state batteries. In-depth knowledge of the microstructure within the composite electrolytes for ideal performances and their correlation with the choice of materials and processing methods are not well-understood. Herein, we report a solution-cast, free-standing composite film comprised of well-integrated ceramic (Li3InCl¬6) and binder (Styrene-Ethylene-Butylene-Styrene, SEBS) phase, which simultaneously provides Li+ transport pathways and the required mechanical support. In the formation of this unique microstructure, we mark the mediator role of dibutyl ether – a low polarity solvent that forms a non-invasive polar-ionic interaction with the electronegative metal elements at the surface of Li3InCl¬6 particles to suspend and disperse Li3InCl6 particles in the dissolved SEBS matrix, facilitating phase integration. This weak interaction only occurs at chosen conditions; increased solvent-to-ceramic ratio and interaction time can induce Li3InCl6 decomposition. Our results correlate the electrochemical performance of a ceramic-rich Li3InCl6-SEBS composite electrolyte film with its microstructure; the latter was demonstrated to be potentially tunable by altering the molecular structure of the solvent and the parameters used in composite electrolyte synthesis procedures. This work provides materials structural-level insights that underpin the design principle of solution-cast solid composite electrolytes.

papers.title: A Brønsted Acid-Base Approach for the Monoselective C-F Substitution of (Trifluoromethyl)alkanes
papers.abstract: We disclose a method for the net coupling of nucleophiles with a single C-F bond of unactivated (trifluoromethyl)alkanes. The process occurs via an initial base-promoted dehydrofluorination/defluorinative nucleophilic addition cascade to generate vinylfluoride intermediates that undergo a rapid hydrofluorination second step to yield gem -difluorinated products. Thus, the aliphatic-CF 3 group of commercial building blocks and complex medicinal compounds can now be transformed into numerous classes of valuable α,α-difluoro(thio)ether substructures in an efficient and modular manner.

papers.title: Unanticipated Enhancement to Phosphide Nucleophilicity in Dimethyl Sulfoxide for Advanced Catalytic P-C Bond Formation Reactions
papers.abstract: An exceptional nucleophilicity of phosphide (R2P-) was discovered for reactions conducted in dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) and leveraged for catalytic P-C bond formation. A range of simple bases affect this reactivity, and sodium hydroxide was chosen for deeper analysis due to its simplicity and abundance. This enhanced reactivity is not solely due to the high dielectric constant of DMSO or super base formation, rather aspects of phosphine association, proton management, and solubility drive the enhanced reactivity, based on comparison between solvents and spectroscopic analysis. The impact of this enhanced reactivity is substantial. Ring-opening reactions of epoxide and cyclopropane substrates are possible under catalytic conditions at ambient temperature. Likewise, hydrophosphination of a sweeping range of alkene and alkyne substrates is accessible at ambient temperature. To further demonstrate the utility of this simple, inexpensive, and water-tolerant catalysis, the catalytic preparation of phosphonium salts was also demonstrated. Despite tremendous advances in s-block catalysts, the hydroxide/DMSO combination provides the greatest combination of activation and versatility of any known P-C bond forming catalyst.

papers.title: HYDRA: Hybrid Multimodal AI-driven Design for Robust High-Entropy Oxide Electrocatalysts in ORR
papers.abstract: The oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) is critical for electrochemical energy devices, yet its slow kinetics and the high cost of platinum-group metal catalysts necessitate alternative materials. High-entropy oxides (HEOs) show immense potential, but their vast design space challenges traditional discovery. This study introduces HYDRA, a Hybrid Multimodal AI-driven Design platform, to accelerate HEO catalyst discovery through intelligent design and cross-modal validation. HYDRA comprises four synergistic modules: a multi-graph neural network for accurate ORR performance prediction, a large language model for extracting synthesizability knowledge and generating protocols, a multi-objective evolutionary algorithm for optimization and design insights, and a neural network for microstructural validation. Our results demonstrate that HY-DRA's predictive model significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in estimating ORR half-wave potential and stability. Ablation studies confirm the critical contributions of multi-scale structural information and defect descriptors. The large language model generates highly feasible and novel synthesis protocols. A successful end-to-end case study, where a HYDRA-designed HEO was synthesized and experimentally validated with high agreement, coupled with precise microstructural confirmation, underscores the framework's robustness. HYDRA thus provides a powerful, interpretable, and practically validated approach to overcome conventional HEO catalyst discovery limitations, accelerating the development of next-generation ORR electrocatalysts.

papers.title: Comprehensive Near Edge X-ray Absorption Fine Structure Analysis of Corrosion in Iron at the Nanoscale
papers.abstract: Corrosion continues to be a major global challenge representing 3% of the GDP of industrialized nations. However, there are still many unanswered scientific and technical questions about the corrosion process and the corrosion products that iron forms. It is not clear which of the many iron oxides, hydroxide and oxyhydroxides form as a scale, particularly under the many different environmental conditions that corrosion can occur under. This is partly due to, for example, similarities in the crystal structures, such that even diffraction cannot resolve them all easily. In this work, we illustrate the use of Near Edge X-ray Absorption Fine Structure in conjunction with high resolution Scanning Transmission X-ray Microscopy to characterize iron corrosion scales at the nanoscale and identify the formation of several coexisting iron phases. Importantly, these phases include magnetite, a ferrimagnetic material. Hence, we briefly consider the use of X-ray magnetic circular dichroism to provide additional magnetic contrast as a further means of resolving the possible iron phases and possible enhancements for subsequent experiments.

papers.title: Structural Signatures of the Hydrophobic Crossover Observed for Hydrated Anthracene
Shining a Light on the Photochemistry of Tetraaryl[3]cumulene-Based Metal-Organic Frameworks
papers.abstract: Achieving bright and long-lived emission with π-conjugated organic chromophores in the solid state presents a significant challenge but also an opportunity for applications ranging from nanoscale electronics to heterogeneous photocatalysis. Tetraryl[n]cumulenes, organic molecules consisting of three or more cumulative double bonds, are highly modular systems with tunable redox and optoelectronic properties, yet their utility remains limited due to rapid quenching from aryl group planarization or excimer formation. Herein, we demonstrate that the incorporation of a tetraryl[3]cumulene-based organic linker within the metal-organic framework (MOF) CORN-MOF-9 (CORN = Cornell University) suppresses these quenching pathways, allowing for bright and long-lived emission. Extensive transient absorption (TA) and photoluminescence (PL) spectroscopic studies support the unique properties of the MOF and also confirm it exhibits spectral diffusion, leading to red-shifted steady-state emission compared to molecular analogs in solution. Overall, our findings represent a new avenue to unlock the promising photochemical properties of cumulenes within materials platforms, paving the way for their use in various applications. Introduction.

papers.title: Alkaline Mineralization of Aryl Trifluoromethyl Groups Near Benzylic N-Heterocycles
papers.abstract: We report complete defluorination of trifluoromethyl arenes bearing an ortho N-heterocycle group upon reaction with potassium tert-butoxide; the trifluoromethyl group is converted to the corresponding t-Bu ester. This transformation uses readily available reagents at ambient temperature and is operationally simple. We have demonstrated 14 successful examples of defluorination, with up to 85% yield. Our findings should inform synthetic route design for targets that contain these functional groups. Moreover, our findings suggest that similar compounds containing aryl trifluoromethyl groups can be defluorinated into inorganic fluoride.

papers.title: Accurate and robust prediction of polymer glass transition temperature using neural network charges and unsupervised machine learning
papers.abstract: Accurate computational modeling of the glass transition is a longstanding challenge in polymer chemistry. Atomistic molecular dynamics simulations offer a powerful approach to observe the changes in viscoelasticity, density and chain mobility associated with the glass transition, yet they often overestimate the glass transition temperature (T g ) and have limited sensitivity to number average molecular weight and dispersity. These deficiencies are largely attributed to high levels of noise in simulation data masking the T g , inaccurate polymer representations, and limited force field transferability. In this study, we build a robust and automated workflow to calculate T g using unsupervised machine learning, and apply it to a range of polymer models and dispersities. We show that our workflow provides improved T g estimates when compared to other established, 'bulk' measurements (e.g., monitoring changes in RMSD or density). We also benchmark different neural network charge models, which streamline polymer force field parameterization, and assess their influence on the T g .

papers.title: Structure-Activity Relationship Study of Anti-Cryptosporidium Benzoxaboroles Yields Enhanced Potency and Curative Efficacy
papers.abstract: Cryptosporidiosis is a major cause of life-threatening diarrhea in children and chronic diarrhea in immunocompromised individuals. Despite the prevalence and burden of Cryptosporidium spp., only a handful of clinical and preclinical candidates have been identified during the last decade. Our previous work identified pyrazolo[3,4-d]pyrimidine benzoxaborole ( 2 ; EC 50 = 0.19 µM) as an orally efficacious inhibitor of Cryptosporidium with a downside of relapse after 7-days post drug treatment. Here we report a structure-activity relationship study around the benzoxaborole ring of compound 2 resulting in rac- 11 with > 7-fold improved in vitro potency (EC 50 = 0.025 µM). Remarkably, rac- 11 is non cytotoxic and displayed curative in vivo efficacy in Cryptosporidium infected immunocompromised NSG mice. Furthermore, resolution of rac- 11 into its enantiomers demonstrated that one enantiomer is approximately twofold more potent ( ent2- 11 ; EC 50 = 0.011 µM), whereas the other is roughly 400-fold less potent, indicating the role of orientation of the methyl group at the C3-position of benzoxaborole. The ent2- 11 also had significantly reduced adverse binding to hPDE5 compared to 2 . Collectively, these findings advance new and effective candidates for the treatment of cryptosporidiosis.

papers.title: Foam-to-Foam Recycling of Non-Isocyanate Polyurethane Foams via Complete Revalorization of Depolymerization Products
papers.abstract: Polyurethane foams have been widely used in industry for decades, yet their toxic precursors and limited recycling pathways remain major challenges in polymer science. Non-isocyanate polyurethanes (NIPUs) mitigate toxicity concerns but lack viable foam-to-foam recycling pathways. Here, we demonstrate a solvent-free chemical recycling route for CO₂-based NIPU foams, where glycerol depolymerizes poly(hydroxyurethane) networks into diol-rich fragments that are subsequently cyclocarbonated into reusable five-membered cyclic carbonates (re-5CC). Integration of both steps into a one-pot process reduces waste, eliminates intermediate purification, and increases monomer yield (>71%) compared to conventional routes. The resulting re-5CC species enable second-generation foams with up to 100% recycled content, offering a closed-loop, low-waste strategy for viable foam-to-foam NIPU production.

papers.title: DM-NMR: A universal model for non-uniform sampling reconstruction of NMR spectra
papers.abstract: Multidimensional nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) is a widely utilized technique for protein studies of structures, dynamics, and interactions, providing crucial atomic-level insight. Non-uniform sampling (NUS) technology is an effective approach to greatly reduce sampling time, and advanced reconstruction algorithms is needed to obtain high-quality NMR spectra. Traditional algorithms require manual parameter tuning, often leading to suboptimal results. The emergence of deep learning (DL) provides a new approach for reconstruction. However, when the sampling scheme or sampling rate employed in experimental settings differs substantially from those represented in the training data, existing DL models must be retrained to preserve performance, which severely limits their general applicability. Here, a diffusion-based model for NMR non-uniform sampling reconstruction, referred to as DM-NMR, is proposed. By learning the characteristics of fully sampled data in the frequency domain and incorporating time domain low-rank constraints during reconstruction, compared to current state-of-art both traditional and DL methods, DM-NMR achieves superior reconstruction performance across various sampling rates and sampling schemes.

papers.title: Scalable Modeling of Multi-Spin Ensembles in SABRE Hyperpolarization: A Symmetry-Based Framework for Zero and Ultralow Fields
papers.abstract: This work presents a theoretical framework for quantitative, scalable modeling of SABRE (Signal Amplification by Reversible Exchange) experiments under zero-and ultralow-field (ZULF) conditions. SABRE exploits the singlet spin order of parahydrogen to hyperpolarize nuclear spins of substrates without chemical modification, enhancing NMR signals. In ZULF SABRE method polarization transfer occurs in ultralow magnetic fields where Zeeman interactions are comparable to or weaker than scalar couplings, enabling coherent mixing of spin states and revealing interactions often suppressed at high fields. Our approach captures the full quantum dynamics of the SABRE complex, including coherent evolution, chemical exchange, and relaxation, within a Liouville-space formalism. We demonstrate that the Hamiltonian, relaxation, and exchange superoperators possess symmetry with respect to the z-projection of the total spin, allowing the dynamics to be rigorously restricted to the zero-quantum coherence subspace. This symmetry-based reduction yields a scalable framework for efficient simulation of multi-spin SABRE systems. The approach is validated against full Liouvillespace calculations for small systems and is further applied to a 14-spin SABRE complex, demonstrating its ability to treat spin systems of a complexity well beyond the reach of conventional full Liouville-space simulations. The framework thus provides a predictive tool for optimal polarization fields, ZULF NMR spectra and the design of novel hyperpolarization experiments.

papers.title: Catalysis for Sustainability: Materials, Methods, and Metrics for a Carbon-Neutral Future
papers.abstract: Catalysis underpins 90% of chemical manufacturing processes, yet the environmental footprint of catalyst production, operation, and disposal remains largely overlooked. This report examines sustainable catalyst design principles through lifecycle analysis, emphasizing earth-abundant materials, low-energy synthesis methods, extended operational lifetimes, regeneration strategies, and endof-life recyclability. Single-atom catalysts (SACs) emerge as transformative materials, achieving nearly 100% metal utilization while enabling reaction pathways at significantly reduced temperatures and pressures. Using ammonia synthesis as a case study-a process consuming 1.5% of global energy and generating 450 million tonnes CO2 annually-we demonstrate how sustainable catalysis can reduce production energy by 65%, extend catalyst lifetimes by 50%, and enable distributed chemical manufacturing compatible with renewable energy systems. Green synthesis routes (hydrothermal, sol-gel, mechanochemical) reduce catalyst production emissions by 60-80% compared to traditional high-temperature methods. Comprehensive sustainability metrics beyond conventional activity and selectivity are proposed, incorporating synthesis energy, turnover number, deactivation rate, regeneration efficiency, atom utilization, embodied carbon, and recyclability. Implementation of these principles across the global chemical industry could avoid 300-400 million tonnes CO2 annually while reducing manufacturing costs, demonstrating that environmental sustainability and economic viability are complementary objectives in catalyst innovation.

papers.title: Do Mutations in Mycobacterial ATP Synthase Undermine Bedaquiline Binding? Insights from Multiscale Molecular Simulations
papers.abstract: Tuberculosis (TB), caused by the bacterium Mycobacterium tuberculosis (MTB), remains a major global health problem. Current antitubercular drugs, used for the treatment of TB, pose a significant challenge in treating Multidrug-resistant (MDR) and extensively drug-resistant (XDR) TB. The recently developed drug Bedaquiline (BDQ) is used for MDR-TB and works by inhibiting the rotation of the ATP synthase enzyme, disrupting energy production, ultimately leading to bacterial cell death. BDQ binds to multiple sites within the ATP synthase, including the lagging, leading, and c-only sites; however, resistance has emerged due to mutations in the enzyme, and the underlying molecular mechanisms remain unclear. In this study, we performed all-atom molecular dynamics, umbrella sampling, and random accelerated molecular dynamics simulations to investigate the structural and energetic effects of clinically relevant mutations associated with BDQ resistance. The total binding free energies of BDQ estimated in wild-type (WT), E61D, and A63P mutants were -47.90, -38.90, and -37.12 kcal/mol, respectively, indicating that single-point mutations can reduce the total binding free energy by at least 9 kcal/mol, with the E61D and A63P mutants exhibiting the greatest loss of binding affinity for BDQ. Umbrella sampling further indicated that D28G and A63P mutants significantly lower the free-energy barrier compared to WT. Residence-time analyses further identify D28G, E61D, and A63P as key mutations that markedly reduce BDQ efficacy. Overall, these computational studies provide molecular-level insights into the mechanisms of BDQ resistance, which can aid in the design of novel inhibitors for MDR-TB treatment.

papers.title: Paving the Way Towards a Compact Complete Chiroptical Toolbox
papers.abstract: Circularly polarised luminescence (CPL) spectroscopy is a technique with applications in materials chemistry, bioimaging, probing fundamental chirality, but conventional photo-elastic modulator CPL instruments remain bulky, expensive and slow. We report a compact single-channel CPL (SC-CPL) spectrometer that alternates left-and righthanded emission through a piezo-actuated pair of orthogonally aligned achromatic quarter-wave plates using a rapid CCD detector. This design minimises moving optics and eliminates the need for detector matching and pre-calibration. It can operate in various acquisition modes such as time gated acquisition mode for long-lived CPL emission and a quasi-continuous mode for short-lived CPL emission. Validation against a benchmark PEM-CPL system using a range of CPL emitters reproduced fine CPL resolution with high sensitivity, orders of magnitude faster. This blueprint SC-CPL reported herein paves the way towards the world's first complete compact chiroptical toolbox. This could lead to significant advancements with pivotal scientific and societal impact.

papers.title: Polymer-Coated Titanium Dioxide Nanoparticles with Enhanced Antimicrobial Activity: Mechanistic Insights into Particle-Membrane Interactions
Radical Deoxygenation of Alcohols via Visible Light Irradiation of a Titanium Porphyrin Catalyst
papers.abstract: Alcohols are ubiquitous motifs in organic molecules that can be employed as radical precursors, usually activated through a two-step process. In this research, we present the unique ability of a titanium porphyrin complex to directly deoxygenate alcohols without pre-activation. The system generates the carbon-centered radical under mild reaction conditions, turning over the catalyst by photoexcitation with purple LEDs. To demonstrate its preliminary value, the radical intermediate can further be utilized for Giese addition and nickel-mediated crosscoupling.

papers.title: Synthesis of (2-β-nitrovinyl)phenethyl Benzoate, a Key Intermediate of Ropinirole Hydrochloride, via a One-pot Method
Zirconium Photocatalysis for Inert Bond Activation: Direct C(sp3)−H Functionalization, Decarboxylative Amination, and Polystyrene Oxidative Degradation
papers.abstract: Zirconium (Zr) is an earth-abundant, environmentally benign, and biocompatible element, yet its role in organic synthesis has historically been limited to transformations of active substrates like alkenes and alkynes. In contrast, the direct catalytic functionalization of inert yet abundant feedstocks, including alkanes, free aliphatic acids, and nonpolar polymers such as polystyrene (PS), remains a formidable challenge. Herein, we report that commercially available ZrCl 4 exhibits potent ligand-to-metal charge transfer (LMCT) reactivity under light irradiation, establishing a unified photocatalytic platform for the activation of the highly thermodynamically stable C(sp 3 )−H and C−C bonds and functionalization of these inert materials. Operating under simple “dump-and-stir” conditions at ambient temperature, the method employs low catalyst loadings to convert alkanes and aliphatic acids directly into high-value C−N, C−C, and C−S coupled products. Remarkably, the same system facilitates near-complete oxidative depolymerization of PS, predominantly yielding benzoic acid, which is a fundamental industrial building block. These findings unveil a previously unknown dimension of zirconium photochemistry, significantly expanding the synthetic versatility of this overlooked metal. Moreover, the strategy offers a general blueprint for sustainable catalysis, enabling efficient bond formation and the productive upgrading of inert feedstocks for both academic and industrial applications.

papers.title: Halide-Directed Nanostructuring of Copper Unraveled by Multivariate Analysis
papers.abstract: Nanostructuring metallic surfaces is a key strategy to tailor morphology and increase surface area, which is highly beneficial for a wide range of applications, including electrocatalysis, energy storage, and solar cells. Copper (Cu) is widely used in various electrocatalytic reactions such as the electrochemical reduction of carbon dioxide. Understanding how Cu can be effectively nanostructured to optimize the structure-activity selectivity relationships remains a significant challenge. Here, we propose a general methodology based on design of experiments (DoE) approach. We systematically evaluate the influence of experimental factors on the morphology, crystal facet distribution, and roughness of Cu electrodes in chloride-and iodide-based electrolytes. Cyclic voltammogram experiments show that the electrode roughness factor depends mainly on the potential scan rate and the number of scans. Additionally, we observed that the choice of halide (Cl - or I - ) significantly impacts the final morphology, highlighting the intrinsic relationship between Cu surface corrosion and the resulting nanostructure. We believe that this type of holistic approach to electrochemical surface nanostructuring can provide valuable guidelines for researchers across diverse fields and facilitate the design and fabrication of application-specific electrodes.

papers.title: Expanding the matrix space – modulating growth factor signals by cell instructive GAG-peptide hydrogels with customizable viscoelastic properties
papers.abstract: This project developed a predictive strategy to engineer multicomponent hydrogels that mimic key features of the extracellular matrix (ECM). We combined self‑assembling peptides with sulfated glycosaminoglycans (GAGs) which bind and present growth factors. By systematically varying the peptide sequence (aromaticity and charge) and GAG sulfation, we established rules that link molecular design to how the materials assemble, how stiff they are, and how they dissipate stress—properties that strongly affect cells. A notable discovery is that sufficiently sulfated GAGs can drive a “coil‑to‑β‑sheet” transition in weakly assembling peptides, acting as an assembly cofactor to trigger gelation and expand the tunable design space. The resulting hydrogels cover a broad, tissue‑relevant stiffness range and exhibit rapid, ECM‑like stress relaxation. We applied these materials to human hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs), which are essential for transplantation but difficult to expand outside the body. Using Design of Experiments (DoE) and regression modeling, we identified net negative matrix charge and an optimal heparin content as critical for homogeneous gels and robust HSC survival and expansion. The optimized formulation maintained primitive stem cell subsets and functional colony‑forming potential. This work provides a materials‑by‑design framework to program peptide–GAG interfaces for regenerative medicine, with potential applications in stem cell culture, organoids, and protein delivery. papers.title: Ion Beam Engineered Band Bending and Hydroxyl-Controlled Photodetection in WO₃ Thin Films
A DFT Study of LiCS molecule and application to prediction of adjusting super atomic molecular orbitals (SAMOs)
papers.abstract: Polar heteronuclear alkali-metal dimers, which can exhibit pronounced charge separation, have been studied experimentally and theoretically because of their unusual bonding and electronic properties. Recent advances in synthetic methodology have increased the feasibility of employing these species as functional components; however, their potential applications remain largely unexplored. A key bottleneck is the computational cost required to predict reliable structural and electronic properties for systems containing heavy alkali elements: high-level wave-function methods such as CCSD(T)-SF are often prohibitively expensive for screening complexes and materials. Herein, we use LiCs as a prototypical system to assess practical computational protocols by benchmarking density functional theory (DFT) calculations against ab initio references and available experimental observables. We find that the CAM-B3LYP, combined with relativistic corrections, reproduces both the equilibrium bond length within 2% error and within 5% error for dipole moment at a substantially reduced computational cost. Using this validated protocol, we investigate the LiCs–benzene complex and show that LiCs can spatially polarize benzene’s Superatom Molecular Orbitals (SAMOs) from the ring toward LiCs while avoiding significant destabilization. This behavior contrasts with that induced by a monovalent cation and by representative alkali–halide ion pairs. These results demonstrate a low-cost route to model alkali-metal dimers and suggest a strategy to regulate SAMOs using polar diatomic alkali species, opening new opportunities in molecular and materials design.

papers.title: Charge Regulation and Orientation Dictate Protein Uptake into Polyelectrolyte Brushes
papers.abstract: The phenomenon of charge regulation is of central importance in the interaction of many proteins with soft, electrically charged environments. Here, we used coarse-grained simulations to study the interaction of a globular protein-represented as a quadrupolar, charge regulating nanoparticle-with a weak polyelectrolyte brush. Our simulations show that a quadrupolar nanoparticle interacting with a brush exhibits multistep complexation, producing double reionization jumps and distinct regimes of charge regulation as the nanoparticle penetrates the brush. In particular, strong local electrostatic fields induced by direct complexation with polymer strands yield nanoparticle charge states that decidedly differ from mean-field predictions based on the local pH alone. Moreover, we show that the nanoparticle orientation becomes a key degree of freedom governing the complexation: quadrupolar symmetry leads to angular locking near the brush surface, resulting in intricate orientational complexation pathways and characteristic kinks in the free-energy. All of these features represent non-mean field coupling effects that arise from strongly localized charge clusters and cannot be described by simple multipole expansions or Poisson-Boltzmann approaches. Overall, our results highlight how higher-order charge asymmetries can profoundly influence the adsorption landscape and underscore the need to go beyond dipolar models when modeling realistic protein-brush interactions.

papers.title: Cysteine Protonation States in Copper Tracking Proteins and its Influence on Biological Cu(I) Transfer Mechanism
papers.abstract: Copper delivery from metallochaperones to P-type ATPases requires coordination by cysteine residues, yet the protonation states of these incoming thiols at the moment of first Cu(I) engagement remain undefined. The long-standing assumption that reactive cysteines exist as thiolates has not been rigorously tested under the conditions relevant to early protein-protein encounters, limiting mechanistic insight into the formation of the initial Cu(I)-S bond. In the Atx1-Ccc2a system, we assess whether the local protein environment can modulate cysteine acidity sufficiently to alter ligand protonation states and reactivity. MD simulations combined with DFT-based pKa analysis demonstrate that neither of the binding site cysteines of Ccc2a undergo substantial pKa reduction in their apo or pre-reactive states; the only perturbation occurs when Cu(I) is already in vicinity to the incoming cysteine thiol. QM/MM calculations further show that direct Cu(I)-thiol coordination is chemically feasible without prior deprotonation. We further analyze the initial Cu(I)-S bond formation within the framework of the Curtin-Hammett principle, explicitly evaluating whether rapid thiol-thiolate equilibration can govern the product distribution during early copper transfer. Our analysis reveals, thiol-thiolate interconversion is slower than Cu(I)-S ligation, indicating that early Cu(I) binding is dictated by the equilibrium population of thiol species rather than by transition-state energetics. Thus, early Cu(I) recognition is directed by transient conformational states and encounter geometries rather than by cysteine activation. These findings refine the mechanistic model of Cu(I) tracking and provide a framework for rational design of metalloprotein mimics and copper homeostasis therapies. † Equal contributions.
