This review summarizes advances in physics-based modeling of platinum dissolution and oxidation, presenting three of the most widely used frameworks: the Darling-Meyers, Holby-Morgan, and Rinaldo-Stumper-Eikerling models. These models form the conceptual foundation for many subsequent studies on platinum dissolution and oxidation, and this review examines how recent work has expanded upon these frameworks to illustrate the conceptual evolution of physics-based degradation models. Additional models proposed in the literature are also discussed as alternative approaches that represent newer and emerging directions in modeling platinum degradation. Finally, the review compares the capabilities and limitations of existing models and highlights emerging trends and potential directions for future model development. This review aims to provide a focused guide for researchers developing next-generation physics-based catalyst degradation models for PEM fuel cells.

papers.title: Bridging Bioassay-Guided Isolation and Metabolomics: Toward Hybrid Strategies in Natural Product Drug Discovery
papers.abstract: Natural products (NPs) remain an important source of drug discovery, providing approximately 32% of newly introduced small molecule drugs between 1981 to 2019. The identification and isolation of bioactive compounds from natural product presents both great opportunities and challenges even for modern pharmaceutical research. Two primary approaches have emerged as dominant methodologies: the traditional bioassay-guided isolation (BGI) and the more recent metabolomics-based discovery approaches. This comprehensive review critically compares these methodologies, including their principles, technical capabilities, strengths, limitations, and their applications in natural product discovery. While BGI has a long history as the gold standard, providing remarkable drugs such as artemisinin, paclitaxel, and vinblastine, metabolomics offers broad chemical coverage, sensitivity, and high throughput capabilities that can overcome the limitations of activity-driven approaches. To accelerate, improve the accuracy and ensure the success of natural product–based research, selecting only one of the two approaches is not advisable. This review recommends combining both approaches to leverage the strengths of each while addressing their respective limitations, thereby enhancing the success of natural product drug discovery research. In this context, metabolomics provides accurate data for compound prioritization from the phytochemical complexity of NPs, whereas BGI delivers precise data for confirming active compounds and verifying bioactivity. By adopting this hybrid method, the research timeline for natural product–based drug discovery can be accelerated and more accurate.

papers.title: Supramolecular dye polymers for aggregation-induced photocatalysis
papers.abstract: Aggregation can profoundly alter the excited-state properties of organic chromophores, yet its role in photocatalytic conversion of solar energy is typically associated with charge delocalization or exciton transport in crystalline supramolecular polymers. Here, we exploit aggregation as a strategy for rigidification of organic chromophores to activate photocatalysis by stabilizing localized excited states. Using amphiphilic distyrylanthracene derivatives, we show that aggregation in water − triggered via concentration, charge screening, or counterion exchange − enhances dye excitation and enables light-driven transformations of solar energy into storable fuels, such as hydrogen (H 2 ) and hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 ). Enhanced reactivity correlates with increased local excited-state population, underlining the role of self-assembly in restricting intramolecular motion and suppressing unproductive non-radiative decay. The counterion dependence follows a reverse Hofmeister effect, with charge diffuse anions promoting aggregation, fluorescence, and photocatalytic function. Aggregated dyes also display enhanced photostability and recyclability compared to their molecular counterparts. Photocatalysis is maximized in kinetically trapped aggregates, which outperform their thermodynamic counterparts, challenging conventional paradigm that activity is favored in extended assemblies. Finally, the approach of aggregation-induced dye rigidification for photocatalysis is validated in a structurally distinct chromophore, confirming the generality of the phenomenon. By achieving excited-state confinement and reactivity instead of charge delocalization, this work reports aggregation-induced photocatalysis (AIP) phenomena, with supramolecular packing emerging as a powerful strategy for preparing photostable, emissive, and functional organic photocatalysts in water.

papers.title: Immersion Freezing Efficiency of ZnAl2O4 and MgAl2O4 Spinels, ZnO, and MgO: The Role of Oxygen Vacancies
papers.abstract: Aerosol particles that catalyze ice nucleation alter the optical properties and precipitation cycles of clouds. Although mineral dust aerosol particles containing metal oxides are susceptible to the formation of oxygen vacancies (VO) on their surfaces, the impact of these defects on ice nucleation activity has not been addressed. To investigate the impact of VO sites, we conducted a droplet immersion freezing assay on zinc aluminate (ZnAl2O4) and magnesium aluminate (MgAl2O4) spinels annealed under air, nitrogen, and oxygen atmospheres. We observe that samples annealed under nitrogen promote ice nucleation at warmer temperatures compared to those treated in oxidizing atmospheres, with the effecting being most pronounced for ZnAl2O4. To further understand these results, we investigated the immersion freezing of zinc oxide (ZnO) and magnesium oxide (MgO). Here, we observe that ZnO nucleates ice at substantially warmer temperatures than MgO after annealing under nitrogen. We hypothesize the trends in ice nucleation activity are due to the varying concentrations of VO that form during the annealing process on the oxide surfaces, which tend to be higher in the absence of O2. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations support our hypothesis, indicating VO are more stable on the surfaces of the Zn-containing oxides. The study suggests that oxygen vacancies, which are common defects on metal oxide surfaces that affect their adsorption and catalytic properties, can influence the efficiency with which mineral dust aerosol particles activate ice formation and affect cloud radiative forcing.

papers.title: Hydrogen Bond-Controlled Site-Selective C–H Borylation at the Remote-Position of Naphthalene Derivatives
papers.abstract: We successfully developed site-selective C–H borylation at the remote position (6-position) of 1-substituted naphthalene derivatives, which was controlled by hydrogen bonding between the substrate-recognition site of the catalyst (hydrogen bond donor) and the functional group of the substrate (hydrogen bond acceptor). By changing the ligands, 7-position-selective remote C–H borylation of naphthalene derivatives with a functional group at the 2-position can also be achieved. These are the rare examples of site-selective C–H borylation at a remote position of naphthalene derivatives.

papers.title: The Effect of Inorganic Impurities in Post-Consumer Plastic Waste on the Cracking of Polyolefins with Zeolite-based Catalysts
papers.abstract: Impurities present in post-consumer plastic waste (PCPW) are a major limiting factor for the catalytic conversion of polyolefin waste into useful chemicals. While the detrimental effect of common impurities present in crude oil, like sulfur and nitrogen as well as metals and their complexes, have been studied extensively, the same cannot be said yet for impurities in PCPW. In this work, we systematically study the effects of a variety of inorganic impurities during catalytic cracking of polyolefins using ultrastable zeolite Y (US-Y) as catalyst. We have prepared model contaminated polymer materials with controlled concentration of individual impurities and tested their impact on the catalyst activity by repeated thermogravimetric analysis with progressively more contaminated catalyst material. Our findings indicate that the most critical inorganic impurities are typical zeolite poisons, e.g., alkali metal and earth-alkali metal ions. Na, K, Ca, Mg and Cu led to noticeable zeolite deactivation at 0.14 wt% loading on pristine polymer. Inert metal oxides, such as SiO2 and TiO 2 only cause deactivation at high loadings (~1 wt%) by blocking access to the zeolite surface. By contrast, cracking of S and Cl contaminated polymer did not lead to deactivation. In addition, examination of the effect of real, mixed PCPW revealed that zeolite US-Y still retains considerable activity even after processing 60 times its weight in PCPW. Metal and metal oxide impurities largely remain on the zeolite material, highlighting the potential of catalytic cracking yielding cleaner pyrolysis oil compared with thermal pyrolysis.

papers.title: In situ observation of ultra-giant spherulites in perovskite hydrates
papers.abstract: Spherulitic growth—commonly observed in polymers—is shown here to be reproducible in lead-halide perovskite hydrates on glass substrates, yielding ultra-giant spherulites spanning the mm–1 cm scale under specific conditions. Here I introduce Hygro-Triggered Giant Spherulite Formation (HT-GSF), an equipment-light process that transforms a routine spin-coated MAPbI₃₋ₓClₓ precursor film into a ~1 cm-scale giant spherulite using only standard glovebox and hot-plate steps. A 3:1 MAI/PbCl₂ precursor (40 wt% in DMF) is spin-coated on glass and annealed at 60 °C for 10 min under N₂ to produce a Cl-rich seed layer containing needle-like precursor crystallites. Subsequent exposure to ambient air (60–65% RH) reproducibly initiates a single surface nucleus that dominates growth and drives rapid two-dimensional radial expansion, completing within ~2 h. Real-time optical microscopy shows an advancing spherulite front that incorporates surrounding particles, consistent with a humidity-enabled dissolution–recrystallization pathway and local solute depletion near the growth interface. Post-annealing at 90 °C for 4 h converts the white precursor network into black perovskite while preserving a pronounced out-of-plane (110) texture. Optical microscopy confirms centimeter-scale, single-nucleus spherulites with strong preferred orientation and far fewer macroscopically visible high-angle grain boundaries than conventional spin-coated films, with 100% yield across >50 trials. Under ambient-air ageing tests, HT-GSF films exhibit only weak hydrate-related signatures after one week, whereas control films develop strong hydrate peaks and visible degradation within hours. HT-GSF provides a simple and reproducible route to mm–cm-scale, highly textured perovskite spherulites on glass, offering a platform for mechanistic studies and future evaluation of device relevance.

papers.title: Structural Determinants of Mac1 Inhibition: Lessons from Ligand Binding Patterns
papers.abstract: This study comprehensively analyzes how various inhibitors bind to the SARS-CoV-2 macrodomain Mac1, a key protein implicated in hampering the host's immune response following viral infection. In this study we used volume-based metadynamics simulations to investigate the binding mechanisms of ADP-ribose and two Mac1 inhibitors: the adenineanalogue GS-441524 and the non-adenine-analogue S09. By combining free-energy simulations with a bioinformatic analysis, we aimed at determining whether the binding patterns observed for the selected ligands are conserved can be generalized across Mac1 inhibitors and can be exploited to guide a rational design for future therapeutics. Our simulations show the pivotal role of the adenosine moiety in Mac1 recognition. Notably, for small molecules, like S09 and GS-441524, the oxyanion hole also emerged as an alternative and essential stabilizing region. This site, which preferentially accommodates electronegative groups, is engaged by approximately 76% of reported Mac1 inhibitors, making it a key target for Mac1 inhibition. In addition, we demonstrate that the unstructured loops 1 and 2 shape ligand entry, with loop 1 functioning as a dynamic gateway. Within this loop, Leu126, part of the virus-specific P-L-L-S motif, serves as a key anchoring residue for potent inhibitors. Collectively, these findings suggest that targeting both the oxyanion hole and Leu126 may enhance both the specificity and affinity of next-generation Mac1 inhibitors.

papers.title: Optimized composition of non-equimolar high-entropy alloy catalysts for stable and high yield of hydrogen-production using methane pyrolysis
papers.abstract: Here, we reports the design, synthesis, and catalytic evaluation of non-equimolar high-entropy alloy (HEA) and high-entropy oxide (HEO) catalysts for CO2-free hydrogen production via methane pyrolysis. Methane decomposition is an attractive hydrogen production route but typically requires very high temperatures and suffers from catalyst deactivation due to carbon deposition. To address these challenges, the current study explores the compositional flexibility and thermodynamic stability of high-entropy materials. A Co-Cr-Cu-Fe-Ni HEA system was compositionally optimized using FactSage thermodynamic calculations by imposing thermodynamic alloy design constraints. The optimized non-equimolar composition (Co24.8Cr15.2Cu8.3Fe34Ni17.7 at.%) was synthesized by vacuum arc melting and ball milling. Controlled oxidation at 550 °C produced the corresponding HEO. The equimolar HEA showed negligible activity, whereas the non-equimolar HEA exhibited moderate methane conversion. Notably, the HEO demonstrated superior reactivity, higher mass loss, and significantly enhanced hydrogen yields across the entire temperature range. Gas analysis revealed that methane decomposition dominates at elevated temperatures, with the HEO achieving substantially higher H2/CO ratios than the HEA. Post-reaction characterization showed uniform carbon coating on HEA surfaces, leading to active-site passivation, whereas HEO promoted directional growth of fibrous carbon. Density functional theory calculations elucidated the underlying mechanism, showing clustered d-band centers in HEO that favor optimal adsorption energies and preferential carbon binding at oxygen sites. The site-specific carbon deposition preserves active metal sites, explaining the enhanced stability and hydrogen yield of HEO catalysts. Overall, the work demonstrates that compositionally optimized nonequimolar HEOs are highly promising catalysts for efficient, stable, and CO2-free hydrogen production via methane pyrolysis

papers.title: The Thermal Properties of CH3COONa•3H2O as Suitable Energy Storage Materials Enhanced by BNNSs
papers.abstract: Sodium acetate trihydrate (CH3COONa•3H2O, SAT), as one kind of medium and low temperature inorganic hydrated salts, has high latent heat and suitable phase transition temperature. However, there are some problems such as supercooling, phase separation and poor cycle stability. In this paper, boron nitride nanosheets (BNNSs) and alumina (Al2O3) were used as nucleating agents, sodium carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC) was used as the thickener to inhibit the supercooling and phase separation of SAT successfully. BNNSs can also improve the thermal conductivity of SAT. It was found that the addition of 0.5 wt% Al2O3 can reduce the supercooling to 5.11 ℃ of SAT, and the addition of 1 wt% CMC can inhibit the phase separation phenomenon of SAT. The addition of BNNSs can further reduce the supercooling of SAT (0.63 ℃) and enhance the heat transfer characteristics of SAT (1.570 W•m-1 •K-1). The prepared composite has good thermal storage performance and cycle stability.

papers.title: Acoustochromatography based on low-cost polymer columns enables rapid extracellular vesicle proteome analysis from 1 µL blood plasma
papers.abstract: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) hold promise as biomarkers for early disease detection, yet their nanoscale size and the protein-rich plasma background make enrichment essential. Conventional approaches such as ultracentrifugation and size-exclusion chromatography require ≥150 µL input, hours of processing, and are poorly compatible with clinical workflows.We present a low-cost polymer-based acoustochromatography device that enables EV enrichment from 1 µL of blood plasma within 2–10 minutes - significantly faster than current gold-standard methods. A novel ultrasound-driven release mode increased recovery by up to two orders of magnitude compared to the previously reported acoustofluidic chromatography method. Comprehensive proteomic analysis confirmed highly pure EV fractions after acoustofluidic enrichment. Apolipoproteins were depleted by >99.6%, below levels reported for other methods, lifting 712 mostly EV associated proteins above background as compared to neat plasma. This low-cost, scalable platform unlocks proteomic profiling of ultra-low-volume samples, paving the way for rapid and clinically compatible EV biomarker diagnostics.

papers.title: Measuring Differences in Protein Allosteric Graphs Constructed via Molecular Dynamics Simulations
papers.abstract: Protein allostery plays essential roles in many biological processes through long-range communication between distant sites. Three-dimensional Shortest Path Map (3D SPM) graphs generated from molecular dynamics trajectories provide an effective, structure-embedded representation of protein conformational dynamics and allosteric communication pathways. However, comparisons among 3D SPM graphs have remained largely qualitative, limiting quantitative insight. Here, we address this gap by introducing an algorithm that uses the earth mover's distance (EMD) and the normalized graph Laplacian to quantitatively measure distances between 3D SPM graphs by evaluating their spatial distributions and network connectivity. This approach allows us to establish the sensitivity of computed allosteric communication networks to the choice of force field and other parameters in the 3D SPM calculations. Furthermore, the quantitative comparison of 3D SPM graphs enables distinguishing mutations that minimally perturb allosteric communication from those that substantially rewire the network. Importantly, decomposition of the EMD highlights the residues and edges that contribute the most to these shifts. This work has the potential to facilitate the analysis of high-throughput experiments regarding protein function and evolution, and to provide guidance for protein engineering.

papers.title: Direct Experimental Evidence of Transient Au δ+ Oxide in Au Electrooxidation
Can We Automate Scientific Reasoning in Closed-Loop Experiments using Large Language Models?
papers.abstract: We present here a detailed study of our hybrid optimisation framework, BORA, which integrates large language model (LLM) reasoning with Bayesian optimisation (BO) for accelerating scientific discovery using closed-loop experiments. We compare five modern LLMs (o4-mini, o3, gpt-5-mini, gpt-5, and gemini-2.5-flash) as optimisers for two benchmark problems: a 10-dimensional photocatalytic hydrogen-evolution experiment and a 7-dimensional physics-based pétanque simulation. The results show that LLM/BO hybrids outperform BO-only approaches, particularly in early-stage exploration where the search is warm-started by LLM-driven hypotheses. Among the models tested, o3 delivered the strongest and most consistent optimisation performance after 150 experiments. LLM-only optimisations without the BO component also matched or surpassed hybrid methods in some settings, locating optima with high repeatability. We demonstrated that appending human hypotheses, prior literature, or experimental datasets can improve convergence, and that LLM reasoning can recover in some cases from deliberately misleading prompts. We also explored outlier runs to understand the limitations and failure modes of these methods, as well as considering the energy implications of the LLM queries. The strongest LLM-only performance was observed with a batch size of one, suggesting that experiment-by-experiment machine reasoning is a viable strategy for certain automated scientific optimisation tasks.

papers.title: Surface-Specific and Bulk Field-Induced Contributions to Vibrational Sum-Frequency Generation Spectra at Charged Graphene Oxide/Water Interfaces
Microsolvation of Protonated Glycine: Infrared Spectra from Data-Driven Quantum Many-Body Simulations
Integrating Ensemble Machine-Learning and Fibril Docking to Discover Potent, Novel Triazole-Naphthalene Tau-Aggregation Inhibitors
papers.abstract: Tau-protein aggregation is a central pathological feature of Alzheimer's disease, so blocking fibril growth is an attractive therapeutic goal. We curated a high-quality set of 289 literature IC₅₀ measurements for human-tau aggregation and trained a stacked-ensemble QSAR model (SVR + RF + XGB) that achieves 5-fold CV Q² = 0.63, external R² = 0.57 and RMSE = 0.73 log-units. Applicability-domain analysis revealed no high-influence outliers in the calibration set, and a 5-nearest-neighbour density test confirmed that each of sixteen previously unreported 1,2,4-triazole-naphthalene derivatives (TND, TND-1…TND-15) lies in locally populated chemical space, albeit at the edge of the global domain. The model predicts pIC₅₀ = 6.75-7.53 (IC₅₀ ≈ 30-177 nM), nominating TND-9, TND-15 and TND-5 as the most potent candidates. Nearly all TNDs fall within the BBB window (MW ≈ 350-450 Da, TPSA < 90 Å²); most obey cLogP ≤ 5, and the few slightly above still map to the BOILED-Egg CNS-positive zone. Retrospective docking against phosphorylated-tau fibrils (PDB ID 6HRF) highlighted TND, TND-5 and TND-14 with sub-micromolar predicted affinity, forming key contacts in the microtubule-binding cleft. TND-8, although highly ranked by docking, was deprioritised owing to low predicted GI absorption. Physicochemical and CNS-oriented ADMET filters further support developability of the top leads. The integrated workflow-combining rigorously validated QSAR, structure-based docking on the 6HRF polymorph and developability profiling-provides an open-source blueprint for tau-aggregation inhibitor discovery. Consensus ranking prioritises TND-5 for immediate in-silico follow-up, with TND, TND-14, TND-9 and TND-15 as secondary leads.

papers.title: Benchmarking Machine Learning Fault Detection Methods on the Tennessee Eastman Process Dataset
papers.abstract: The Tennessee Eastman Process (TEP) dataset is a standard benchmark for process control and fault diagnosis due to its complex, multivariate dynamics. We evaluate a broad range of machine learning and deep learning methods for multivariate time-series anomaly detection on the dataset, covering 17 of its 20 fault types. After preprocessing the dataset, we benchmark classical models such as XGBoost and sequence models including LSTM classifiers, LSTM-FCN, a convolutional transformer, and a proposed Transformer-Kalman (TransKal) classifier. We also assess hybrid LSTM and convolutional autoencoder approaches. Supervised models were trained on combined normal and faulty data, while semi-supervised models used only normal data. Finally, we evaluate the models using an independent dataset to assess generalizability. Several models achieved 99%+ multiclass accuracy, but showed fragility on the independent dataset.

papers.title: Combined Interferometric Scattering Microscopy and Fluctuation Correlation Spectroscopy (iSCAT-FlucCS) for Measuring Nanostructures Growth and Size-Distribution
papers.abstract: Controlling the morphology and structural homogeneity of nanostructures is vital to optimizing their potential applications. This necessitates a fundamental understanding of the involved kinetic rates and their optimization. In-situ analysis of nanostructure growth, which provides information on the associated morphology within the same sample, is essential for establishing accurate correlations. To observe in-situ growth, optimize kinetics, and map associated morphology, this study introduces the development of an experimental platform based on interferometric scattering (iSCAT). This platform enables simultaneous monitoring of growth kinetics via microscopy and the extraction of size distributions from the same sample, within the same reaction vessel, under identical conditions, through iSCAT fluctuation correlation spectroscopy (iSCAT-FlucCS), a bimodal system. Utilizing this platform, we investigate light-induced, seed-mediated synthesis of silver nanorods and systematically analyze the effects of precursor concentrations, seed volume, and illumination wavelength on both reaction rates and the final morphology of the synthesized nanostructures. The results demonstrate a direct correlation between kinetic rate constants and particle morphology; specifically, high nucleation rates favour the formation of spherical particles, whereas elevated autocatalytic growth rates, combined with suppressed nucleation, promote anisotropic elongation into nanorods. Additionally, we show that iSCAT-FlucCS can reliably and accurately recover particle size and size distribution, aligning with conventional ensemble averaging techniques. This work establishes iSCAT-FlucCS as a comprehensive, label-free, and non-invasive tool for probing, understanding, and ultimately controlling nanostructure synthesis dynamics and morphology, with potential applications in nanomaterials design, mechanistic investigations, and real-time reaction optimization.

papers.title: Highly Luminescent Carbazole-functionalized Tris(tribromophenyl)methyl Radicals with Stable Circularly Polarized Photoluminescence
papers.abstract: Brominated trityl radicals form stable enantiomers and are promising candidates for molecular qubits in spintronic and quantum technological applications, due to their long spin coherence times. However, their inherently weak photoluminescence (ϕ < 3 %) limits optical spin readout. Here, we report the first synthesis of three carbazolefunctionalized tris(2,4,6-tribromophenyl)methyl (TTBrM) radicals via Buchwald-Hartwig cross-coupling. These chiral open-shell emitters exhibit remarkably high photoluminescence quantum yields of up to ϕ = 72%, comparable to their chlorinated analogues, with red-shifted emission (λ PL = 646-688 nm), due to enhanced charge-transfer character. Enantiomeric resolution via chiral chromatography yields stable atropisomers (T rac > 90 °C) with strong circular dichroism (CD) and circularly polarized luminescence (CPL) showing dissymmetry factors (gabs, glum) of order 10⁻⁴, originating from the trityl propeller core. EPR confirms spin localization on the trityl unit (g ≈ 2.006), while donor methylation improves photostability (t 1/2 up to 49 min) and modestly extended phase memory times (T m = 1.49-1.68 µs). These bright, chiral TTBrM radicals represent a significant advance toward stable molecular qubits with efficient optical spin readout for quantum technologies.

papers.title: Diastereoselective Heterogeneous Hydrogenation of Bicyclic Arenes Directed by Amines and Alcohols
papers.abstract: The heterogeneous hydrogenation of aromatic compounds using supported metal catalysts is an efficient strategy to increase the three-dimensionality and molecular complexity of organic molecules. However, most heterogeneous hydrogenation methods lack stereoselectivity or rely upon the steric properties of the substrate for stereocontrol, which limit their predictability and generality for pharmaceutical synthesis applications. In this work, we develop two synthetic methods for the amine-and hydroxyl-directed hydrogenation of benzofused arenes using Rh/C and Pt 3 Cu/SiO 2 as heterogeneous catalysts, respectively. Mechanistic studies on the amine-directed reaction reveal that simultaneous adsorption of the amine and benzene functional groups to the Rh metal surface is extremely strong, outcompeting adsorption of the benzene or amine individually and enabling good turnover and high diastereoselectivity toward the amine-directed product. A broad scope of benzofused scaffolds are effective substrates, generating up to four stereocenters in a single step. The utility of the method is demonstrated in the synthesis of a novel chiral ligand, a pyridine bisoxazoline compound derived from perhydro- cis -aminoindanol, which shows enantioselectivity comparable to its aromatic counterpart in three model asymmetric reactions.

papers.title: 3D-printed optical VOC sensors based on donor-substituted coumarin TADF emitters
papers.abstract: Volatile organic compounds (VOCs) pose a major environmental and health concern, motivating the development of solid-state optical sensing materials that are both responsive and easily manufacturable. Here we introduce a new family of donor-substituted coumarin thermally activated delayed fluorescent emitters, and embed them within photocurable acrylate resins. These materials retain strong solid-state photoluminescence and can be 3D printed into functional sensing architectures that show reproducible, intensity-based optical responses to chemically diverse VOCs vapors. This work demonstrates how tailored emitter design and 3D printing can be combined to realise versatile VOC-responsive optical materials.

papers.title: Exploring the Synergy of Combining BINAP and tCzBN Motifs Within Multi-Resonant TADF Emitters to Enhance OLED Performance
papers.abstract: Two new multiresonant thermally activated delayed fluorescence (MR-TADF) emitters, BINAP-BN1 and BINAP-BN2, containing a 1,1'-binaphthalene (BINAP) unit and a varying number of tCzBN units (one in BINAP-BN1 and two in BINAP-BN2), were synthesized. In toluene, both showed emission maxima at ca. 490 nm, photoluminescence quantum yields (Φ PL ) up to 82%, and Δ E ST of ~0.15 eV. Significant differences in their optoelectronic properties emerged as their 1 wt% doped films in mCBP. BINAP-BN1 has a Φ PL of 82%, while that of BINAP-BN2 is 64%. Aggregation-induced emission broadening at higher doping concentrations is suppressed for BINAP-BN1 but not for BINAP-BN2, attributed to the less sterically hindered BINAP moiety in the former. These photophysical differences translated in device performance. The organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs) with BINAP-BN1 and BINAP-BN2 achieved maximum external quantum efficiencies (EQE max ) of 20.1 and 14.1%, respectively, at corresponding CIE coordinates of (0.08, 0.42) and (0.10, 0.50). A hyperfluorescence (HF) device employing HDT-1 as sensitizer and BINAP-BN1 as terminal emitter improved EQE max to 22.0% and reduced efficiency roll-off to 32% at 1000 cd/m², compared to 52% in the binary device. In comparison, a device with 1 wt% tCzBN in mCBP showed an EQE max of 15.6%, rising to 21.6% in a HF configuration.

papers.title: Beyond The RISC Rate: A Figure of Merit for MR-TADF Materials and the Path to High Efficiency OLEDs Having Minimal Efficiency Roll-Off and High Stability
papers.abstract: The relatively slow reverse intersystem cross rate constant ( k RISC ) of multi-resonant thermally activated delayed fluorescence (MR-TADF) emitters has been recognized as perhaps the most critical factor governing their rather significant efficiency roll-off in organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs). A recent study identified a figure of merit for TADF materials, which captures the relevant exciton dynamics processes and correlates these with efficiency roll-off in the resulting device. Two MR-TADF emitters tBTCzBN and tSeCzBN, containing, respectively, dibenzothiophenocarbazole and dibenzoselenophenocarbazoles were designed. Their rigid p-and n-doped nanographene structures, incorporating heavy chalcogen atoms at optimal locations, result in fast 𝑘 γ S s of 1.7×10 8 and 7.7 ×10 7 s -1 , k RISC values of 2.6 ×10 5 and 3.9 ×10 6 s -1 , and FOMs of 1.8 ×10 5 and 3.9 ×10 5 s -1 for tBTCzBN and tSeCzBN, respectively. The sensitizer-free OLEDs with tBTCzBN and tSeCzBN exhibited green electroluminescence [CIE coordinates of (0.14, 0.61), and (0.18, 0.61)]. Notably, the device with tSeCzBN delivered superior high maximum external quantum efficiencies (EQE max ) of 37.1%, with EQE 1000 of 31.7%, which is one of the highest reported EQE1000 values, and is matched by a remarkably low efficiency roll-off of 14%, especially compared to other MR-TADF OLEDs. Moreover, the incorporated chalcogen atoms modulate the frontier molecular orbital levels of the emitter, resulting in much-improved operational stability as a result of suppressed hole trapping. This work highlights the distinct benefits and the importance of judicious incorporation of heavy atoms within MR-TADF emitter structures to facilitate efficient exciton harvesting and enhance device performance.

papers.title: Nanoplastics can build themselves
papers.abstract: To understand nanoplastics through modeling, e.g., to assess their toxicity and environmental impact, reliable starting structures are required. In this study, we present a new approach to generate nanoplastic particles from classical molecular dynamics simulations. Starting with the initial aggregation of monomer units and allowing for their subsequent growth into polymer strands yields stable aggregates with polymers of diverse length, avoiding the need to define the number of polymer units with a set length a priori. The generated particles are compared to existing model nanoplastics and show agreement in terms of structural characteristics and energetics. The novel approach is computationally efficient and allows for a greater diversity of structures than approaches with predefined chain lengths.

papers.title: Silicon-Carbon Bond Cleavage from a Hydroboration Sequence
papers.abstract: The reactions of internal pyridyl/trialkylsilyl alkynes with the potent hydroboration reagent bis(1-methyl- ortho -carboranyl)borane (HB Me o Cb 2 ) results in unanticipated Si-C alkyl cleavage following a regioselective 1,1-hydroboration under mild conditions. The rare Si-Me bond rupture of the trimethylsilyl group occurs by an intramolecular frustrated Lewis pair system forming a silylium heterocycle with a pendant borate bearing the methyl group. Investigating a methyl/ethyl mixed silyl substituent, SiEtMe 2 , revealed the reaction is completely selective in breaking the Si-Me bond over the Si-Et bond. Exposure of the silylium/borate zwitterion to methanol resulted in O-H bond cleavage and ring opening to a zwitterionic pyridinium/borate. These findings provide insight into the challenging selective functionalization of Si-C alkyl bonds.

papers.title: Metal-catalysed Hydroboration of Amide-containing Styrenes
papers.abstract: Hydroboration of alkenes is one of the most important methods for preparing alkylboron reagents. While alkylboronic esters are considered to be functional group compatible reagents, methods to prepare them do not always show the same tolerance. In this work, we explore the hydroboration of amide-containing styrenes using catalysts derived from Cu, Ir and Rh. Tertiary amides were found to be compatible with each method we tested. However, secondary amides, with an acidic NH bond, were only successfully hydroborated with Ir and Rh catalysts, but not the Cu-catalyst. The selectivity of hydroboration was consistent with previous findings, with Cu giving only branched products, Ir giving linear only products, and Rh favouring branched products though with variable regioselectivity. Finally, an amide-containing benzylic boronic ester was successfully used in a range of transformations of the boron group, including Cu-catalysed amination, Suzuki-Miyaura cross coupling, and oxidation.

papers.title: OPTIMIZATION OF ENZYMATIC HYDROLYSIS OF CORNCOB FOR BIOFUEL PRODUCTION USING MULTI-ENZYME SYSYTEMS
papers.abstract: The depletion of fossil fuels and the associated environmental challenges have accelerated the search for sustainable biofuels from renewable sources like corncob. This study investigated the use of synergistic enzyme cocktails to enhance the enzymatic hydrolysis of acid-pretreated corncob. Initial screening showed that only pectinase and β-glucosidase demonstrated significant synergy with cellulase. Using Response Surface Methodology (RSM), a highly predictive quadratic model, with an R 2 value of 0.9571, was developed to optimize the enzyme cocktail. The optimal blend, consisting of 10 mg/g cellulase, 39.88 mg/g pectinase, and 38.20 mg/g β-glucosidase, achieved a hydrolysis yield of 42.35%. This represents a 5.25-fold increase compared to using cellulase alone. These findings underscore the effectiveness of enzyme synergy and process optimization as key strategies for efficiently valorizing corncob into fermentable sugars for sustainable biobutanol production

papers.title: A General Photooxidation Platform for Alcohols via Transient Excited-State α-Keto Esters
papers.abstract: Transient excited-state auxiliaries provide a powerful strategy for enabling difficult bond activations under mild conditions. Here we report a general alcohol oxidation platform in which phenylglyoxalate α-keto esters act as visible-light-activated, traceless oxidation devices, converting primary and secondary alcohols to aldehydes and ketones without external photocatalysts, metals, or stoichiometric oxidants. The protocol shows broad functionalgroup tolerance and supports late-stage oxidation of complex scaffolds, including pharmacophores, carbohydrates, steroids and a peptide. Practicality is further demonstrated through in situ alcohol activation and efficient continuous-flow scale-up. Mechanistic experiments and DFT studies support a photoinduced fragmentation pathway consistent with a 1,5-HAT-initiated biradical process, underscoring the utility of excitedstate α-keto esters as transient, traceless auxiliaries for preparative oxidation chemistry.

papers.title: The Chemical Simplex: Geometric Foundations of Mixture Observability, Intrinsic Dimensionality, and Rank Constraints in Chemometrics
What Electrochemical Voltages Can-and Cannot-Tell Us about Electrolyte Non-Ideality
papers.abstract: Electrochemical voltages depend on ionic activities and are therefore intrinsically sensitive to electrolyte non-ideality. Inverse electrochemical approaches leverage this dependence to infer thermodynamic information directly from measured voltages rather than predicting voltages from assumed activity models. A central challenge is the interpretation and identifiability of inferred quantities when both the electrolyte and the membrane phase are strongly non-ideal. Here, we show that voltage measurements necessarily constrain effective thermodynamic descriptors that integrate electrolyte, membrane, and interfacial non-ideality. We further establish identifiability through sensitivity analysis linking perturbations in descriptor components to the non-ideal voltage contribution. These results define fundamental limits on what voltage observables can-and cannot-reveal about electrolyte non-ideality.

papers.title: AI-Assisted Designing of Novel Anticancer Compounds
papers.abstract: Anti-cancer drug design has historically been a challenging and resource-intensive process. Artificial intelligence (AI) and deep learning now enable rapid generation and prioritization of novel drug-like compounds. This study presents a SMILES-to-SELFIES Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) model that was trained on existing anticancer compounds to generate structurally diverse candidate molecules followed by ADMET filtering, molecular docking, synthetic accessibility scoring, and QSAR prediction. A total of 100 new molecules were generated, of which top candidates showed strong predicted potency and favorable pharmacokinetic properties. Particularly, Molecule-43 demonstrated the highest predicted inhibitory potential and drug-likeness score. Several candidates exhibited strong predicted binding against five cancer-associated target proteins (EGFR, P53, AKT1, BCL-2, and IKKβ), with Molecule 43 showing consistent multi-target affinity. QSAR prediction using Random Forest models further supported the inhibitory potential of prioritized compounds. These results demonstrate a promising computational strategy for accelerating anticancer drug discovery. This work is a purely computational study, and all results represent predictive hypotheses requiring experimental validation.

papers.title: Misconceptions in Unbound Volume of Distribution and Their Implications for Pharmacokinetic Scaling and Drug Design
papers.abstract: Unbound volume of distribution is sometimes treated as an intrinsic, species-invariant property. Mechanistic analysis shows that it can be influenced by plasma protein binding through tissueplasma binding relationships, and that assuming constant tissue binding across species is not generally valid. Case evidence and modeling indicate that modulating plasma protein binding can meaningfully affect half-life and hepatic extraction, thereby improving oral bioavailability and in vivo efficacy. These insights argue for revisiting common cross-species scaling practices and for considering plasma protein binding as an explicit design parameter.

papers.title: CO₂ Responsive Nanoscopic and Macroscopic Materials Directed by Peptides
papers.abstract: Stimuli such as pH, light, and electromagnetic fields have enabled precise control over nanoscale interactions, yet gases remain relatively unexplored as regulators of material behavior despite their central roles in biology, energy, and climate. Here, we introduce carbon dioxide as a dynamic and reversible stimulus for controlling nanoscale and macroscale matter using sequence specific peptide design. Peptide-functionalized nanoparticles exhibit pronounced and tunable responses to CO2 across orders of magnitude changes in gas flow rate, with sensitivity governed by site-and sequence-specific changes in peptide structure. This gas-controlled response translates from colloidal nanoparticles to cm-scale biocompatible hydrogels that reversibly and colorimetrically respond to CO2. Leveraging this responsiveness, we further demonstrate spatial patterning of a hydrogel through a gas-permeable mask using CO2 as a lithographic stimulus. Consequently, this work establishes gas-mediated control as a general and scalable strategy for programming responsive materials across length scales.

papers.title: Fluorination of Alkoxide Ligands: Neither too much, Nor too little for Optimal Ligand Field Strength
papers.abstract: Fluorination is generally expected to act predictably in ligand design: each added fluorine atom withdraws electron density, weakens σ-donation, and steadily modulates reactivity. However, reported catalytic systems show activity instead peaking at intermediate fluorination-a non-monotonic trend that simple donor-strength arguments cannot explain. To disentangle this non-monotonicity, we prepared a series of homoleptic Mo(V) alkoxides bearing fluorinated tert-butoxide ligands via Mo(IV) → Mo(V/III) disproportionation. As oxo-free d¹ species with trigonal-bipyramidal geometry, these complexes provide a direct EPR handle on ligand-field splitting, indicating strengthened axial fields at partial fluorination. Computations (X2C-DFT and DLPNO-CCSD(T)) reveal enhanced donor-acceptor overlap and favorable electrostatics at intermediate F-content, rationalizing the fluorination sweet spot observed experimentally in catalysis. 17 O NMR calculations pinpoint the physical origin of this effect towards C-CF3 σ* acceptor orbitals. The findings provide understanding of fluorination and can be used to develop new alkoxide ligands and analogous promising synthons for alkoxide-containing catalysts.

papers.title: Periodic Trends in Electron Withdrawing Ability: Effects on Carbon-Fluorine Reductive Elimination from Palladium as a Model System
papers.abstract: Tri(1-adamantyl)phosphine (Ad 3 P) represents a prototypical trialkylphosphine with more polarizable diamoindoid substituents. While certain properties of Ad 3 P, such as its relatively high donicity, have been correlated to increased polarizability, a more systematic assessment of the electronic properties of adamantyl-type fragments and associated ligand effects in catalysis is desirable. In this work, a suite of isosteric trialkylphosphines featuring tert -butyl, 1-adamantyl as well as related heteroadamantyl and (hetero)diamantyl fragments were parameterized and evaluated to isolate electronic substituent effects on the energetics of a challenging model reaction-C(sp 2 )-F reductive elimination (RE) from (R 3 P)Pd II (Ar)F complexes. The RE energy barriers correlated more strongly to electrostatic versus polarizability, dispersion, or inductive parameters. Ligands varying by substitution (N, O, S, or Se) at remote δ positions of the diamondoid fragment still manifested significant net electron withdrawing effects, particularly for chalcogen-containing ligands. Surprisingly, the withdrawing effect was insensitive to chalcogen identity, which we attribute to compensation between periodic trend (i.e., electronegativity and bond angle) and geometry-dependent local dipole alignment. Observation that substituent withdrawing ability and concomitant ligand donicity can be tuned by geometric constraints may provide new opportunities for ligand design in transition metal catalysis beyond typical notions of substituent electronic effects.

papers.title: Site Specific Hydrogen Deuterium Exchange Mass Spectrometry Enables Deep Explorations of Dynamic Allosteric Networks in Protein-Drug Interactions
A fresh look at signatures of s-wave scattering: Symmetry and the breakdown of the Born-Oppenheimer approximation
papers.abstract: The peculiar behavior of σ-type anionic states is analyzed in terms of the interaction between bound and continuum states. Within a simple Landau–Zener model, strong diabatic coupling leads to a broad avoided crossing and strongly mixed adiabatic states, whereas weak diabatic coupling leads to a narrow avoided crossing and an abrupt change in the character of the adiabatic states. By using symmetry analysis and numeric calculations, we show that σ-type anionic states such as those in HCl, methyl chloride, and pyrrole interact much stronger with the continuum than π ∗ -type anionic states such as the N 2 resonance. Strong interaction leads to the breakdown of the Born–Oppenheimer approximation, which results in a finite probability to decay into the detachment continuum even in the regions where the anionic state is energetically below the neutral state. We show that calculations with a complex absorbing potential capture this special character of σ-type anions through removal of the detachment continuum, affording diabatization of the anionic state, while describing the decay into the continuum via imaginary energy Γ.

papers.title: Evolving transition-state search with agentic large language models
papers.abstract: Accurate identification of transition states (TSs) is fundamental to computational chemistry. Modern reaction-discovery efforts increasingly rely on refining large reaction datasets, where even a small fraction of TS-search failures can leave key pathways unresolved and bias the resulting reaction network. Here, we introduce an adaptive evolutionary framework for TS search workflows that prioritizes completion of a target dataset over global algorithmic robustness. The framework iteratively focuses on reactions for which no validated TS has been found and dynamically modifies the workflow to search the remaining TSs. Rather than converging toward a single universally optimal TS search workflow, the framework generates a sequence of specialized workflow variants that collectively solve the dataset. Applied to the Transition1X benchmark (over 10,000 reactions), this adaptive evolution refines a state-of-the-art TS-search workflow to achieve a 99.96% TS localization success rate. More broadly, these results suggest that adaptive, LLM-driven evolutionary workflow optimization provides a transferable strategy for achieving near-complete coverage in large-scale, failure-prone scientific workflows.

papers.title: Tuning Hydrogen Evolution Activity via Composition-Engineered MoS₂-WS₂ Mixed Crystals
papers.abstract: We report growth of mixed crystal of transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) Mo1-xWxS2 (0 ≤ 𝑥 ≤ 1) thin films using simple and scalable solution-based method, i.e. spin coating for enhanced hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). For this purpose, a mixture of single source Mo/W precursors (with different Mo/W ratios) solution was spin coated onto a planer substrate, followed by moderate temperature sulfurization in a reducing environment. The composition of the mixed crystal was precisely tuned by varying Mo:W precursor ratio. The uniformity and surface coverage of the obtained thin films was confirmed by optical microscopy, AFM and SEM. High resolution AFM image revealed a nanoflower type nanostructure which has potentially higher active edge sites. Raman, XPS and UV-Vis spectroscopy verified successful formation of mixed crystal films and revealed systematic shift in the structural and electronic signature with changing composition. Electrochemical study revealed a strong influence of the composition of the mixed crystal on the catalytic performance. For instance, mixed crystal Mo0.5W0.5S2 showed superior HER activity compared to MoS2 and WS2 in its pure form, with overpotential of 229 mV at 10 mA/cm 2 , Tafel slope 69 mV/dec and charge transfer resistance of 75 ohm. These enhancements in the catalytic activities are attributed to optimization of electronic band structure of the alloy and defect induced activation sites. Overall, this work shows the potential of solution-based growth of mixed crystal as an economical, scalable approach for enhance hydrogen evolution reaction.

papers.title: Unusual meroterpenoids suggests an unprecedent cascade of Diels-Alder reactions in their biosynthesis
papers.abstract: In nature, cascade reactions are used to produce specialised metabolites with highly complex architectures in just a few steps. Understanding their mechanisms paves the way for synthesising a wide variety of innovative three-dimensional structures. In this study, we present the targeted isolation of litseifolins A-C, meroterpenoids with an unusual 6/6/5/6 tetracyclic skeleton and up to five asymmetric centres. We propose a plausible biosynthetic pathway, supported by DFT calculations and experimental synthetic evidence. The study culminated in the biomimetic synthesis of litseifolins A-C under mild conditions. This process started with the putative biosynthetic precursor and involved an original intermolecular Diels-Alder/IMHDA cascade followed by dehydration. This study highlights the importance of combining computational and synthetic approaches for elucidating biosynthesis.

papers.title: Insights Into the Debated Lyase Mechanism of Bifunctional DNA Glycosylases From MD and QM/MM MD Simulations: The Case Study of DNA Oxidative Damage Repair by hOGG1
papers.abstract: DNA damage induced by reactive oxygen species (ROS) can result in mutations that contribute to the development of human diseases such as cancer, neurological disorders, cardiovascular disease, and diabetes. Human 8-oxoguanine DNA glycosylase (hOGG1) is responsible for repairing the major DNA oxidative product, namely 8-oxoguanine (8oG). hOGG1 is a member of the bifunctional DNA glycosylase family, which cleaves both the glycosidic and phosphodiester bonds in damaged nucleotides as part of base excision repair (BER). While nucleotide deglycosylation to yield an enzyme-DNA imine crosslink has been well studied both experimentally and 2 computationally for several bifunctional glycosylases, relatively little is known about the subsequent and typically rate-limiting phosphodiester bond cleavage step. To gain the first atomic level details of the β-lyase pathway for a bifunctional glycosylase, the present study uses a combination of classical MD and QM/MM MD simulations to characterize the hOGG1 mechanism of action. Our simulations reveal that the cleaved 8oG glycosylation product rapidly leaves the active site, precluding the previously proposed product-assisted elimination and supporting the allosteric nature of 8oG activators. Although QM/MM MD calculations suggest a neutral crosslink prevents lyase activity, a pathway involving initial hydrolysis of a cationic crosslink followed by D268-catalyzed phosphate elimination is catalytically feasible and the first proposed mechanism to unify all existing experimental kinetic, mutagenic, and structural data. Furthermore, K249 is demonstrated to be a viable substitute for D268 in the elimination step, rationalizing reports that hOGG1 can accommodate D268 mutation. Our newly characterized mechanism of action can push forward the development of small molecule hOGG1 inhibitors and activators as disease therapeutics, while key mechanistic features may be generalizable to understand the function of other bifunctional glycosylases.

papers.title: Lipid Membrane-Coated Nanopipettes for Enhanced Resistive Pulse Sensing of Exosomes
papers.abstract: We report the use of lipid membrane-coated quartz nanopipettes to enhance exosome detection via resistive pulse sensing (RPS). By exploiting the self-assembly and compositional versatility of lipid molecules, nanopipettes were functionalised with lipid membranes comprising neutral and cationic lipids, with or without cholesterol, to modulate surface charge and membrane viscosity. Using bovine milkderived exosomes as a model system, we demonstrate a marked improvement in capture efficiency and a reduction in non-specific adsorption. This improvement further enabled statistical analysis of translocation times and signal amplitudes, providing significant insights into the interactions between exosomes and lipid membranes during nanopore passage under an applied electric field.

papers.title: A green and efficient strategy for fabricating supercapacitor devices using mechanochemically synthesised Cu-HHTP MOF
papers.abstract: Supercapacitors are attractive energy-storage devices owing to their high power density, fast charge-discharge rates, and long cycle life, but their performance critically depends on electrode materials that must combine high accessible surface area, efficient ion transport, and adequate electrical conductivity. Two-dimensional π-conjugated metal-organic frameworks (2D conductive MOFs) have emerged as promising alternatives to porous carbons, as they couple electric double-layer capacitance with additional pseudocapacitive contributions from redox-active sites. Among them, a copper-catecholate MOF based on 2,3,6,7,10,11-hexahydroxytriphenylene (HHTP) ligand (Cu-HHTP) has shown notable charge-storage capability but its structural model has remained uncertain due to its tendency to form micro-to nanocrystalline powders during solvothermal synthesis. Herein, the crystal structure of Cu-HHTP is elucidated by three-dimensional electron diffraction (3D ED), unambiguously defining the framework connectivity and enabling a structure-guided rationale for the optimization of a rapid and efficient mechanosynthesis of this MOF. Phase-pure Cu-HHTP with improved crystalline size was obtained by liquid-assisted grinding in the presence of a modulator, providing a greener and scalable alternative to solution synthesis. The mechanochemically prepared material is processed into composite electrodes, assembled into symmetric coin-cell supercapacitors with an aqueous electrolyte (1M Na 2 SO 4 ), and benchmarked against a solvothermally synthesised analogue. Two-electrode cyclic voltammetry, galvanostatic charge-discharge, and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy, complemented by three-electrode measurements, reveal predominantly EDLC behaviour with additional faradaic contributions associated with the HHTP motif. Notably, mechanochemically synthesised Cu-HHTP delivers enhanced supercapacitor performance, including higher reversible specific capacitance, greater energy and power densities, and improved cycling stability, while exhibiting a modest increase in series resistance.

papers.title: Enantioselective Synthesis of Gamma-Butenolides from Streptomyces rochei and Derivatives
papers.abstract: Given the challenges of discovering new natural products, further investigations into the regulatory systems that control their production are needed. Herein, we describe an enantioselective, divergent synthesis of two known autoregulators from Streptmyces rochei, the Streptomyces rochei butenolides (SRBs), along with nine derivatives. Key reactions include enantioselective alkynylation and regioselective photo-oxidation We also develop a quantitative green-fluorescence protein (GFP) based reporter assay and use this assay to assess key structural features for natural product induction.

papers.title: Spin-crossover iron(II) complexes featuring boronic acid and boronic ester groups: synthesis and magnetic properties
papers.abstract: A series of bis(pyrazol-1-yl)pyridine (1-BPP)-based iron(II) complexes bearing either a boronic acid group or boronic monoester groups, with the general formula [Fe II (1-BPP)2](ClO4)2, have been synthesized and characterized in the solid state. The boronic acid or boronic monoester substituents are introduced at the 4-position of the pyridine ring. Despite their close structural similarity, the four iron(II) complexes exhibit markedly different magnetic properties. Complex 1a, which contains a boronic acid group, undergoes an incomplete, thermally induced spin-crossover in the solid state. Conversion of the boronic acid group into monomethyl or monoethyl esters stabilizes the high-spin state in 1b and 1c, respectively. Further substitution with electron-donating tert-butyl groups in 2b enforces a pure low-spin state.

papers.title: Deciphering the impact of both hydrogen bond donor and acceptor on the physicochemical properties of eutectic solvents
papers.abstract: Solvent selection plays a crucial role in many chemical reactions and solvent tunability has the potential to improve many of them. However, commonly used organic solvents only offer certain interactions, hindering their usability. In this study, we explore the possibility of solvent tuning by studying the physicochemical properties of both binary and ternary eutectic solvents. Here, we rationally designed solvents by varying the number of carbons of hydrogen bond acceptors (HBAs) and hydrogen bond donors (HBDs), altering the HBA:HBD molar ratios, and generating linear combinations of binary solvents to form ternary and quaternary solvents. The physical properties we studied were density and viscosity, while the chemical properties were acidity, basicity and polarity as determined by the Kamlet-Taft solvatochromic scale. The results showed that the HBD dictated the overall physicochemical properties of the solvent since a change in number of carbons led to significant changes in all the properties. Meanwhile, the acceptor only influenced physical properties as they were the only ones affected by a change in the number of carbons in the HBA. Additionally, using ternary and quaternary mixtures of these eutectic solvents, we demonstrated how solvent tunability is achievable as they exhibit a linear relationship between solvent properties and composition. Developing an understanding of how the individual components affect the overall physicochemical properties of ternary eutectic solvents is crucial for the fine-tuning of these solvents to improve chemical reactions.

papers.title: Anisotropic hot spot formation at a grain boundary in shock-compressed TATB high explosive crystal
PEDOT:PSS/EG-based solid-state ion-selective electrochemical sensors for multiplexed Na⁺ and K⁺ detection in saliva, serum, and interstitial fluid
papers.abstract: Accurate monitoring of sodium (Na +) and potassium (K +) ions in biological fluids is critical for assessing electrolyte balance and health status in calves and is strongly associated with major diseases such as bovine respiratory disease (BRD) and neonatal diarrhoea (scours). Alterations in Na + and K + concentrations provide key insight into dehydration, metabolic disturbance, and disease progression; however, routine electrolyte monitoring in veterinary settings remains challenging due to matrix complexity, sensor drift, and limited stability of solid-state ion-selective electrodes. Here, we report a multiplexed solid-state ion-selective sensor platform based on microfabricated interdigitated gold electrodes modified with a poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene):polystyrenesulfonate (PEDOT:PSS) solid-state layer and drop-cast Na +-and K +-selective membranes. Ethylene glycol (EG) was incorporated into the PEDOT:PSS layer to enhance electrical conductivity and interfacial charge transport, and the solid-state thickness and EG concentration were systematically optimized. The fabricated sensors exhibited near-Nernstian responses with sensitivities of 54 mV.dec-1 for Na + over a linear range of 10-170 mM and 51 mV.dec-1 for K + over 1-40 mM. Stable open-circuit potential responses were obtained with rapid equilibration (~10 s), low drift, high selectivity, minimal hysteresis, and excellent long-term stability. Sensor performance was validated in complex biofluids, including artificial saliva (AS), fetal bovine serum (FBS), and simulated interstitial fluid (ISF), using a standard addition approach. Quantitative comparison with commercial ionselective meters yielded recovery values within acceptable ranges. Overall, this work demonstrates a robust and scalable electrolyte sensing platform with strong potential for onfarm diagnostics, point-of-care testing, and future wearable systems for animal health monitoring.

papers.title: Time-Evolved Hetero-Alkali Interphases Enable Long-Life Sulfide-Based Anode-Free Solid-State Batteries
papers.abstract: Sulfide-based anode-free solid-state batteries (AFSSBs) offer compelling advantages in terms of energy density and safety, yet their practical implementation is severely hindered by undesirable interfacial reactions between sulfide solid electrolytes (SEs) and freshly plated lithium (Li), as well as non-uniform Li plating/stripping behavior. Herein, an effective interfacial stabilization strategy by incorporating sodium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide (NaFSI) additive into the Li5.4PS4.4Cl1.6 (LPSC) is investigated. Unlike conventional Li-based additives that form static passivation layers, NaFSI introduces a transient hetero-alkali chemistry that kinetically governs interphase evolution during fresh Li plating. NaFSI induces a timesequenced interphase evolution: an initial NaF/LiF-rich layer that suppresses early sulfide reduction, followed by a LiF/Li3N-rich layer that optimizes Li⁺ transport during repeated anode-free cycling. This evolved robust and fast ion conducting layer mitigates interfacial impedance growth, enhances Li + transport kinetics, and suppresses localized Li growth and filamentary shorting. As a result, the anode-free full cell with NaFSI modified LPSC as the interlayer exhibits an excellent cycling stability over 500 cycles at 0.2 C with a capacity retention of 77.6%, whereas the cell with bare LPSC suffers from rapid capacity decay after 100 cycles, retaining only 32.1% of its initial capacity. This work establishes dynamic heteroalkali additive chemistry as a general strategy to kinetically program solid-solid interphases, guiding the interface design in anode-free solid-state batteries.

papers.title: Surface Structure and Electrochemical Signatures of Copper Nanocrystals with Tunable Facets
papers.abstract: Understanding the surface structure of copper nanocrystals is critical for optimizing their catalytic performance in electrochemical reactions such as CO2 reduction, hydrogen evolution, and nitrate reduction. Copper nanowires (CuNWs) and nanoplates (CuNPls) exhibit distinct morphologies and facet distributions influenced by halide ion concentration during synthesis. Here we systematically modulated Br⁻ and I⁻ concentrations to direct the growth of CuNWs and CuNPls, characterized their structures via XRD, SEM, and TEM, and probed their surface facets using cyclic voltammetry and Pb underpotential deposition. CuNWs predominantly expose (100) facets with higher surface roughness, while CuNPls are dominated by (111) facets with smoother surfaces, each displaying unique electrochemical fingerprints. These insights into facet-controlled synthesis and surface characterization provide a foundation for rational design of copper-based electrocatalysts tailored for sustainable energy applications.

papers.title: Explaining What Matters: Faithfulness in Molecular Deep Learning
papers.abstract: Deep learning is accelerating drug and molecule discovery. Yet, the 'opaque' nature of these models limits their reliability for hypothesis-driven research, motivating the need for explainable AI (xAI). Although xAI is gaining traction in the molecular sciences, systematic benchmarking is rare. Moreover, faithfulness-the extent to which an explanation reflects a model's internal reasoning-remains overlooked. Here, we address this gap by evaluating the faithfulness of eight xAI feature attribution methods across two molecular representations and five neural network architectures on ≈14,000 molecules. We find that (a) some xAI methods are inherently more faithful than others, regardless of the architecture, and (b) faithfulness can still vary markedly on a per-molecule basis. Our findings show that faithfulness evaluation has an untapped potential to reveal model behavior, including biases and shortcuts. To support a broad adoption, the methods, metrics, and results of this study have been provided as an open-access platform named MolFaith, available at the following URL: https://github.com/molML/MolFaith. We expect our study to advance molecular xAI by enabling more informed use of feature attribution methods and propel the development of more faithful xAI approaches.

papers.title: DFT Investigation of carbonate substituted hydroxyapatite by Infrared Spectra
papers.abstract: Carbonate substitution in hydroxyapatite significantly alters its vibrational response, yet experimental infrared (IR) assignments remain ambiguous due to overlapping features from distinct defect configurations. We present a systematic first-principles study of the IR signatures of carbonate defects in hydroxyapatite using density functional theory molecular dynamics. A dataset of 33 structurally distinct carbonate-substituted models, including bulk and surface substitutions with various charge-compensation schemes, was constructed. IR spectra were obtained from finite-temperature dipole autocorrelation functions. Comparative analysis of peak positions, intensities, and line shapes reveals quantitative structure-spectra relationships that uniquely link specific carbonate environments to their vibrational fingerprints. Surface-associated carbonate defects produce a characteristic OH-stretching doublet near 3600 cm⁻¹. Substitution of phosphate by carbonate leads to diagnostic features in the 1100-1500 cm⁻¹ region whose positions and relative intensities depend on the number of substituted phosphate groups and proton/hydroxyl compensation. The local hydrogen-bonding environment is found to modulate ν(CO₃²⁻) band frequencies and shapes. These results provide a physically grounded reference for interpreting experimental IR spectra of carbonated apatites and demonstrate the utility of first-principles vibrational spectroscopy for resolving defect chemistry in complex inorganic solids.

papers.title: dmf-g16: A Gaussian Wrapper for Reliable Double-Ended Transition-State Searches with Native Input Formats
papers.abstract: Transition-state (TS) searches play a central role in computational studies of chemical reactions. While many advanced methods are now available, their practical use in routine workflows requires nontrivial effort. As a result, users often remain tied to familiar software packages and established input formats and workflows. Here, we present dmf-g16, a Gaussian-specific front end for the Direct MaxFlux (DMF) reaction-path optimization method implemented in PyDMF. dmf-g16 enables DMF-based TS searches with minimal changes to existing Gaussian workflows: users simply replace the Gaussian executable with dmf-g16, while Gaussian native QST2/QST3 input files are used without modification. For QST-formatted inputs, dmf-g16 performs DMF-based path optimization with Gaussian as an external energy and gradient engine, and subsequently refines the TS in Gaussian using the highest-energy point along the optimized path as the initial structure. Benchmark calculations for 121 reactions show a marked improvement in TS-search reliability compared to Gaussian native QST2, increasing the success rate from 31.4% to 93.4%. Although the explicit path optimization requires additional computational cost, the wall-clock time is typically only a few times that of QST2 and can be further reduced by parallel evaluation along the reaction path. Overall, dmf-g16 offers a practical and robust alternative to Gaussian native QST for routine TS searches.

papers.title: Continuous Flow Synthesis of MWCNT@HKUST-1 Hybrid Composites in scCO2 Environment: Effects of Injection Temperature on Morphology, Crystallinity, and Porosity
Nano-Composite Synthesis: Harnessing the Potential of Continuous Flow scCO2 Reactor for Sub-Second synthesis of GO@HKUST-1
Charge-Mixed Nanogels Enable Enhanced Efficacy and Reduced Cytotoxicity in siRNA Delivery
papers.abstract: Cationic nanogels represent a distinctive class of polymeric vectors for siRNA delivery; however, their applications are constrained by a fundamental trade-off between efficacy and cytotoxicity. In this study, we designed an innovative charge-mixed nanogel to tackle this dilemma. Using a robust electrostatic templated polymerization (ETP) method, we synthesized a library of cationic nanogels with precisely regulated charge composition, size, and cross-linking degree. A systematic investigation elucidated their effects on delivery efficacy and cytotoxicity reduction. Specifically, the charge, size, and cross-linking degree of the nanogels cooperatively regulate their delivery efficiency, while the reduction in cytotoxicity relies primarily on the dilution of positive charge through the incorporation of ionic units into the cationic network. The established structure-activity relationship led to the identification of an optimal formulation consisting of 80% cationic units and 20% anionic groups, with a hydrodynamic radius of approximately 83 nm and a 20% cross-linking degree using a disulfide cross-linker. This design promotes intracellular GSH-responsive dissociation of the nanogels and subsequent siRNA release. We demonstrate that the engineered charge-mixed nanogels facilitate excellent cellular uptake (4.4 times that of Lipo 3000) and superior silencing efficiency while significantly reducing cytotoxicity. Our study provides both instructive design principles for cationic nanocarriers and a promising vector that reconciles high delivery potency with excellent biocompatibility for advanced siRNA therapeutics.

papers.title: Coordinating electron transport and layer thickness enhances electrochemiluminescence in solid-state emitters
papers.abstract: Electrochemiluminescence (ECL) efficiency critically depends on electron transport within the light-emitting layer, yet the interplay between electron diffusion length and emitter thickness remains underexplored. Here we synthesized carbon nitride photoelectrodes with tunable thicknesses to systematically investigate this relationship. By defining the ratio of electron diffusion length (Ln) to light-emitting layer thickness (d), we identified an optimal Ln/d range (~0.9-1.2) that maximizes ECL performance by balancing the dynamic competition among bulk electron transport and interfacial reactions. This coordination enhances electron availability and mass transfer, leading to record-high ECL efficiencies in carbon nitride systems. The universality of this strategy was confirmed across diverse ECL materials, including metal-organic frameworks and silver nanoclusters. These findings provide a quantitative descriptor for designing efficient solid-state ECL emitters by dynamically tuning emitter thickness to match intrinsic electron transport properties, advancing the development of highperformance ECL devices.

papers.title: Conditionally Deprotectable Phosphoramidite Chemistry for Recording-by-Synthesis of DNA-Encoded N-Methyl Peptides
papers.abstract: DNA-Encoded Library (DEL) enables the efficient discovery of bioactive ligands. However, conventional DELs utilize unprotected DNA barcodes, which are susceptible to damage during library construction due to chemical reactions. The instability of DNA barcodes limits the applicable reaction conditions and building blocks, and restricts the number of synthesis cycles to approximately 2-4. As a result, the application of DELs has been mainly confined to small molecules, making it challenging to extend the approach to medium-sized molecules such as peptides. In this study, we report a chemically stable DNA barcode that addresses this issue. We focused on the Recording-by-Synthesis method, which chemically constructs DNA barcodes, and developed the N -acetylpyrrolidin-2-ylmethyl (NAPM) protective group to overcome one of its challenges, the fragility of protected phosphodiester group. The NAPM protective group is stable under conditions used for the solid-phase peptide synthesis, while allowing for deprotection under neutral to weakly basic heating conditions. By integrating the NAPM protective group in short DNA barcode technology, we established a new Recording-by-Synthesis approach that enables ligand synthesis under standard organic solvent-based reaction conditions. Using this strategy, we successfully achieved 10 cycles of alternating synthesis of DNA barcode and peptide, even incorporating bulky N -methyl amino acids.

papers.title: Reaching for Transition-Metal Chemical Accuracy by Adding Ladders to Fifth-Rung Density Functionals
papers.abstract: Strong electron correlation effects due to multiconfigurational character remain a consistent challenge for modern density functional theory (DFT). Despite their prominent position atop Jacob's Ladder at rung 5, double-hybrid functionals are often even more sensitive to strong correlation than lower-rung functionals, casting doubt on their general usefulness for transition-metal complexes. Much of these problems can be traced to the second-order Møller-Plesset (MP2) correlation energy, which is the most common wavefunction-theoretic ingredient in double-hybrid functionals. Herein we use adiabatic connection to define a size-consistent, non-empirical double-hybrid functional that uses Coulomb-attenuated linearized hole-hole ladder coupled-cluster correlation as a robust alternative to MP2. The resultant ωB97L-V functional consistently outperforms other non-empirical double-hybrids on main-group chemistry, can smoothly dissociate covalent bonds, and performs exceptionally well for reaction energies of transition-metal complexes. Furthermore, ωB97L-V is the first functional to achieve sub-kcal/mol accuracy for the metal-organic reaction barrier heights in the MOBH28 data set. The results of our simple parameterization hold implications for functional design, suggesting that short-range correlation may be a widely-overlooked ingredient for improving the performance of double-hybrid DFT on transition-metal complexes. Our work sets the stage for further improvements to ωB97L-V and future double-hybrid functionals that add many-body screening to the MP2 correlation energy.

papers.title: Electrocatalytic Oxidation of Ethylene Glycol on Au (111): An ab initio Molecular Dynamics and HPLC study
papers.abstract: This work combines ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) simulations with highperformance liquid chromatography (HPLC) analysis to investigate the impact of solvation on the electro-catalytic oxidation of Ethylene glycol (EG) on Au (111) surface. Already in mild-moist conditions, glycolaldehyde can form besides ethylenedioxy species. EG decomposes via proton transfer to interfacial OHadsorbing mainly at on-top and bridge

papers.title: Tuning Oxidation and Mechanical Behavior of Refractory High-Entropy Alloys via Minor Alloying Elements and Surface Segregation
papers.abstract: Refractory high-entropy alloys (RHEAs) are an intriguing class of materials which can possess excellent strength at elevated temperatures, but often at the expense of oxidation resistance and ductility. Herein, we leverage a threefold approach of data-driven modeling, first-principles simulations, and experimental data to study the impact of minor alloying elements in CrMoNbTaV and HfNbTaVW, two RHEAs which possess excellent strength and ductility synergy, but lack sufficient oxidation resistance. An atomistic representation of the RHEA structure is obtained via calculation of the Warren-Cowley short-range order parameters. CrMoNbTaV with a representative coinage metal (Ag), platinum group metal (Pt), and metalloid (Si) are selected to study their elemental surface segregation tendencies and oxygen adsorption properties. The results reveal both strong surface segregation and a substantial impact on oxygen adsorption for each of the minor alloying elements, which is deemed to be beneficial for improving oxidation resistance. The trends in the modified RHEA's oxygen adsorption properties are attributed to the shift in the local atomic density of states at the RHEA surface. Finally, we discover that at atomic concentrations of 5% and above, minor alloying elements can have significant impacts on both the strength and ductility, and clear trends in the directionality of the observed changes in strength and ductility are observed based on the type of minor alloying element present.

papers.title: Catenation Enhances Potency of a Bioactive Cyclopeptide
papers.abstract: While mechanically interlocked molecules have revolutionized molecular machines and materials science, their potential in biomedicine remains largely underexplored. Artificial topological entanglement is often assumed to compromise bioactivity, restricting most biomedical applications to prodrug systems. Here, we challenge this assumption by showing that mechanical interlocking can be harnessed to enhance biological performance. We synthesize [2]-and [3]catenanes derived from a bioactive cyclopeptide and show that catenation modulates target binding affinity, significantly improves cellular uptake, and retains excellent plasma stability, collectively leading to a substantial gain in cellular potency. Integrated structural and computational analyses elucidate how mechanical interlocking tunes target binding and reveal the critical role of co-conformational flexibility. This work establishes mechanical bonds as versatile and active supramolecular design elements for developing biofunctional molecular machines.

papers.title: De Rerum Natura: How do Halide Perovskites Self-Heal from Damage?
Iminodiacetic Acid-Modified TiO2 Electron Transport Layers for Efficient and Stable All-Inorganic CsPbIxBr3-x Perovskite Solar Cells
papers.abstract: The electron transport layer (ETL) plays a decisive role in governing the photovoltaic performance of perovskite solar cells (PSCs).
